exam.name: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
exam.overview: A role-independent, entry-level exam for people with up to six months of AWS exposure. Covers the value of the cloud, the shared responsibility model, security best practices, core compute, network, database and storage services, and billing and pricing.

questions.question: A company plans to use an Amazon Snowball Edge device to transfer files to the AWS Cloud. Which activities related to a Snowball Edge device are available to the company at no cost?
options: Use of the Snowball Edge appliance for a 10-day period
The transfer of data out of Amazon S3 and to the Snowball Edge appliance
The transfer of data from the Snowball Edge appliance into Amazon S3
Daily use of the Snowball Edge appliance after 10 days
questions.explanation: With AWS Snowball Edge, data transfer into Amazon S3 (ingress) is free — AWS does not charge for the upload of data from the device to S3. However, appliance use beyond the free 10-day period per job and data egress out of S3 onto the device are billed, so daily use after 10 days (D) and the S3-to-device transfer (B) are not free, and the 10-day free period is per job, not a perpetual free appliance allowance (A).

questions.question: A company has deployed applications on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to assess application vulnerabilities and must identify infrastructure deployments that do not meet best practices. Which AWS service can the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector is an automated vulnerability management service that continuously scans EC2 workloads for software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and unintended network exposure, and it also assesses deployments against AWS best practices. AWS Trusted Advisor (A) checks account-level best practices but is not a vulnerability assessment tool, AWS Config (C) records configuration changes and evaluates compliance rules rather than scanning for application vulnerabilities, and GuardDuty (D) detects malicious activity and threats (e.g., unusual API calls), not vulnerabilities or best-practice drift.

questions.question: A company has a centralized group of users with large file storage requirements that have exceeded the space available on premises. The company wants to extend its file storage capabilities for this group while retaining the performance benefit of sharing content locally. What is the MOST operationally efficient AWS solution for this scenario?
options: Create an Amazon S3 bucket for each user. Mount each bucket by using an S3 file system mounting utility.
Configure and deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Connect each user’s workstation to the file gateway.
Move each user’s working environment to Amazon WorkSpaces. Set up an Amazon WorkDocs account for each user.
Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance and attach an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Provisioned IOPS volume. Share the EBS volume directly with the users.
questions.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway's File Gateway presents itself as an NFS/SMB file share while durably storing the files in Amazon S3, so users keep local-network file performance while storage capacity is effectively extended to the cloud with minimal operational effort. Mounting S3 buckets with third-party mounting utilities (A) is not an AWS-supported, performant solution, moving users to WorkSpaces/WorkDocs (C) replaces the storage requirement rather than extending the existing file share, and sharing a single EBS volume from one EC2 instance (D) does not extend capacity beyond that volume and creates a single point of failure.

questions.question: According to security best practices, how should an Amazon EC2 instance be given access to an Amazon S3 bucket?
options: Hard code an IAM user’s secret key and access key directly in the application, and upload the file.
Store the IAM user’s secret key and access key in a text file on the EC2 instance, read the keys, then upload the file.
Have the EC2 instance assume a role to obtain the privileges to upload the file.
Modify the S3 bucket policy so that any service can upload to it at any time.
questions.explanation: The AWS shared responsibility model and IAM best practices require that workloads obtain permissions through an IAM role rather than long-lived credentials; an EC2 instance uses an instance profile to assume a role that grants s3:PutObject permissions, so no access keys ever exist on the instance. Hardcoding keys in application code (A) or storing them in a text file (B) exposes long-lived credentials, and making the bucket policy accept any service (D) grants effectively public write access, violating least privilege.

questions.question: Which option is a customer responsibility when using Amazon DynamoDB under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?
options: Encryption of data at rest in DynamoDB
questions.explanation: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, for a managed service like DynamoDB AWS is responsible for the security OF the cloud (physical security, patching, and encryption of data at rest by default), while the customer is responsible for security IN the cloud — which includes controlling access to DynamoDB tables via IAM policies. Physical security (A), service patching (B), and the default encryption of data at rest (D) are all AWS responsibilities for DynamoDB.

questions.question: Which option is a perspective that includes foundational capabilities of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)?
questions.explanation: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) organizes guidance into six perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, and Operations. Governance is one of those perspectives, whereas Sustainability (A), Performance efficiency (D), and Reliability (D's alternative) are pillars of the Well-Architected Framework, not AWS CAF perspectives.

questions.question: A company is running and managing its own Docker environment on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants an alternative to help manage cluster size, scheduling, and environment maintenance. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers that removes the need to manage cluster size, instance provisioning, and environment maintenance — you just run the tasks. Lambda (A) runs functions rather than general Docker environments, RDS (B) is a managed relational database, and Athena (D) is a serverless SQL query service over S3; none manage container clusters.

questions.question: A company wants to run a NoSQL database on Amazon EC2 instances. Which task is the responsibility of AWS in this scenario?
options: Update the guest operating system of the EC2 instances.
Maintain high availability at the database layer.
Patch the physical infrastructure that hosts the EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: When you run a NoSQL database on EC2 instances, AWS operates the physical infrastructure beneath those instances, so patching the physical hardware/hypervisor is AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model. The guest OS updates (A), database-layer high availability (B), and security group configuration (D) are all the customer's responsibility, since security groups are configured by the customer even though AWS operates the infrastructure.

questions.question: Which AWS services or tools can identify rightsizing opportunities for Amazon EC2 instances? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer includes a Rightsizing Recommendations feature that analyzes utilization metrics and recommends smaller/optimized EC2 instances to cut cost, and AWS Compute Optimizer specifically recommends optimal EC2 instance types based on observed CPU, memory, network, and storage utilization — both identify rightsizing opportunities. AWS Billing Conductor (B) is for customizing billing reports and credits, CodeGuru (C) is an automated code review/service profiling tool, and SageMaker (D) is a machine-learning service; none perform EC2 rightsizing analysis.

questions.question: Which of the following are benefits of using AWS Trusted Advisor? (Choose two.)
options: Detecting underutilized resources to save costs
Improving security by proactively monitoring the AWS environment
Implementing enforced tagging across AWS resources
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects your AWS environment and reports best-practice checks across cost optimization (detecting underutilized/idle resources to save money) and security (proactively flagging security gaps such as open security groups or missing MFA), which are two of its core categories. It does not provide container orchestration (A), key management (B), or org-wide enforced tagging (E) — those are services like EKS/ECS, KMS, and tag-policy features respectively.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage that users experience when they move on-premises workloads to the AWS Cloud?
options: Elimination of expenses for running and maintaining data centers
Price discounts that are identical to discounts from hardware providers
Distribution of all operational controls to AWS
questions.explanation: A widely cited advantage of AWS Cloud is the shift from capital expense to variable expense: customers stop spending on building and maintaining their own data centers, eliminating those costs. Discounts from AWS are not identical to hardware-provider discounts (B), customers retain control of their own applications and data rather than distributing all operational controls to AWS (C), and operational expenses are transformed rather than eliminated entirely (D).

questions.question: A company wants to manage deployed IT services and govern its infrastructure as code (IaC) templates. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS Service Catalog is the service designed for managing and governing approved IT services and infrastructure-as-code templates, letting organizations create portfolios of curated products that users can deploy under guardrails. Resource Explorer (A) is for finding resources, Organizations (C) manages accounts and policies across an organization, and Systems Manager (D) operates and automates resources — none provide service/IaC template catalog governance.

questions.question: Which AWS service or tool helps users visualize, understand, and manage spending and usage over time?
questions.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer is the built-in tool for visualizing, understanding, and managing your spending and usage over time, with filtering, forecasting, and trend graphs out of the box. AWS Organizations (A) aggregates billing across accounts but does not provide usage/spend visualization, the Pricing Calculator (B) estimates future costs for services rather than analyzing actual spending, and Service Catalog (D) manages service offerings, not cost analysis.

questions.question: A company is using a central data platform to manage multiple types of data for its customers. The company wants to use AWS services to discover, transform, and visualize the data. Which combination of AWS services should the company use to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: AWS Glue is the serverless ETL service that discovers and transforms (prepares/curates) data, and Amazon QuickSight is the BI service that visualizes data as dashboards and reports — together they cover discover, transform, and visualize. Amazon EFS (B) is file storage, Amazon Redshift (C) is a data warehouse rather than a data-discovery/transform tool for a general data platform, and Amazon QLDB (E) is a ledger database with no visualization capability.

questions.question: A global company wants to migrate its third-party applications to the AWS Cloud. The company wants help from a global team of experts to complete the migration faster and more reliably in accordance with AWS internal best practices. Which AWS service or resource will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Professional Services is a global team of AWS experts that helps customers migrate to the cloud faster and more reliably by applying AWS-proven best practices and providing guidance and delivery assistance. AWS Support (A) provides technical support and guidance but is not a team that engages to deliver the migration itself, Launch Wizard (C) simplifies deploying specific applications (e.g., SAP, Microsoft SQL Server) on EC2, and AWS Managed Services (AMS) operates your infrastructure after deployment rather than leading a migration engagement.

questions.question: An e-learning platform needs to run an application for 2 months each year. The application will be deployed on Amazon EC2 instances. Any application downtime during those 2 months must be avoided. Which EC2 purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: The application only runs 2 months per year with no downtime allowed in that window, so On-Demand Instances are the most cost-effective: they charge per hour/second with no commitment, meaning you pay only while running and are never interrupted (unlike Spot). Reserved Instances (A) would be wasted for the other 10 months of idle time unless fully utilized, Dedicated Hosts (B) are far more expensive than needed, and Spot Instances (C) can be interrupted by AWS at any time, violating the no-downtime requirement.

questions.question: A developer wants to deploy an application quickly on AWS without manually creating the required resources. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a platform-as-a-service that automatically handles capacity provisioning, load balancing, scaling, and health monitoring, letting a developer deploy an application quickly without manually creating the underlying resources. Amazon EC2 (A) gives you virtual servers you must configure yourself, CodeBuild (C) runs build jobs rather than deploying the application environment, and Personalize (D) is a recommendation service.

questions.question: A company is storing sensitive customer data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to protect the data from accidental deletion or overwriting. Which S3 feature should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: S3 Versioning keeps multiple versions of each object in a bucket, so an accidental overwrite or deletion of sensitive customer data can be recovered by restoring a previous version — the AWS-documented protection against accidental deletion/overwrite. Lifecycle rules (A) manage object expiration and transitions, bucket policies (C) control access, and server-side encryption (D) protects data at rest — none prevent deletion or overwriting of objects.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides the ability to manage infrastructure as code?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation is the AWS infrastructure-as-code service that lets you model and provision AWS and third-party resources with templates, managing their lifecycle through stacks. CodePipeline (A) is a CI/CD orchestration service, CodeDeploy (B) automates code deployments, and Direct Connect (C) is a dedicated network connection — none manage infrastructure as code.

questions.question: An online gaming company needs to choose a purchasing option to run its Amazon EC2 instances for 1 year. The web traffic is consistent, and any increases in traffic are predictable. The EC2 instances must be online and available without any disruption. Which EC2 instance purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: With predictable, consistent traffic over a 1-year term and a requirement for uninterrupted availability, Reserved Instances give the largest discount over On-Demand (up to ~72%) for a 1-year commitment while running continuously with no interruption risk — the most cost-effective option. On-Demand (A) costs more for a known steady 1-year workload, Spot Instances (C) and Spot Fleet (D) can be interrupted when AWS needs capacity, which violates the no-disruption requirement.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature allows a user to establish a dedicated network connection between a company’s on-premises data center and the AWS Cloud?
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated private network connection between an on-premises data center and AWS, reducing network costs and increasing bandwidth throughput compared with internet-based connections. VPC peering (B) connects two VPCs, AWS VPN (C) provides an encrypted connection over the public internet rather than a dedicated line, and Route 53 (D) is a DNS service.

questions.question: Which option is a physical location of the AWS global infrastructure?
questions.explanation: An AWS Region is a physical location in the world where AWS clusters multiple Availability Zones; Regions and Availability Zones are the physical locations of AWS global infrastructure (along with edge locations). DataSync (A) is a data transfer service, Amazon Connect (C) is a contact-center service, and AWS Organizations (D) manages multiple AWS accounts — none are physical infrastructure locations.

questions.question: A company wants to protect its AWS Cloud information, systems, and assets while performing risk assessment and mitigation tasks. Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework is supported by these goals?
questions.explanation: The Security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework is centered on protecting information and systems through confidentiality and integrity protections — including risk identification and mitigation — which directly matches the stated goals. Reliability (A) focuses on recovery from failures, Operational excellence (C) on running and monitoring systems, and Performance efficiency (D) on using resources efficiently.

questions.question: What is the purpose of having an internet gateway within a VPC?
options: To create a VPN connection to the VPC
To allow communication between the VPC and the internet
To impose bandwidth constraints on internet traffic
To load balance traffic from the internet across Amazon EC2 instances
questions.explanation: An internet gateway is a horizontally scaled, redundant VPC component that allows communication between your VPC and the internet, routing traffic from the VPC to the internet and vice versa. It does not create VPN connections (A), it does not impose bandwidth constraints (C — that's what NAT gateway bandwidth limits or traffic shaping do, not an internet gateway's purpose), and load balancing across EC2 instances (D) is the job of Elastic Load Balancing.

questions.question: A company is running a monolithic on-premises application that does not scale and is difficult to maintain. The company has a plan to migrate the application to AWS and divide the application into microservices. Which best practice of the AWS Well-Architected Framework is the company following with this plan?
options: Integrate functional testing as part of AWS deployment.
Deploy the application to multiple locations.
questions.explanation: Breaking a monolith into microservices implemented as loosely coupled dependencies is the AWS Well-Architected Framework practice of implementing loose coupling: each service can be changed, scaled, and maintained independently, so a failure in one does not cascade. The other options describe different practices — automated deployments (B) and functional testing (A) are operational excellence practices, and deploying to multiple locations is not a Well-Architected loose-coupling recommendation.

questions.question: A company has an AWS account. The company wants to audit its password and access key rotation details for compliance purposes. Which AWS service or tool will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: The IAM credential report is a downloadable (API/CLI/console) report that lists all users in an AWS account and the status of their credentials — including password age, access key age, and last used/rotation timestamps — exactly what's needed for auditing password and access key rotation for compliance. IAM Access Analyzer (A) identifies resources shared with external entities, AWS Artifact (B) provides AWS's own compliance documents, and AWS Audit Manager (D) automates evidence collection for audits but is not the tool for credential rotation details.

questions.question: A company wants to receive a notification when a specific AWS cost threshold is reached. Which AWS services or tools can the company use to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets lets you define a cost (or usage) threshold and sends alerts — by email, via SNS, or to Chatbot — when a specified budget amount is reached or forecasted to be exceeded, and Amazon CloudWatch can also notify you through alarms on billing metrics (e.g., estimated charges) when a threshold is crossed. Cost Explorer (C) visualizes historical/forecasted spend but does not send threshold notifications, SQS (A) is a message queue with no native cost monitoring, and the Cost and Usage Report (E) is a detailed billing dataset, not a alerting tool.

questions.question: Which AWS service or resource provides answers to the most frequently asked security-related questions that AWS receives from its users?
questions.explanation: The AWS Knowledge Center hosts answers to the most frequently asked security-related (and other) questions from AWS users, maintained by AWS support engineers. AWS Artifact (A) provides AWS compliance reports and agreements, Amazon Connect (B) is a contact-center service, and AWS Chatbot (D) is for interacting with AWS from chat tools — none are FAQ knowledge bases for security questions.

questions.question: Which tasks are customer responsibilities, according to the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)
options: Configure the AWS provided security group firewall.
Classify company assets in the AWS Cloud.
Determine which Availability Zones to use for Amazon S3 buckets.
Select Amazon EC2 instances to run AWS Lambda on.
questions.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, configuring security groups (A) and classifying (tagging/governance of) company assets in the cloud (B) are both customer responsibilities — configuration of the customer's cloud resources and data governance live with the customer. Availability Zone selection for S3 (C) isn't a customer choice (S3 spans AZs automatically), and patching/upgrading DynamoDB (D) and selecting the EC2 instances Lambda runs on (E) are AWS responsibilities since Lambda is a managed service.

questions.question: Which of the following are pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The AWS Well-Architected Framework defines six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability. Reliability (B) and Operational excellence (E) are both pillars, while Availability (A), Scalability (C), and Responsive design (D) are general design concepts, not named pillars.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature is used to send both text and email messages from distributed applications?
questions.explanation: Amazon SNS is a fully managed publish/subscribe messaging service that can deliver messages to subscribers over multiple protocols simultaneously, including SMS text messages and email (with HTTP/S, SQS, Lambda, and other endpoints) — one publish fans out to both text and email. Amazon SES (B) is specifically for email, CloudWatch alerts (C) can notify but are alarms on metrics rather than an application messaging service for distributed apps, and SQS (D) is a queue that does not natively deliver email or SMS.

questions.question: A user needs programmatic access to AWS resources through the AWS CLI or the AWS API. Which option will provide the user with the appropriate access?
options: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys
questions.explanation: Access keys (an access key ID and secret access key) are the credentials AWS provides for programmatic access to AWS resources through the AWS CLI, AWS API, SDKs, and other programmatic tools. Amazon Inspector (A) is a vulnerability scanner, SSH public keys (C) are for logging into EC2 instances rather than calling AWS APIs, and KMS keys (D) are encryption keys, not authentication credentials for API access.

questions.question: A company runs thousands of simultaneous simulations using AWS Batch. Each simulation is stateless, is fault tolerant, and runs for up to 3 hours. Which pricing model enables the company to optimize costs and meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Batch workloads that are stateless, fault tolerant, and interruptible are ideal candidates for Spot Instances, which use spare EC2 capacity at discounts of up to 90% compared to On-Demand — the optimal pricing model for cost-sensitive, resilient batch simulations. Reserved Instances (A) commit to steady-state use rather than elastic fault-tolerant bursts, On-Demand (C) costs significantly more when the workload tolerates interruption, and Dedicated Instances (D) provide isolated hardware at a premium with no discount benefit for this use case.

questions.question: What does the concept of agility mean in AWS Cloud computing? (Choose two.)
options: The speed at which AWS resources are implemented
The speed at which AWS creates new AWS Regions
The low cost of entry into cloud computing
questions.explanation: In AWS Cloud computing, agility refers to the speed with which resources can be provisioned (A) and the ability to experiment quickly (C) — the cloud lets you spin up and tear down resources in minutes, enabling rapid innovation and iteration. The rate at which AWS creates new Regions (B), elimination of wasted capacity (D), and low cost of entry (E) are not the definition of agility.

questions.question: A company needs to block SQL injection attacks. Which AWS service or feature can meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) lets you create rules that filter and block malicious web requests, including SQL injection attacks, by inspecting HTTP request content against match rules — it is the AWS service purpose-built for application-layer attacks like SQL injection. AWS Shield (B) protects against DDoS attacks rather than request-content inspection, and network ACLs (C) and security groups (D) filter traffic at the port/protocol level, so they cannot detect SQL injection payloads inside HTTP requests.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature identifies whether an Amazon S3 bucket or an IAM role has been shared with an external entity?
questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer continuously analyzes IAM policies to identify resources — such as S3 buckets, IAM roles, SQS queues, and Secrets Manager secrets — that are shared with an external entity (another AWS account or an anonymous/public principal), reporting the external access it detects. AWS Service Catalog (A) manages service offerings, Systems Manager (B) operates resources, and AWS Organizations (D) manages accounts; none detect external sharing of resources.

questions.question: A cloud practitioner needs to obtain AWS compliance reports before migrating an environment to the AWS Cloud. How can these reports be generated?
options: Download the reports from AWS Artifact.
Open a case with AWS Support.
Generate the reports with Amazon Macie.
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for accessing AWS's security and compliance reports and agreements (e.g., SOC, PCI DSS, ISO reports) on demand — you download the reports directly from Artifact before migrating. Contacting the AWS Compliance team (A) or Support (B's alternative, C) is unnecessary since Artifact provides them self-service, and Amazon Macie (D) discovers sensitive data in S3, it does not generate AWS compliance reports.

questions.question: An ecommerce company has migrated its IT infrastructure from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. Which cost is the company’s direct responsibility?
options: Cost of the hardware infrastructure on AWS
Cost of power for the AWS servers
Cost of physical security for the AWS data center
questions.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, application software licenses (A) remain the customer's direct cost responsibility after migrating to AWS — bring-your-own-license costs travel with you. The hardware infrastructure (B), power (C), and physical security of the data center (D) are all AWS costs, as AWS owns and operates the data centers.

questions.question: A company is setting up AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) on an AWS account. Which recommendation complies with IAM security best practices?
options: Use the account root user access keys for administrative tasks.
Grant broad permissions so that all company employees can access the resources they need.
Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) for added security during the login process.
Avoid rotating credentials to prevent issues in production applications.
questions.explanation: Enabling multi-factor authentication (MFA) adds a second authentication factor beyond the password, which is a core IAM security best practice for protecting the root user and IAM users. Using root-user access keys (A), granting broad permissions instead of least privilege (B), and avoiding credential rotation (C's alternative, D) all directly violate IAM security best practices, which require eliminating root access keys, granting least privilege, and regularly rotating credentials.

questions.question: Elasticity in the AWS Cloud refers to which of the following? (Choose two.)
options: How quickly an Amazon EC2 instance can be restarted
The ability to rightsize resources as demand shifts
The maximum amount of RAM an Amazon EC2 instance can use
How easily resources can be procured when they are needed
questions.explanation: Elasticity in the AWS Cloud is the ability to scale resources up or down as demand shifts (B) and to procure/provision resources quickly when they are needed (E) — matching capacity to workload in real time. EC2 restart speed (A) is unrelated, maximum RAM of an instance (C) is a static instance attribute, and pay-as-you-go billing (D) describes the pricing model, not elasticity itself.

questions.question: Which service enables customers to audit API calls in their AWS accounts?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail is the service that records API calls and account activity across your AWS account, enabling you to audit who did what, when, and from where — including via the console, CLI, SDKs, and AWS services. Trusted Advisor (B) checks best practices, Inspector (C) scans for vulnerabilities, and X-Ray (D) traces application requests — none audit API calls across the account.

questions.question: What is a customer responsibility when using AWS Lambda according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Managing the code within the Lambda function
Confirming that the hardware is working in the data center
Shutting down Lambda functions when they are no longer in use
questions.explanation: For AWS Lambda, AWS manages the underlying compute infrastructure (patches the OS, maintains the runtime environment), while the customer is responsible for managing the code within the Lambda function — including code quality, versions, and function configuration. Confirming hardware health (B), patching the operating system (C), are AWS's responsibility, and while managing function lifecycle matters, the canonical customer responsibility listed is managing the function code (A).

questions.question: A company has 5 TB of data stored in Amazon S3. The company plans to occasionally run queries on the data for analysis. Which AWS service should the company use to run these queries in the MOST cost-effective manner?
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena is a serverless interactive query service that lets you run standard SQL queries directly against data in Amazon S3 without managing infrastructure, and you pay only per query — the most cost-effective option for occasional ad-hoc analytics on stored data. Redshift (A) is a data warehouse that requires provisioned clusters (costlier for occasional queries), Kinesis (C) is for streaming data ingestion, and RDS (D) is a relational database that would require loading the 5 TB of S3 data into it first.

questions.question: Which AWS service can be used at no additional cost?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations is provided at no additional charge — you pay only for the AWS resources you use in the accounts you manage, and features like consolidated billing and service control policies cost nothing extra. SageMaker (A), AWS Config (B), and CloudWatch (D) all incur charges for their usage beyond their free tiers.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) capability belongs to the people perspective?
questions.explanation: Cloud fluency (C) belongs to the People perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework, which focuses on building organizational knowledge, skills, and cloud literacy so workforce members can adopt the cloud. Data architecture (A) belongs to the Platform perspective, Event management (B) to Operations, and Strategic partnership (D) to Business.

questions.question: A company wants to make an upfront commitment for continued use of its production Amazon EC2 instances in exchange for a reduced overall cost. Which pricing options meet these requirements with the LOWEST cost? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Reserved Instances (C) and Savings Plans (D) both require an upfront (or partial-upfront) commitment to continued use in exchange for the largest discounts over On-Demand — Savings Plans often offering the lowest overall price for flexible committed compute usage. Spot Instances (A) are discounted but involve no commitment (they're spare capacity), On-Demand (B) has no commitment and thus no discount, and Dedicated Hosts (E) are among the most expensive options.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate its on-premises relational databases to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to use infrastructure as close to its current geographical location as possible. Which AWS service or resource should the company use to select its Amazon RDS deployment area?
questions.explanation: AWS Regions are geographic locations around the world where AWS clusters data centers; choosing an RDS deployment Region close to the current geographical location minimizes latency, so AWS Regions are what the company uses to select its deployment area. Amazon Connect (A) is a contact-center service, Wavelength (B) embeds compute inside telco networks for ultra-low-latency mobile apps (not for choosing an RDS region), and Direct Connect (D) is a dedicated network link, not a location selection mechanism.

questions.question: A company is exploring the use of the AWS Cloud, and needs to create a cost estimate for a project before the infrastructure is provisioned. Which AWS service or feature can be used to estimate costs before deployment?
questions.explanation: The AWS Pricing Calculator lets you estimate the cost of AWS services before you provision anything, configuring services and quantities to produce an estimate for a project with no deployment required. AWS Free Tier (A) describes usage limits for new accounts rather than estimating project cost, Billing and Cost Management (C) analyzes actual incurred spend, and the Cost and Usage Report (D) is a detailed record of past usage and charges.

questions.question: A company is building an application that needs to deliver images and videos globally with minimal latency. Which approach can the company use to accomplish this in a cost effective manner?
options: Deliver the content through Amazon CloudFront.
Store the content on Amazon S3 and enable S3 cross-region replication.
Implement a VPN across multiple AWS Regions.
Deliver the content through AWS PrivateLink.
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a global content delivery network (CDN) that caches copies of images and videos at edge locations close to viewers worldwide, so content is delivered with minimal latency and served from edge cache hits at CDN egress pricing, the cost-effective way to distribute static media globally. S3 cross-region replication (B) only copies data between Regions; it does not deliver content to end users with low latency by itself. A VPN across Regions (C) is connectivity infrastructure, not a content delivery mechanism, and AWS PrivateLink (D) provides private access to services rather than public content distribution.

questions.question: Which option is a benefit of the economies of scale based on the advantages of cloud computing?
options: The ability to trade variable expense for fixed expense
Lower variable costs over fixed costs
Increased operational costs across data centers
questions.explanation: One of the AWS Cloud Benefits tied to economies of scale is that AWS's aggregated usage lets it lower the variable (pay-as-you-go) cost of running workloads compared to what an individual organization could achieve on its own, so customers get lower variable costs. Trading variable for fixed expense (A) is actually the reverse of the cloud benefit (the cloud converts fixed infrastructure cost into variable expense), increased speed and agility (B) is a real cloud benefit but stems from rapid elasticity rather than economies of scale, and increased operational costs (D) describes the opposite of what the shared, aggregated infrastructure model delivers.

questions.question: Which of the following is a software development framework that a company can use to define cloud resources as code and provision the resources through AWS CloudFormation?
questions.explanation: The AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) is an open-source software development framework that lets developers define cloud resources as code in languages such as TypeScript, Python, Java, and C#, and provision them through AWS CloudFormation. The AWS CLI (A) is a command-line tool for issuing individual API calls, not a framework for defining resources as code; AWS Developer Center (B) is a website with resources and documentation; and AWS CodeStar (B, discontinued) was a CI/CD project-management service, not an infrastructure-as-code framework.

questions.question: A company is developing an application that uses multiple AWS services. The application needs to use temporary, limited-privilege credentials for authentication with other AWS APIs. Which AWS service or feature should the company use to meet these authentication requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) is the service that issues temporary, limited-privilege security credentials (such as access key ID, secret access key, session token, and expiration) that applications can use to authenticate against AWS APIs, exactly matching the requirement for temporary, limited-privilege credentials. IAM users (B) hold long-lived static credentials rather than temporary ones, IAM instance profiles (D) only provide credentials to EC2 instances (one specific delivery mechanism, not a general authentication service for multiple use cases), and Amazon API Gateway (A) is an API management service, not a credential-issuing service.

questions.question: Which AWS service is a cloud security posture management (CSPM) service that aggregates alerts from various AWS services and partner products in a standardized format?
questions.explanation: AWS Security Hub is the AWS cloud security posture management (CSPM) service that aggregates, organizes, and prioritizes security findings and alerts from multiple AWS services (such as GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie) and supported partner products, normalizing them into a standardized, schema-compliant format (the AWS Security Finding Format). Amazon GuardDuty (D) is a threat detection service that produces findings rather than aggregating them across services, Amazon EventBridge (C) is a general event-routing service and not a security-posture aggregator, and AWS Trusted Advisor (B) provides best-practice recommendations rather than standardized aggregated security alerts.

questions.question: Which AWS service is always provided at no charge?
questions.explanation: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is a global AWS service that is provided at no charge; you do not pay for IAM users, groups, roles, or policies. Amazon S3 (A) charges for storage, requests, and data transfer, Elastic Load Balancers (C) are billed by hour and data processed, and AWS WAF (D) charges per web ACL, rule, and request — all of these are usage-based paid services.

questions.question: To reduce costs, a company is planning to migrate a NoSQL database to AWS. Which AWS service is fully managed and can automatically scale throughput capacity to meet database workload demands?
questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed serverless NoSQL key-value and document database that automatically scales throughput capacity to match workload demand (via on-demand capacity mode or auto scaling), which matches both the NoSQL requirement and automatic throughput scaling while reducing operational cost. Amazon Redshift (A) is a data warehouse, not a NoSQL database; Amazon Aurora (B) and Amazon RDS (D) are relational (SQL) databases rather than NoSQL stores, and scaling them typically involves instance-class changes rather than automatic throughput-capacity scaling.

questions.question: A company is using Amazon DynamoDB. Which task is the company’s responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
questions.explanation: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, for a managed service like DynamoDB, AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (patching the OS, provisioning and securing hosts, operating the database software), while the customer is responsible for security IN the cloud — which includes managing database access permissions (who can read/write the tables). Patching the OS (A), provisioning hosts (B), and securing the operating system (D) are all AWS responsibilities for managed DynamoDB.

questions.question: A company has a test AWS environment. A company is planning on testing an application within AWS. The application testing can be interrupted and does not need to run continuously. Which Amazon EC2 purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances let you run fault-tolerant or interruptible workloads at discounts of up to 90% off On-Demand prices, since AWS can reclaim the capacity when needed — ideal for a test environment where interrupted testing is acceptable, making it the MOST cost-effective option. On-Demand (A) costs the full hourly rate with no discount, Reserved Instances (D) require a 1- or 3-year commitment suited to steady-state workloads rather than intermittent testing, and Dedicated Instances (B) are the most expensive option since they provide single-tenant hardware.

questions.question: Which AWS service gives users the ability to discover and protect sensitive data that is stored in Amazon S3 buckets?
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie is a data security service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover, classify, and help protect sensitive data (such as PII and financial data) stored in Amazon S3 buckets. Amazon Detective (B) analyzes security findings to investigate root causes of potential security issues, Amazon GuardDuty (C) is a threat detection service that monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior, and AWS IAM Access Analyzer (D) identifies resources shared with external entities — none of these focus on discovering and protecting sensitive data stored in S3.

questions.question: Which of the following services can be used to block network traffic to an instance? (Choose two.)
options: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) flow logs
questions.explanation: Security groups (stateful, instance-level firewalls) and network ACLs (stateless, subnet-level firewalls) are the two VPC mechanisms that filter and can block network traffic to/from an instance, so A and C are correct. VPC flow logs (B) only record traffic metadata for analysis; they do not block anything. Amazon CloudWatch (D) is a monitoring service, and AWS CloudTrail (E) records API activity — neither is a network traffic-filtering control.

questions.question: Which AWS service can identify when an Amazon EC2 instance was terminated?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 is a durable object storage service designed to hold any amount of data, making it the appropriate choice for a backup repository of application files. Amazon EBS (C) provides block storage volumes attached to individual EC2 instances and is not designed as a shared backup repository, Amazon RDS (D) is a relational database service rather than a file backup store, and AWS Storage Gateway (B) is a hybrid-cloud storage service that extends on-premises storage to AWS rather than being the primary cloud backup repository itself.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fully managed MySQL-compatible database?
questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service; it registers domain names and resolves them to AWS resources, which is exactly what 'registering and managing DNS' requires. Amazon CloudFront (B) is a CDN for content delivery, AWS Direct Connect (C) provides dedicated private network connectivity between on-premises and AWS rather than DNS, and Amazon VPC (D) is a logically isolated network in the AWS Cloud, not a DNS service.

questions.question: Which AWS service supports a hybrid architecture that gives users the ability to extend AWS infrastructure, AWS services, APIs, and tools to data centers, co-location environments, or on-premises facilities?
questions.explanation: AWS Outposts is a family of fully managed services that extend AWS infrastructure, services, APIs, and tools to on-premises facilities, co-location environments, or customer data centers — matching the requirement of running AWS services on customer premises. AWS Snowmobile (A) is a data-transfer service for migrating large volumes of data to AWS, not a way to run AWS services locally; AWS Local Zones (B) place compute, storage, and databases close to large population centers in AWS-managed facilities rather than the customer's own site; and AWS Fargate (D) is a serverless compute engine for containers that runs in the AWS Cloud only.

questions.question: Which AWS service can run a managed PostgreSQL database that provides online transaction processing (OLTP)?
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS supports multiple relational database engines including PostgreSQL (as well as MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server, and its own Amazon Aurora), providing a managed OLTP database service. Amazon DynamoDB (A) is a NoSQL key-value/document database, not PostgreSQL; Amazon Athena (B) is a serverless interactive query service over data in S3, not a database engine you run; and Amazon EMR (D) is a managed Hadoop/Spark big-data processing platform rather than an OLTP database service.

questions.question: A company wants to provide managed Windows virtual desktops and applications to its remote employees over secure network connections. Which AWS services can the company use to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Amazon WorkSpaces provides managed, secure virtual desktops (Windows or Linux) streamed to users over the network, and Amazon AppStream 2.0 delivers streamed desktop applications to users — together these are the two AWS services that provide managed Windows virtual desktops/applications to remote employees, so B and C are correct. Amazon Connect (A) is an omnichannel contact center service, AWS Site-to-Site VPN (D) creates encrypted network tunnels between networks (a connectivity primitive, not a desktop service), and Amazon ECS (E) runs containers rather than virtual desktops.

questions.question: A company wants to monitor for misconfigured security groups that are allowing unrestricted access to specific ports. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor includes security best-practice checks that inspect security group configurations and can identify unrestricted access (0.0.0.0/0) to specific ports (such as 22 for SSH or 3389 for RDP), directly matching the misconfigured-security-group monitoring requirement. Amazon CloudWatch (B) monitors metrics and logs but does not understand security group rules, Amazon GuardDuty (C) detects malicious activity and threats rather than auditing firewall configurations, and the AWS Health Dashboard (D) reports on AWS service events and maintenance, not customer resource configuration.

questions.question: Which AWS service is a key-value database that provides sub-millisecond latency on a large scale?
questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a key-value and document database designed for single-digit millisecond performance at any scale, commonly described as providing sub-millisecond latency reads at large scale, which matches the question exactly. Amazon Aurora (B) is a relational (SQL) database rather than a key-value store, Amazon DocumentDB (C) is a document database emulating MongoDB (not primarily characterized as key-value with sub-millisecond latency), and Amazon Neptune (D) is a graph database optimized for highly connected data rather than simple key-value lookups.

questions.question: A company is deploying a machine learning (ML) research project that will require a lot of compute power over several months. The ML processing jobs do not need to run at specific times. Which Amazon EC2 instance purchasing option will meet these requirements at the lowest cost?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances let you use spare EC2 capacity at discounts of up to 90% compared to On-Demand prices, and since the ML research jobs do not need to run at specific times and can tolerate interruption, Spot is the lowest-cost purchasing option for months of heavy compute. On-Demand (A) charges full hourly rates with no discount, Reserved Instances (C) require a 1- or 3-year commitment (suited to steady-state predictable usage rather than flexible job scheduling) and cost more than Spot, and Dedicated Instances (D) provide single-tenant hardware at the highest price point.

questions.question: Which AWS services or features provide disaster recovery solutions for Amazon EC2 instances? (Choose two.)
options: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots
questions.explanation: Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) capture a launchable image (root volume plus configured instance state) and EBS snapshots back up volume data; together they let you reconstruct EC2 instances in another Region or Account after an outage, providing disaster recovery capability, so B and C are correct. EC2 Reserved Instances (A) are a pricing model and do not protect or replicate any data, AWS Shield (D) is a DDoS-protection service for edge services like CloudFront, and Amazon GuardDuty (E) is a threat-detection service — none of these create recoverable copies of compute or data.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides command line access to AWS tools and resources directly from a web browser?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudShell is a browser-based, pre-authenticated shell environment that gives you command line access to AWS services and tools (AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, Bash, Python, git, and more) directly from the AWS Management Console without needing local installation or credential configuration. AWS CloudHSM (A) is a dedicated hardware security module service, Amazon WorkSpaces (C) provides virtual desktops, and AWS Cloud Map (D) is a service-discovery registry — none of them provide a browser-based command line for AWS tooling.

questions.question: A network engineer needs to build a hybrid cloud architecture connecting on-premises networks to the AWS Cloud using AWS Direct Connect. The company has a few VPCs in a single AWS Region and expects to increase the number of VPCs to hundreds over time. Which AWS service or feature should the engineer use to simplify and scale this connectivity as the VPCs increase in number?
questions.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway is a regional hub-and-spoke router that connects thousands of VPCs, VPN connections, and Direct Connect gateways through a single gateway, so as the number of VPCs grows into the hundreds the engineer simply attaches each new VPC to the Transit Gateway instead of creating an ever-growing mesh of individual connections — the standard way to simplify and scale hybrid VPC connectivity. VPC endpoints (A) provide private connectivity to individual AWS services, not connectivity between on-premises networks and many VPCs; Amazon Route 53 (C) is a DNS service; and AWS Secrets Manager (D) stores and rotates secrets, which is unrelated to network connectivity.

questions.question: A company wants to assess its operational readiness. It also wants to identify and mitigate any operational risks ahead of a new product launch. Which AWS Support plan offers guidance and support for this kind of event at no additional charge?
questions.explanation: The AWS Enterprise Support plan includes access to a Technical Account Manager (TAM) who provides architectural guidance and operational reviews such as pre-launch and event readiness assessments at no additional charge, matching the requirement to assess operational readiness and mitigate risks ahead of a product launch. Business Support (A) and Developer Support (C) do not include a TAM or proactive readiness reviews, and Basic Support (B) only provides customer service and documentation resources with no consultative guidance.

questions.question: A company wants to establish a schedule for rotating database user credentials. Which AWS service will support this requirement with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?
questions.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is designed specifically to store, retrieve, rotate, and manage database credentials and other secrets; it can automatically rotate database user credentials on a configurable schedule using built-in or custom Lambda rotation functions, with the least operational overhead since rotation is fully managed. AWS Systems Manager (A) manages operational tasks and parameters but its Parameter Store cannot natively rotate database credentials, AWS License Manager (D) tracks software licenses rather than credentials, and AWS Managed Services (C, actually labeled License Manager in position C) — more precisely, AWS Managed Services provides ongoing management of AWS environments and is not a credential-rotation service.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature can be used to create a private connection between an on-premises workload and an AWS Cloud workload?
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated private network connection between an on-premises data center and AWS, providing a private connection for hybrid workloads that does not traverse the public internet. Amazon Route 53 (A) is a DNS service, Amazon Macie (B) is a sensitive-data discovery service for S3, and while AWS PrivateLink (D) provides private connectivity, it is designed for private access to AWS services and VPC endpoints rather than connecting an on-premises network to an AWS workload — the dedicated on-premises-to-AWS private link is Direct Connect.

questions.question: Which AWS service is used to provide encryption for Amazon EBS?
questions.explanation: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) is the AWS service used to create and manage the cryptographic keys that encrypt Amazon EBS volumes; when you enable EBS encryption, EBS integrates with KMS to encrypt data at rest using a KMS key (an AWS managed key by default or a customer managed key of your choice). AWS Certificate Manager (A) issues and manages SSL/TLS certificates for in-transit encryption, not data-at-rest encryption of volumes; AWS Systems Manager (B) is an operations management service with no encryption-key function; and AWS Config (D) records resource configuration history and evaluates compliance, it does not encrypt anything.

questions.question: A company wants to manage its AWS Cloud resources through a web interface. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: The AWS Management Console is the web-based graphical user interface that lets users manage AWS cloud resources through a browser, directly matching the requirement for a web interface. The AWS CLI (B) is a command-line tool, AWS SDKs (C) are libraries for embedding AWS API calls into application code, and AWS Cloud9 (D) is a cloud-based integrated development environment (IDE) for writing and debugging code — none of these are a general web interface for resource management.

questions.question: Which of the following are advantages of the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: Trade variable expenses for capital expenses
questions.explanation: High economies of scale (B) means AWS's massive aggregate usage lowers per-unit costs passed on to customers, and the ability to launch globally in minutes (C) reflects the cloud's instant global reach — both are canonical AWS Cloud advantages, so B and C are correct. Option A reverses the actual benefit (the cloud trades capital expenses for variable expenses, not the other way around), focusing on managing hardware infrastructure (D) is the opposite of shifting that work to AWS, and overprovisioning capacity (E) describes the wasteful old model the cloud replaces with elastic scaling.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud benefit is shown by an architecture’s ability to withstand failures with minimal downtime?
questions.explanation: High availability is the cloud benefit describing an architecture's ability to withstand failures (of components or entire Availability Zones) with minimal downtime by distributing workloads across redundant targets, which is exactly what the question describes. Agility (A) is about responding quickly to change, elasticity (B) is about scaling resources up and down with demand, and scalability (C) is about handling growing demand — none of these specifically describe withstanding failures with minimal downtime.

questions.question: A developer needs to maintain a development environment infrastructure and a production environment infrastructure in a repeatable fashion. Which AWS service should the developer use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation lets a developer define infrastructure as code in templates and apply them repeatedly, so the same development and production environment infrastructure can be provisioned and maintained in a consistent, repeatable fashion (and kept in sync via stack updates). AWS Ground Station (A) is a service for communicating with satellites, AWS Shield (B) is DDoS protection, and AWS IoT Device Defender (D... rather, AWS IoT Device Defender) is a security service for IoT devices — none of them manage infrastructure repeatability.

questions.question: Which task is the customer’s responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Maintain the security of the AWS Cloud.
Patch the operating system of Amazon RDS instances.
questions.explanation: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, configuring firewalls and networks (such as security groups and network ACLs) is configuration of the customer's own environment and therefore the customer's responsibility (security in the cloud). Maintaining the security of the AWS Cloud (A), applying OS patches to managed RDS instances (C), and implementing physical and environmental controls at data centers (D) are all AWS responsibilities (security of the cloud).

questions.question: Which AWS service helps deliver highly available applications with fast failover for multi-Region and Multi-AZ architectures?
questions.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network and anycast IP addresses to route user traffic to the nearest healthy endpoint across AWS Regions and Availability Zones, providing fast failover for multi-Region and multi-AZ architectures by rerouting traffic in seconds when health checks fail. AWS WAF (A) is a web application firewall, AWS Shield (C) provides DDoS protection, and AWS Direct Connect (D) is dedicated private network connectivity — none of these route application traffic across Regions/AZs with fast failover.

questions.question: A company has a set of ecommerce applications. The applications need to be able to send messages to each other. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) is a fully managed message queuing service that lets decoupled applications (such as a set of ecommerce applications) send, store, and receive messages at any scale, directly meeting the requirement for applications to send messages to each other. AWS Auto Scaling (A) adjusts compute capacity, Elastic Load Balancing (B) distributes incoming traffic across targets, and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (D) is designed for real-time streaming of large data records rather than general application-to-application message passing.

questions.question: What are the benefits of consolidated billing for AWS Cloud services? (Choose two.)
options: A minimal additional fee for use
Custom cost and usage budget creation
questions.explanation: Consolidated billing aggregates usage across all AWS accounts in an organization onto a single bill (C), and because usage is pooled, accounts can qualify for volume discounts / tiered pricing that would not be available individually (A), so A and C are correct. Consolidated billing does not add a fee for use (B) — it is free — and it does not offer installment payment options (D) or create custom cost and usage budgets (E); budgets are a separate AWS Budgets feature.

questions.question: A user wants to review all Amazon S3 buckets with ACLs and S3 bucket policies in the S3 console. Which AWS service or resource will meet this requirement?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
questions.explanation: Access Analyzer for S3 (S3 Block Public Access / Access Analyzer settings in the S3 console) reviews buckets and reports those with ACLs or bucket policies that grant public or external access, letting a user review all S3 buckets' ACLs and bucket policies from the console, matching the requirement. S3 Multi-Region Access Points (A) simplify access management across Regions for applications, not review of existing bucket policies; S3 Storage Lens (B) analyzes storage metrics and recommendations, not access policies; and AWS IAM Identity Center (C) is a workforce identity (single sign-on) service, unrelated to auditing S3 bucket access.

questions.question: What is the best resource for a user to find compliance-related information and reports about AWS?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is the AWS service that provides on-demand access to AWS security and compliance reports and agreements (such as SOC, PCI DSS, and ISO reports) — it is the self-service portal for compliance-related information and reports about AWS. AWS Marketplace (B) is a catalog of third-party software and services, Amazon Inspector (C) is an automated vulnerability-management service for workloads, and AWS Support (D) provides technical assistance rather than self-service compliance documentation.

questions.question: Which AWS service enables companies to deploy an application close to end users?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a global content delivery network (CDN) that caches content at edge locations worldwide, deploying the application's content close to end users to reduce latency — exactly what 'deploy an application close to end users' means for content delivery. AWS Auto Scaling (B) adjusts compute capacity based on demand, AWS AppSync (C) is a managed GraphQL service, and Amazon Route 53 (D) is a DNS service that routes users to endpoints but does not itself deploy/caching content close to them.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature improves network performance by sending traffic through the AWS worldwide network infrastructure?
questions.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator improves network performance and availability by routing traffic over the AWS global backbone network between users and applications, avoiding public-internet congestion and providing static anycast IPs for fast regional failover — sending traffic through AWS's worldwide network infrastructure as described. A route table (A) routes traffic within a VPC, AWS Transit Gateway (B) is a regional VPC/VPN router, and Amazon VPC (D) is a logically isolated network in the cloud — none of these optimize end-user traffic over the AWS global network.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides highly durable object storage?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 is highly durable object storage (designed for 99.999999999% / eleven nines of durability) built to store any amount of data, making it the answer for highly durable object storage. Amazon Elastic File System (B) and Amazon FSx (D) provide file storage (NFS/SMB-style), and Amazon Elastic Block Store (C) provides block storage volumes — none are object storage or characterized by S3's durability guarantee.

questions.question: Which responsibility belongs to AWS when a company hosts its databases on Amazon EC2 instances?
questions.explanation: When a company hosts its database on its own Amazon EC2 instance (a customer-deployed database), the customer is responsible for the database software, its patches, and backups, while AWS is responsible for the underlying infrastructure — including installing and patching the operating system that the instance runs on. So OS installations (D, and OS patches too) are AWS's responsibility here; database backups (A) and database software patches (B) are the customer's responsibility for self-managed databases on EC2, and OS patches (C) is also AWS's responsibility for the EC2 layer... precisely: for databases running ON EC2 instances, AWS patches the OS (customer would only patch the OS if they brought unusual shared-responsibility edge cases, but standard answer: AWS handles OS layer, customer handles database layer).

questions.question: Which of the following are advantages of moving to the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: The ability to turn over the responsibility for all security to AWS.
The ability to use the pay-as-you-go model.
The ability to have full control over the physical infrastructure.
No longer having to guess what capacity will be required.
No longer worrying about users access controls.
questions.explanation: The pay-as-you-go model (B) lets you pay only for the compute and services you actually use instead of investing in fixed data centers, and because AWS manages a virtually unlimited pool of resources you no longer need to guess (or over-provision) capacity ahead of demand (D) — both are core advantages of moving to the AWS Cloud, so B and D are correct. Security remains a shared responsibility, so you cannot turn over 'all' security to AWS (A) and access controls remain your responsibility (E); customers also do not have full control over physical infrastructure (C), which AWS operates.

questions.question: Which AWS service is a hybrid cloud storage service that provides on-premises users access to virtually unlimited cloud storage?
questions.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway is a hybrid cloud storage service that extends on-premises storage to AWS, giving on-premises users and applications access to virtually unlimited cloud storage (file, volume, or tape gateway configurations) while keeping low-latency local access. AWS DataSync (A) is an online data-transfer service for moving large datasets between storage systems and AWS, Amazon S3 Glacier (B) is archival storage within S3 rather than an on-premises access gateway, and Amazon EBS (D) is block storage for EC2 instances in the cloud, not a hybrid gateway service.

questions.question: A company plans to migrate to AWS and wants to create cost estimates for its AWS use cases. Which AWS service or tool can the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: The AWS Pricing Calculator lets you estimate the cost of AWS services for your use cases before you use them — including planning a migration by modeling expected usage — which matches the requirement to create cost estimates for planned AWS use cases. AWS Cost Explorer (C) visualizes and analyzes your actual historical and current spending (and forecasts) after you start using AWS, Amazon CloudWatch (B) is a monitoring service, and AWS Budgets (D) sets alerts against spending or usage thresholds rather than producing pre-migration estimates.

questions.question: Which tool should a developer use to integrate AWS service features directly into an application?
questions.explanation: An AWS Software Development Kit (SDK) provides language-specific libraries and APIs that let a developer integrate AWS service features (such as S3, DynamoDB, or Lambda calls) directly into application code. AWS CodeDeploy (B) is a deployment service, AWS Lambda (C) is a serverless compute service that runs your code, and AWS Batch (D) runs batch computing jobs — these are themselves AWS services rather than tools for integrating service features into your application.

questions.question: Which of the following is a recommended design principle of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
options: Reduce downtime by making infrastructure changes infrequently and in large increments.
Invest the time to configure infrastructure manually.
Learn to improve from operational failures.
Use monolithic application design for centralization.
questions.explanation: In the AWS Well-Architected Framework's Operational Excellence pillar, the design principle 'Learn from operational failures' means teams should analyze failures to improve systems and processes — matching 'learn to improve from operational failures' (C). Making large, infrequent infrastructure changes (A) increases risk rather than reducing it (the framework favors small, frequent, reversible changes), manually configuring infrastructure (B) contradicts the infrastructure-as-code principle, and monolithic design (D) contradicts the Reliability/Performance Efficiency guidance toward loosely coupled, distributed components.

questions.question: Using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to grant access only to the resources needed to perform a task is a concept known as:
questions.explanation: Granting IAM access only to the resources needed to perform a task is the definition of least privilege access — giving users and roles the minimum permissions required and nothing more (C). 'Restricted access' (A) and 'as-needed access' (B) are not the AWS security terms for this concept, and 'token access' (D) refers to temporary credential mechanisms, not the principle of minimal permissions.

questions.question: Which AWS service or tool can be used to set up a firewall to control traffic going into and coming out of an Amazon VPC subnet?
questions.explanation: A network ACL is the firewall that operates at the subnet level and controls traffic both entering and leaving a VPC subnet (with allow and deny rules), making it the correct answer for a firewall controlling traffic in and out of a subnet. A security group (A) operates at the instance/network-interface level, not the subnet level; AWS WAF (B) protects web applications (CloudFront, API Gateway, ALB) from common web exploits rather than VPC subnets; and AWS Firewall Manager (C) is a central management service that configures firewall rules across resources (often built on top of WAF/Shield/security groups) rather than being the subnet-level firewall itself.

questions.question: A company wants to operate a data warehouse to analyze data without managing the data warehouse infrastructure. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift Serverless lets you run analytics queries against your data warehouse without provisioning or managing the underlying cluster infrastructure — AWS automatically provisions and scales capacity as needed — matching the requirement to operate a data warehouse without managing its infrastructure. Amazon Aurora (A) and Amazon RDS (D) are relational database services (not data warehouses), and AWS Lambda (C) is a serverless compute service for running code, not a data warehouse.

questions.question: How does AWS Cloud computing help businesses reduce costs? (Choose two.)
options: AWS charges the same prices for services in every AWS Region.
AWS enables capacity to be adjusted on demand.
AWS offers discounts for Amazon EC2 instances that remain idle for more than 1 week.
AWS does not charge for data sent from the AWS Cloud to the internet.
AWS eliminates many of the costs of building and maintaining on-premises data centers.
questions.explanation: AWS's cost model reduces cost two ways: capacity can be scaled up or down on demand so you pay only for what you use (B), and migrating off premises eliminates the capital and operational expense of building and maintaining your own data centers (E). AWS pricing varies by Region (A) rather than being identical everywhere, idle instances are charged for regardless of usage with no discount for idling (C), and data transferred out to the internet is billed (D) rather than free.

questions.question: A company wants to grant users in one AWS account access to resources in another AWS account. The users do not currently have permission to access the resources. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: An IAM role is the standard mechanism for granting principals in one AWS account access to resources in another account: the trusting account defines the role, the trusted account's users assume it and receive temporary credentials for the permissions the role defines. IAM groups, tags, and Access Analyzer are all intra-account constructs (groups and tags organize and label identities within a single account; Access Analyzer reports external access findings) and cannot grant cross-account access on their own.

questions.question: Which task is the responsibility of AWS when using AWS services?
options: Creation of security group rules for outbound access
Maintenance of physical and environmental controls
Application of Amazon EC2 operating system patches
questions.explanation: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, AWS is responsible for 'security OF the cloud,' which includes the physical security and environmental controls of its data centers. Everything else listed is on the customer side of the model: managing IAM user permissions, configuring security group rules, and patching the operating system of EC2 instances (for EC2, AWS patches only the underlying hypervisor).

questions.question: A company wants to automate infrastructure deployment by using infrastructure as code (IaC). The company wants to scale production stacks so the stacks can be deployed in multiple AWS Regions. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation is the AWS infrastructure-as-code service: you describe resources in a template and CloudFormation provisions and manages them, and StackSets extend this to deploy the same stack across multiple AWS Regions and accounts from a single definition, directly meeting the multi-Region scaling requirement. CloudWatch is for monitoring, AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance, and Trusted Advisor provides best-practice checks — none of them deploy infrastructure.

questions.question: Which option is an AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) platform perspective capability?
questions.explanation: In the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework, the platform perspective focuses on the underlying technology platform, including data architecture, compute, network, and storage design. Data protection belongs to the security perspective, data governance to the people/business perspectives, and data science is not one of the six CAF perspectives (business, people, governance, platform, security, operations).

questions.question: A company is running a workload in the AWS Cloud. Which AWS best practice ensures the MOST cost-effective architecture for the workload?
questions.explanation: Rightsizing — regularly reviewing and right-sizing resource usage to match actual demand — is the AWS-recommended best practice for ensuring the most cost-effective architecture, because it directly reduces waste from over-provisioned resources. Loose coupling improves resilience, caching improves performance, and redundancy improves availability; none of them primarily target cost effectiveness.

questions.question: A company is using a third-party service to back up 10 TB of data to a tape library. The on-premises backup server is running out of space. The company wants to use AWS services for the backups without changing its existing backup workflows. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway lets the company keep its existing backup workflows intact while offloading data to AWS: the Tape Gateway (virtual tape library) interface presents itself as a standard tape target, so backup software keeps writing to 'tapes' while data is stored durably and cost-effectively in S3. EBS is block storage, ECS runs containers, and Lambda runs event-driven functions — none of them preserve an existing tape-based backup workflow.

questions.question: Which AWS tool gives users the ability to plan their service usage, service costs, and instance reservations, and also allows them to set custom alerts when their costs or usage exceed established thresholds?
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets is the tool for planning service usage and costs, tracking reservations, and setting custom alerts when cost or usage exceeds a chosen threshold. Cost Explorer visualizes historical and forecasted spend but is not the threshold-alerting tool, the Cost and Usage Report is a detailed billing export rather than an alerting service, and Reserved Instance reporting only shows reservation coverage and utilization.

questions.question: Which tasks are the customer’s responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, the customer is responsible for everything 'in' the cloud, which includes client-side data encryption (B, data the customer encrypts before upload) and configuring IAM credentials (C, identity and access management is entirely customer-managed). Establishing the global infrastructure (A) and securing edge locations (D) are AWS responsibilities, and AWS patches managed RDS DB instances (E), making it an AWS responsibility.

questions.question: A developer has been hired by a large company and needs AWS credentials. Which are security best practices that should be followed? (Choose two.)
options: Grant the developer access to only the AWS resources needed to perform the job.
Share the AWS account root user credentials with the developer.
Add the developer to the administrator’s group in AWS IAM.
Configure a password policy that ensures the developer’s password cannot be changed.
Ensure the account password policy requires a minimum length.
