questions.explanation: Security best practices for granting a developer credentials are least privilege — access only to the resources needed for the job (A) — and a strong account password policy requiring minimum length (E). Sharing root user credentials (B) is explicitly prohibited by AWS, making the developer an administrator (C) violates least privilege, and a password that cannot be changed (D) is itself a security defect.

questions.question: A company has multiple AWS accounts that include compute workloads that cannot be interrupted. The company wants to obtain billing discounts that are based on the company’s use of AWS services. Which AWS feature or purchasing option will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Consolidated billing (via AWS Organizations) pools usage across accounts, letting the company qualify for volume discounts and tiered pricing based on combined usage while keeping accounts separate — appropriate for steady, uninterruptible workloads. Resource tagging (A) labels resources for cost allocation but does not itself produce discounts, pay-as-you-go (C) is the default on-demand rate with no discount mechanism, and Spot Instances (D) are interruptible by definition, which rules them out for workloads that cannot be interrupted.

questions.question: A user wants to allow applications running on an Amazon EC2 instance to make calls to other AWS services. The access granted must be secure. Which AWS service or feature should be used?
questions.explanation: AWS Firewall Manager is a centralized security management service that lets the company define and apply firewall rules — WAF rules, security group rules, and more — across multiple accounts and resources from one place, which is exactly the 'one central location, multiple VPCs' requirement. Security groups (A) are per-resource and would have to be applied individually to each VPC, IAM roles (C) govern identity permissions rather than network traffic, and IAM user SSH keys (D) authenticate shell access, not network filtering.

questions.question: A company wants a fully managed Windows file server for its Windows-based applications. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon FSx is the fully managed service for Windows file servers, supporting SMB protocols, Active Directory integration, and the features Windows applications expect, so it directly meets the requirement for a managed Windows file server. Amazon EKS and ECS are container orchestration services, and Amazon EMR is for big-data processing — none provides a managed Windows file system.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate its NFS on-premises workload to AWS. Which AWS Storage Gateway type should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 File Gateway presents a file interface (NFS) whose files are stored as objects in Amazon S3, making it the right Storage Gateway type for migrating NFS on-premises workloads while keeping a low-latency NFS front end. Tape Gateway (A) is for virtual tape backups, Volume Gateway (B) presents iSCSI block volumes, and Amazon FSx File Gateway (C) is for on-premises FSx for Windows File Cache access rather than NFS-to-S3 migration.

questions.question: A company needs to track the activity in its AWS accounts, and needs to know when an API call is made against its AWS resources. Which AWS tool or service can be used to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail is the service that records API calls and account activity — who did what, when, and from where — across AWS services, directly satisfying the requirement to track activity and know when API calls are made against resources. CloudWatch (A) is for metrics, logs, and alarms rather than API audit history, Amazon Inspector (B) scans workloads for vulnerabilities, and IAM (D) manages identities and permissions but does not log activity.

questions.question: A company has an uninterruptible application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application constantly processes a backlog of files in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. This usage is expected to continue to grow for years. What is the MOST cost-effective EC2 instance purchasing model to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Savings Plans offer the deepest discounts (up to ~72%) for steady-state, predictable compute usage committed over 1 or 3 years, making them the most cost-effective model for a workload that cannot be interrupted and is expected to run for years. Spot Instances (A) are interruptible by design, On-Demand (B) carries no commitment discount, and Dedicated Hosts (D) are the most expensive option and are meant for licensing/physical-server requirements rather than cost savings.

questions.question: A company wants an AWS service to provide product recommendations based on its customer data. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize is the managed recommendation service built for exactly this use case: it ingests customer data and produces personalized product recommendations using the same technology used by Amazon.com. Amazon Polly (A) converts text to speech, Amazon Comprehend (C) does natural language analysis, and Amazon Rekognition (D) analyzes images and video — none produces recommendations.

questions.question: A company is planning its migration to the AWS Cloud. The company is identifying its capability gaps by using the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) perspectives. Which phase of the cloud transformation journey includes these identification activities?
questions.explanation: In the AWS CAF transformation journey, the Align phase is where the company identifies capability gaps across its CAF perspectives and aligns people, processes, and technology around the transformation. Envision (A) sets the vision and the initial business case, while Launch (D) and Scale (C) come later as the company implements and then expands its cloud initiatives.

questions.question: A social media company wants to protect its web application from common web exploits such as SQL injections and cross-site scripting. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that protects web applications against common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting by letting you write rules that inspect and filter HTTP requests. Amazon Inspector (A) scans for software vulnerabilities, Amazon GuardDuty (C) detects threat intelligence and anomalous activity, and Amazon CloudWatch (D) is for monitoring metrics and logs — none is a web exploit firewall.

questions.question: Which fully managed AWS service assists with the creation, testing, and management of custom Amazon EC2 images?
questions.explanation: EC2 Image Builder is the fully managed service that automates the creation, testing, versioning, and management of custom AMIs, including applying patches and running validation tests. An AMI (B) is the resulting image itself rather than a management service, AWS Launch Wizard (C) helps deploy supported applications, and Elastic Beanstalk (D) is a platform-as-a-service for applications rather than an image factory.

questions.question: A company wants an automated process to continuously scan its Amazon EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector is the automated vulnerability management service that continuously scans EC2 instances (and container images) for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. Amazon GuardDuty (A) analyzes threat intelligence for malicious activity, Amazon Detective (C) investigates security findings after the fact, and Amazon Cognito (D) is an identity service for applications — none continuously scans for software vulnerabilities.

questions.question: A company needs to perform data processing once a week that typically takes about 5 hours to complete. Which AWS service should the company use for this workload?
questions.explanation: A 5-hour weekly batch job exceeds Lambda's maximum function timeout (15 minutes), so Amazon EC2 is the appropriate service: it can run for the full duration and can be launched and terminated around the job window. AWS Lambda (A) cannot run 5 hours in one invocation, AWS CodeDeploy (C) deploys code rather than running data-processing jobs, and AWS Wavelength (D) extends infrastructure to edge networks for low-latency mobile use cases.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature provides log information of the inbound and outbound traffic on network interfaces in a VPC?
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs is the feature that captures information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in a VPC — accepted and rejected traffic — providing exactly the inbound/outbound log information required. CloudWatch Logs (A) stores application and system logs, CloudTrail (B) records API calls rather than network packets, and IAM (D) manages permissions rather than network traffic.

questions.question: A company wants to design a centralized storage system to manage the configuration data and passwords for its critical business applications. Which AWS service or capability will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: Systems Manager Parameter Store is the most cost-effective choice for centralized configuration data and (non-sensitive) passwords: the standard tier is free, while advanced parameters and Secrets Manager charge per secret. Secrets Manager (B) would work but costs more per secret and is aimed at credentials requiring rotation, AWS Config (C) tracks resource configuration compliance rather than storing app config, and S3 (D) is object storage without Parameter Store's hierarchical parameter model and IAM-integrated retrieval.

questions.question: A company plans to deploy containers on AWS. The company wants full control of the compute resources that host the containers. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 gives the customer full control over the underlying compute resources — instance type, AMI/OS, sizing, networking, and the placement of the containers — because the customer manages the host instances themselves. Amazon EKS (A) and Amazon ECS (D) are container orchestration services whose control planes are managed by AWS, and AWS Fargate (B) is a serverless compute engine that abstracts the underlying servers away entirely, so neither offers control of the compute resources hosting the containers.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature allows users to create new AWS accounts, group multiple accounts to organize workflows, and apply policies to groups of accounts?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations is the account management service that lets you create new AWS accounts, organize multiple accounts into organizational units, and apply service control policies (SCPs) to groups of accounts from a central place. IAM (A) manages identities and permissions within a single account, not across accounts; Trusted Advisor (B) provides best-practice recommendations; and CloudFormation (C) provisions infrastructure as code — none of them create or group accounts.

questions.question: A company wants to store and retrieve files in Amazon S3 for its existing on-premises applications by using industry-standard file system protocols. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 File Gateway presents Amazon S3 storage as industry-standard NFS and SMB file shares to on-premises applications, so existing applications can read and write files using normal file system protocols while the data lands in S3. AWS DataSync (A) is for high-throughput data transfer/migration between on-premises and AWS, not for presenting a live file protocol interface; AWS Snowball Edge (B) is a physical device for offline bulk transfers; and AWS Transfer Family (D) exposes S3 over FTP/FTPS/SFTP, not file system protocols.

questions.question: A company wants to block SQL injection attacks. Which AWS service or feature should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF inspects HTTP requests with SQL-injection match rules to block attacks on CloudFront, ALB, and API Gateway. NACLs (B) and security groups (C) filter network packets, and ACM (D) provisions TLS certificates.

questions.question: A company wants a unified tool to provide a consistent method to interact with AWS services. Which AWS service or tool will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: The AWS CLI provides one consistent command-line tool across all services for scripting and automation. ECS (B) runs containers, Cloud9 (C) is a browser IDE, and VPN (D) links networks.

questions.question: A company needs to evaluate its AWS environment and provide best practice recommendations in five categories: cost, performance, service limits, fault tolerance and security. Which AWS service can the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Trusted Advisor evaluates five categories: cost optimization, performance, service limits, fault tolerance, and security. Shield (A) mitigates DDoS, WAF (B) filters web requests, and Service Catalog (C) publishes approved products.

questions.question: Which perspective in the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) includes capabilities for configuration management and patch management?
questions.explanation: The CAF operations perspective covers configuration, patch, change, and incident management for running workloads. Platform (A) delivers infrastructure, security (C) protects assets, and governance (D) oversees programs.

questions.question: A company has a compute workload that is steady, predictable, and uninterruptible. Which Amazon EC2 instance purchasing options meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Steady predictable uninterruptible compute earns the best pricing from Reserved Instances (B) or hourly-commitment Savings Plans (D). On-Demand (A) has no discount, Spot (C) can be interrupted, and Dedicated Hosts (E) add isolation cost.

questions.question: Which Amazon EC2 pricing model is the MOST cost efficient for an uninterruptible workload that runs once a year for 24 hours?
questions.explanation: A once-yearly 24-hour uninterruptible run fits On-Demand pay-per-use with no commitment waste. Reserved (B) needs steady use, Spot (C) can be interrupted, and Dedicated (D) reserves hardware at a premium.

questions.question: Which option is a shared responsibility between AWS and its customers under the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Configuration of Amazon EC2 instance operating systems
questions.explanation: Patch management is shared: AWS patches underlying infrastructure and managed platforms while customers patch guest OSes and applications. EC2 OS configuration (A) and app encryption (B) are customer duties, and physical security (D) is entirely AWS.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate its on-premises workloads to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to separate workloads for chargeback to different departments. Which AWS services or features will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Separate AWS accounts per department (E) with consolidated billing (B) rolling charges together enable departmental chargeback. Placement groups (A) control instance placement, edge locations (C) cache content, and Config (D) audits configuration.

questions.question: Which task is a responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Enable client-side encryption for objects that are stored in Amazon S3.
Configure IAM security policies to comply with the principle of least privilege.
Patch the guest operating system on an Amazon EC2 instance.
Apply updates to the Nitro Hypervisor.
questions.explanation: The Nitro hypervisor is AWS-managed infrastructure, so hypervisor updates are AWS's duty. Client-side encryption (A), IAM policies (B), and guest OS patching (C) are customer duties.

questions.question: Which option is a benefit of using AWS for cloud computing?
options: Trade variable expense for fixed expense
Spending money running and maintaining data centers
questions.explanation: Pay-as-you-go pricing bills only for resources consumed with no upfront commitment. Fixed-for-variable expense (A) reverses the benefit, and decreased agility (C) and running data centers (D) are on-premises burdens.

questions.question: Which option is an AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) business perspective capability?
questions.explanation: Data monetization, deriving measurable business value from data, is a CAF business perspective capability. Culture evolution (A) is people, event management (B) is operations, and platform architecture (D) is platform.

questions.question: A company is assessing its AWS Business Support plan to determine if the plan still meets the company’s needs. The company is considering switching to AWS Enterprise Support. Which additional benefit will the company receive with AWS Enterprise Support?
options: A full set of AWS Trusted Advisor checks
Phone, email, and chat access to cloud support engineers 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
A designated technical account manager (TAM) to assist in monitoring and optimization
A consultative review and architecture guidance for the company’s applications
questions.explanation: Enterprise Support adds a designated Technical Account Manager for proactive monitoring and optimization. Full Trusted Advisor checks (A) and 24/7 engineer access (B) already come with Business Support, and consultative reviews (D) are available through other advisory engagements.

questions.question: Which pricing model will interrupt a running Amazon EC2 instance if capacity becomes temporarily unavailable?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances reclaim capacity with two minutes notice when AWS needs it back, interrupting workloads. On-Demand (A) and Reserved options (B, D) run uninterrupted.

questions.question: Which options are AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) security perspective capabilities? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The CAF security perspective includes incident response processes (C) and infrastructure protection controls (D). Observability (A) is a platform capability, incident and problem management (B) is operations, and availability and continuity (E) is a reliability concern.

questions.question: A company wants to run its workload on Amazon EC2 instances for more than 1 year. This workload will run continuously. Which option offers a discounted hourly rate compared to the hourly rate of On-Demand Instances?
questions.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans commit hourly spend for one or three years in exchange for discounted rates on that family. Graviton (A) is a processor type, Dedicated Hosts (B) add isolation cost, and Auto Scaling (D) adjusts capacity.

questions.question: Which characteristic of the AWS Cloud helps users eliminate underutilized CPU capacity?
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the cloud characteristic that lets you automatically scale resources up (and back down) with demand, so you never pay for — and never have to pre-provision — idle, underutilized CPU capacity. Agility (A) is about moving fast, reliability (C) is about surviving failures, and durability (D) is about data surviving over time — none of them directly addresses eliminating wasted CPU capacity.

questions.question: Which AWS services can a company use to achieve a loosely coupled architecture? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Amazon SQS (B) and AWS Step Functions (E) both decouple components so they communicate asynchronously through messages or state-machine executions rather than direct calls, which is the essence of a loosely coupled architecture. Amazon WorkSpaces (A) is a desktop-as-a-service offering, Amazon Connect (C) is a contact center service, and AWS Trusted Advisor (D) is a best-practice recommendation service — none provides decoupling between application components.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud service can send alerts to customers if custom spending thresholds are exceeded?
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets lets you define custom spending thresholds (by service, account, tag, or across accounts) and sends alerts — by email and SNS — when actual or forecasted spending exceeds those thresholds. Cost Explorer (B) visualizes and forecasts historical/forecasted spend but does not send threshold alerts on its own, cost allocation tags (C) categorize costs for reporting, and AWS Organizations (D) aggregates accounts but has no built-in custom-threshold alerting.

questions.question: A company plans to migrate to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to use the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) to define and track business outcomes as part of its cloud transformation journey. Which AWS CAF governance perspective capability will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Benefits management is the AWS CAF Governance perspective capability focused on defining, tracking, and realizing the business outcomes (benefits) of a cloud transformation, which matches the requirement to define and track business outcomes. Risk management (B) also sits in Governance but addresses identifying and mitigating risk rather than tracking outcomes, application portfolio management (C) belongs to the Application Portfolio Management/Platform area focused on application rationalization, and cloud financial management (D) is about cost and spend rather than business outcomes broadly.

questions.question: A company needs to quickly and securely move files over long distances between its client and an Amazon S3 bucket. Which S3 feature will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration (B) is the S3 feature built for quickly and securely moving files over long distances: it uploads data to a nearby CloudFront edge location and carries it to the bucket over AWS's optimized network path. S3 Versioning (A) keeps prior versions of objects, S3 ACLs (C) are an (older) access-control mechanism, and S3 Intelligent-Tiering (D) automatically moves objects between storage classes to reduce cost — none speeds up long-distance transfers.

questions.question: A company needs to continuously run an experimental workload on an Amazon EC2 instance and stop the instance after 12 hours. Which instance purchasing option will meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: On-Demand Instances (A) are the most cost-effective for an experimental workload that runs for just 12 hours and is then stopped, because there is no commitment and billing simply stops when the instance does. Reserved Instances (B) require a one- or three-year commitment that would be wasted on a 12-hour run, Spot Instances (C) can be interrupted mid-experiment (they are meant for interruptible workloads), and Dedicated Instances (D) cost a premium for single-tenant hardware that this use case does not need.

questions.question: Which cloud transformation journey phase of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) focuses on demonstrating how the cloud helps accelerate business outcomes?
questions.explanation: The CAF Envision phase demonstrates how cloud capabilities accelerate business outcomes and defines measurable goals. Scale (A) expands migrations, Align (C) secures stakeholder buy-in, and Launch (D) delivers pilot workloads.

questions.question: Which option is a customer responsibility under the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Maintenance of underlying hardware of Amazon EC2 instances
questions.explanation: Customers own their application data security, including classification, encryption, and access control. Hardware maintenance (A), data-center security (C), and VPC infrastructure components (D) are AWS duties.

questions.question: A company wants its Amazon EC2 instances to operate in a highly available environment, even if there is a natural disaster in a particular geographic area. Which approach will achieve this goal?
options: Use EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions.
Use EC2 instances in multiple Amazon CloudFront locations.
Use EC2 instances in multiple edge locations.
Use EC2 instances in AWS Local Zones.
questions.explanation: Spreading EC2 across multiple Regions survives a regional natural disaster since Regions are geographically independent. CloudFront and edge locations (B, C) cache content without relocating compute, and Local Zones (D) extend a single Region.

questions.question: A company wants to modernize and convert a monolithic application into microservices. The company wants to move the application to AWS. Which migration strategy should the company use?
questions.explanation: Converting a monolith to microservices is refactoring or re-architecting. Rehost (A) lifts unchanged, replatform (B) makes small optimizations, and repurchase (C) swaps products.

questions.question: A systems administrator created a new IAM user for a developer and assigned the user an access key instead of a user name and password. What is the access key used for?
options: To access the AWS account as the AWS account root user
To access the AWS account through the AWS Management Console
To access the AWS account through a CLI
To access all of a company’s AWS accounts
questions.explanation: IAM access keys authenticate programmatic CLI and SDK calls with signed requests. Root access (A) uses separate credentials, console login (B) uses username and password, and one key cannot span all company accounts (D).

questions.question: Which option is an environment that consists of one or more data centers?
questions.explanation: An Availability Zone consists of one or more discrete data centers with independent power and networking within a Region. CloudFront (A) is a CDN, VPC (C) is a virtual network, and Outposts (D) extends AWS on premises.

questions.question: A company is moving an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The company must migrate 50 petabytes of file storage data to AWS with the least possible operational overhead. Which AWS service or resource should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Snowmobile moves up to 100 PB per truck offline, the practical choice for 50 PB of file storage with minimal operational effort. Snowball Edge devices (B) hold about 80 TB each, Data Exchange (C) licenses datasets, and DMS (D) migrates databases.

questions.question: A company has an application with robust hardware requirements. The application must be accessed by students who are using lightweight, low-cost laptops. Which AWS service will help the company deploy the application without investing in backend infrastructure or high-end client hardware?
questions.explanation: Amazon AppStream 2.0 streams GPU-heavy applications to lightweight laptops with no backend infrastructure to manage. AppSync (B) builds GraphQL APIs, WorkLink (C) secures mobile intranet access, and Beanstalk (D) manages app servers.

questions.question: A company wants to query its server logs to gain insights about its customers’ experiences. Which AWS service will store this data MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 durably stores server logs at the lowest per-GB cost with Athena available for querying. Aurora (A) is a relational database, EFS (B) is shared file storage, and EBS (C) attaches to single instances at higher cost.

questions.question: Which of the following is a recommended design principle for AWS Cloud architecture?
options: Build a single application component that can handle all the application functionality.
Make large changes on fewer iterations to reduce chances of failure.
Avoid monolithic architecture by segmenting workloads.
questions.explanation: Segmenting workloads avoids monoliths so components scale and fail independently. Tight coupling (A) and single components (B) are anti-patterns, and large infrequent changes (C) increase failure blast radius.

questions.question: Which AWS service helps users audit API activity across their AWS account?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail logs API activity across the account for auditing who did what and when. Inspector (B) scans vulnerabilities, WAF (C) filters web requests, and Config (D) tracks configuration history.

questions.question: Which task is a customer’s responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Management of the guest operating systems
Maintenance of the configuration of infrastructure devices
Management of the host operating systems and virtualization
Maintenance of the software that powers Availability Zones
questions.explanation: Customers manage guest operating systems on EC2 including patching and configuration. Infrastructure devices (B), host OS and virtualization (C), and AZ software (D) are AWS duties.

questions.question: A company wants to automatically add and remove Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants the EC2 instances to adjust to varying workloads dynamically. Which service or feature will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: EC2 Auto Scaling adds and removes instances dynamically with demand policies. DynamoDB (A) is a database, Spot (B) is a pricing model, and the Snow Family (C) transfers data offline.

questions.question: A user wants to securely automate the management and rotation of credentials that are shared between applications, while spending the least amount of time on managing tasks. Which AWS service or feature can be used to accomplish this?
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager automates credential storage, rotation, and retrieval between applications. CloudHSM (A) hosts key hardware, KMS (B) manages encryption keys, and server-side encryption (D) protects objects rather than rotating credentials.

questions.question: Which security service automatically recognizes and classifies sensitive data or intellectual property on AWS?
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie uses ML to automatically discover and classify sensitive data and IP across S3. GuardDuty (A) detects threats, Inspector (C) scans vulnerabilities, and Shield (D) mitigates DDoS.

questions.question: Which actions are best practices for an AWS account root user? (Choose two.)
options: Share root user credentials with team members.
Create multiple root users for the account, separated by environment.
Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the root user.
Create an IAM user with administrator privileges for daily administrative tasks, instead of using the root user.
Use programmatic access instead of the root user and password.
questions.explanation: Root best practices enable MFA on the root user (C) and use a separate IAM admin for daily tasks instead of root (D). Sharing root credentials (A) and creating multiple roots (B) are impossible or unsafe, and programmatic root use (E) should be avoided.

questions.question: A company is running a critical workload on an Amazon RDS DB instance. The company needs the DB instance to be highly available with a recovery time of less than 5 minutes. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Create a read replica of the DB instance.
Create a template of the DB instance by using AWS CloudFormation.
Take frequent snapshots of the DB instance. Store the snapshots in Amazon S3.
Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ deployment.
questions.explanation: Converting RDS to Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby for automatic failover within minutes. Read replicas (A) scale reads asynchronously, CloudFormation templates (B) redeploy infrastructure, and snapshots (C) restore more slowly.

questions.question: A company plans to migrate its application to AWS and run the application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application will have continuous usage for 1 year. Which EC2 instance purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: Continuous 1-year EC2 use earns the best pricing from a 1-year Reserved Instance. Spot (B) can be interrupted, On-Demand (C) has no discount, and Dedicated Hosts (D) add isolation cost.

questions.question: A company needs to transfer data between an Amazon S3 bucket and an on-premises application. Who is responsible for the security of this data, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
questions.explanation: Data in transit between S3 and on-premises, including encryption and access control, is the customer's responsibility under shared responsibility. AWS (B) secures the underlying platform, and vendors or partners (C, D) are not parties to the model.

questions.question: Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework refers to the ability of a system to recover from infrastructure or service disruptions and dynamically acquire computing resources to meet demand?
questions.explanation: Recovering from disruptions while dynamically acquiring resources defines the reliability pillar. Security (A) protects data, performance efficiency (C) uses resources well, and cost optimization (D) avoids waste.

questions.question: A company wants to identify Amazon S3 buckets that are shared with another AWS account. Which AWS service or feature will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer identifies S3 buckets and other resources shared cross-account. Lake Formation (A) governs data lakes, credential reports (B) audit keys and MFA, and CloudWatch (C) monitors metrics.

questions.question: Which AWS service gives users the ability to build interactive business intelligence dashboards that include machine learning insights?
questions.explanation: Amazon QuickSight builds interactive BI dashboards with ML insights. Athena (A) queries S3 with SQL, Kendra (B) searches documents, and Redshift (C) warehouses data.

questions.question: Which of the following is an AWS value proposition that describes a user’s ability to scale infrastructure based on demand?
questions.explanation: Resource elasticity scales infrastructure up and down with demand. Speed of innovation (A) ships features faster, decoupled architecture (C) isolates components, and global deployment (D) expands geography.

questions.question: Which action is a security best practice for access to sensitive data that is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket?
options: Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) on the S3 bucket.
Use IAM roles for applications that require access to the S3 bucket.
Configure AWS WAF to prevent unauthorized access to the S3 bucket.
Configure Amazon GuardDuty to prevent unauthorized access to the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: IAM roles grant applications temporary S3 credentials without storing long-lived keys, the documented best practice. Replication (A) copies objects, WAF (C) filters web requests, and GuardDuty (D) detects threats rather than preventing access.

questions.question: A company wants to know more about the benefits offered by cloud computing. The company wants to understand the operational advantage of agility. How does AWS provide agility for users?
options: The ability the ensure high availability by deploying workloads to multiple regions
A pay-as-you-go model for many services and resources
The ability to transfer infrastructure management to the AWS Cloud
The ability to provision and deprovision resources quickly with minimal effort
questions.explanation: Cloud agility refers to the ability to provision and deprovision resources quickly and with minimal effort, so teams can experiment and respond to change rapidly — AWS describes agility as one of the main advantages of cloud computing. High availability across Regions (A) is a reliability concern, pay-as-you-go (B) is the cost model benefit, and transferring infrastructure management to AWS (C) describes reduced operational burden rather than agility itself.

questions.question: A company needs a central user portal so that users can log in to third-party business applications that support Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
questions.explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS Single Sign-On) is the AWS service that provides a central user portal for single sign-on into third-party business applications that support SAML 2.0, as well as AWS accounts and applications. Amazon Cognito (B) is aimed at application end users rather than an employee portal for SAML 2.0 business apps, IAM (A) manages permissions but does not provide a SAML user portal, and the AWS CLI (D) is a command-line tool with no SSO portal capability.

questions.question: Which AWS service should users use to learn about AWS service availability and operations?
questions.explanation: The AWS Health Dashboard is the single place to view the current and historical health of AWS services, including service availability and operational issues (the Personal Health Dashboard also shows events affecting your specific resources). EventBridge (A) is an event router, Service Catalog (B) catalogs approved products, and Control Tower (C) governs multi-account setups — none report service health.

questions.question: Which AWS service or tool can be used to capture information about inbound and outbound traffic in an Amazon VPC?
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs capture information about IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in a VPC, which is exactly the inbound/outbound traffic data requested. Amazon Inspector (B) assesses workloads for vulnerabilities, VPC endpoint services (C) enable PrivateLink connections, and a NAT gateway (D) performs address translation — none record traffic metadata.

questions.question: What is the customer ALWAYS responsible for managing, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
questions.explanation: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, customers are always responsible for the data they put into the cloud — 'security in the cloud' includes customer data, while AWS is responsible for 'security of the cloud' hardware and infrastructure. Networking infrastructure, software licenses, and encryption-key management are split elsewhere in the model depending on the service, but responsibility for customer data never transfers to AWS.

questions.question: Which AWS service can be used to retrieve compliance reports on demand?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for on-demand access to AWS compliance reports and agreements, such as SOC, PCI DSS, and ISO reports. Secrets Manager (A) stores secrets, Security Hub (C) aggregates security findings, and Certificate Manager (D) provisions TLS certificates — none provide compliance documentation.

questions.question: Which AWS service enables users to check for vulnerabilities on Amazon EC2 instances by using predefined assessment templates?
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector is an automated vulnerability management service that continuously scans EC2 instances (and workloads) for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure using assessment templates and rules. AWS WAF (A) protects web applications, Trusted Advisor (B) gives best-practice checks, and Shield (D) protects against DDoS — none perform vulnerability assessments of instances.

questions.question: A company plans to migrate to the AWS Cloud. The company is gathering information about its on-premises infrastructure and requires information such as the hostname, IP address, and MAC address. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Application Discovery Service collects information about on-premises servers — including hostname, IP address, MAC address, and configuration — to help plan migrations. DataSync (A) moves file data, Application Migration Service (B) migrates entire servers, and DMS (D) migrates databases; only Discovery Service gathers the inventory metadata described.

questions.question: Which action will help increase security in the AWS Cloud?
options: Enable programmatic access for all IAM users.
Use IAM users instead of IAM roles to delegate permissions.
Rotate access keys on a reoccurring basis.
Use inline policies instead of customer managed policies.
questions.explanation: Rotating access keys on a recurring basis limits the damage if a key is compromised and is a documented IAM security best practice. Enabling programmatic access for all IAM users (A) increases the number of long-lived credentials rather than improving security, IAM roles (B) are preferred over long-lived IAM users for delegation, and inline policies (D) are harder to manage at scale than customer managed policies.

questions.question: A company is planning to migrate its application to the AWS Cloud. Which AWS tool or set of resources should the company use to analyze and assess its readiness for migration?
questions.explanation: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) organizes migration guidance into perspectives (business, people, governance, platform, security, operations) and is the AWS toolset specifically for analyzing and assessing readiness to migrate to the cloud. The Pricing Calculator (B) estimates costs, the Well-Architected Framework (C) reviews workload architecture against best practices, and Budgets (D) tracks spend — none assess migration readiness.

questions.question: Which of the following describes some of the core functionality of Amazon S3?
options: Amazon S3 is a high-performance block storage service that is designed for use with Amazon EC2.
Amazon S3 is an object storage service that provides high-level performance, security, scalability, and data availability.
Amazon S3 is a fully managed, highly reliable, and scalable file storage system that is accessible over the industry-standard SMB protocol.
Amazon S3 is a scalable, fully managed elastic NFS for use with AWS Cloud services and on-premises resources.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 is AWS's object storage service, offering high performance, security, scalability, and data availability for objects at any scale. Option A describes Amazon EBS (block storage), option C resembles Amazon FSx (managed file storage over SMB), and option D describes Amazon EFS (elastic NFS) — not S3.

questions.question: Which AWS benefit is demonstrated by on-demand technology services that enable companies to replace upfront fixed expenses with variable expenses?
questions.explanation: The pay-as-you-go (variable expense) model is what lets companies replace upfront fixed expenses (buying data centers and servers) with variable expenses that vary with usage — AWS cites this as a key financial benefit of cloud. Economies of scale (B) describes AWS's lower unit costs passed on to users, while availability (A) and global reach (D) are unrelated to the fixed-vs-variable expense distinction.

questions.question: Which AWS services or features enable users to connect on-premises networks to a VPC? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates an encrypted connection over the public internet between an on-premises network and a VPC, and AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated private network link — both connect on-premises networks to a VPC. Elastic Load Balancing (B) distributes traffic within AWS, VPC peering (D) connects two VPCs, and CloudFront (E) is a CDN — none connect to on-premises networks.

questions.question: A user needs to quickly deploy a nonrelational database on AWS. The user does not want to manage the underlying hardware or the database software. Which AWS service can be used to accomplish this?
questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed serverless NoSQL (nonrelational) database, so users can deploy it quickly without managing hardware or database software. Amazon RDS (A) and Aurora (C) are relational databases, and Redshift (D) is a data warehouse — while all are managed, only DynamoDB is nonrelational as required.

questions.question: Which actions are examples of a company’s effort to rightsize its AWS resources to control cloud costs? (Choose two.)
options: Switch from Amazon RDS to Amazon DynamoDB to accommodate NoSQL datasets.
Base the selection of Amazon EC2 instance types on past utilization patterns.
Use Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies to move objects that users access infrequently to lower-cost storage tiers.
Use Multi-AZ deployments for Amazon RDS.
Replace existing Amazon EC2 instances with AWS Elastic Beanstalk.
questions.explanation: Rightsizing means matching resource capacity to actual workload demand: choosing EC2 instance types based on past utilization patterns (B) and using S3 Lifecycle policies to move infrequently accessed objects to cheaper storage tiers (C) both rightsize resources to control cost. Switching databases to NoSQL (A) is a re-platforming choice, Multi-AZ (D) is for high availability, and moving to Elastic Beanstalk (E) is a deployment-platform change — none are rightsizing.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature can a company use to apply security rules to specific Amazon EC2 instances?
questions.explanation: Security groups are stateful virtual firewalls attached to specific EC2 instances (or ENIs), so security rules apply to the individual instances they're associated with. Network ACLs (A) operate at the subnet level rather than per instance, Trusted Advisor (C) provides recommendations, and AWS WAF (D) protects web applications at the HTTP layer.

questions.question: Which design principles support the reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
options: Deploy resources globally to improve response time.
questions.explanation: The reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework is supported by design principles including automatically recovering from failure (E) and scaling automatically to meet demand (C) — e.g., using monitoring and automation to detect failure and restore service, and scaling capacity with demand. Performing operations as code (A) and enabling traceability (B) belong to the operational excellence pillar, and globally deploying resources (D) is not itself a reliability design principle.

questions.question: A company that uses AWS needs to transfer 2 TB of data. Which type of transfer of that data would result in no cost for the company?
options: Inbound data transfer from the internet
Outbound data transfer to the internet
questions.explanation: AWS does not charge for data transfer inbound (upload) from the internet to AWS, so a 2 TB inbound transfer costs nothing. Outbound data transfer to the internet (B) is charged (with a monthly free tier), data transfer between Regions (C) is charged in both directions, and data transfer between Availability Zones (D) is charged per GB in both directions.

questions.question: A company wants to create templates that the company can reuse to deploy multiple AWS resources. Which AWS service or feature can the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation lets you create reusable templates that describe AWS resources so you can deploy them repeatedly and consistently across environments and accounts. Marketplace (A) sells third-party software, an AMI (B) is an image for launching EC2 instances rather than a general resource-deployment template, and OpsWorks (C) is a configuration-management service.

questions.question: A company is building an application that requires the ability to send, store, and receive messages between application components. The company has another requirement to process messages in first-in, first-out (FIFO) order. Which AWS service should the company use?
questions.explanation: Amazon SQS is a fully managed message queue for decoupling components, and it offers a FIFO queue type that guarantees first-in, first-out ordering and exactly-once processing. Step Functions (A) orchestrates workflows, SNS (B) is a pub/sub notification service (its FIFO topic is for fan-out rather than queue semantics between components), and Kinesis (D) orders streaming data by shard rather than providing a general FIFO message queue.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature is a browser-based, pre-authenticated service that can be launched directly from the AWS Management Console?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudShell is a browser-based shell that is pre-authenticated in the AWS Management Console, letting you run AWS CLI and administrative tasks without managing credentials or local setup. Lightsail (B) is a simplified VPS offering, Cloud9 (C) is a cloud IDE rather than the console's built-in shell, and 'AWS API' (A) is not a service.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate its database to a managed AWS service that is compatible with PostgreSQL. Which AWS services will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS supports PostgreSQL as a managed relational database engine, and Amazon Aurora offers a PostgreSQL-compatible edition — both are managed services compatible with PostgreSQL. Athena (A) queries data in S3, EC2 (C) is self-managed compute, and DynamoDB (D) is a NoSQL database — none are PostgreSQL-compatible managed databases.

questions.question: A company has a fleet of cargo ships. The cargo ships have sensors that collect data at sea, where there is intermittent or no internet connectivity. The company needs to collect, format, and process the data at sea and move the data to AWS later. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Snowball Edge is an edge-compute and data transfer device designed to collect, format, and process data locally in disconnected or intermittent environments (like ships at sea) and then transfer it to AWS when connectivity allows. IoT Core (A) requires connectivity to AWS, Lightsail (B) is cloud-based VPS hosting, and Storage Gateway (C) is a hybrid service that needs a live link to AWS.

questions.question: A company hosts an application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The application uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send messages. Which AWS service or feature will give the application permission to access required AWS services?
questions.explanation: An IAM role grants an EC2 instance's application permissions to access other AWS services (like SNS) through temporary credentials delivered via the instance profile — this is the standard way to give workloads permissions. ACM (A) manages certificates, Security Hub (C) aggregates security findings, and GuardDuty (D) is a threat detection service — none grant application permissions.

questions.question: A user has limited knowledge of AWS services, but wants to quickly deploy a scalable Node.js application in the AWS Cloud. Which service should be used to deploy the application?
questions.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk deploys a scalable Node.js app from uploaded code while provisioning load balancing and scaling automatically. CloudFormation (A) needs templates, EC2 (C) needs server management, and OpsWorks (D) needs Chef/Puppet configuration.

questions.question: A company needs a content delivery network that provides secure delivery of data, videos, applications, and APIs to users globally with low latency and high transfer speeds. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: CloudFront is the CDN delivering data, video, apps, and APIs globally with low latency over HTTPS. Load balancing (B) distributes within Regions, S3 (C) stores origins, and Elastic Transcoder (D) converts media.

questions.question: A company needs to use third-party software for its workload on AWS. Which AWS service or feature can the company use to purchase the software?
questions.explanation: AWS Marketplace sells third-party software and AMIs for AWS workloads. Resource Access Manager (A) shares resources, Managed Services (B) operates environments, and License Manager (C) tracks licenses.

questions.question: A company needs fully managed, highly reliable, and scalable file storage that is accessible over the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
options: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
questions.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server provides managed highly available file storage over SMB. S3 (A) is object storage, EFS (B) serves NFS for Linux, and EBS (C) attaches block storage to one instance.

questions.question: A company needs to centrally configure and manage Amazon VPC security groups across multiple AWS accounts within an organization in AWS Organizations. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Firewall Manager centrally configures and manages security groups and WAF rules across Organization accounts. GuardDuty (B) detects threats, Detective (C) investigates, and WAF (D) filters single-resource traffic.

questions.question: Which task is a responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Configure identity and access management for applications.
Manage encryption options for data that is stored on AWS.
Configure security groups for Amazon EC2 instances.
Maintain the physical hardware of the infrastructure.
questions.explanation: Maintaining physical infrastructure hardware is entirely AWS's duty. Application IAM (A), encryption choices (B), and EC2 security groups (C) are customer duties.

questions.question: A company has an Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet. The company wants to initiate a connection to the internet to pull operating system updates while preventing traffic from the internet from accessing the EC2 instance. Which AWS managed service allows this?
questions.explanation: A NAT gateway in a public subnet lets private-subnet EC2 reach the internet for updates while blocking inbound connections. VPC endpoints (A) reach AWS services privately, PrivateLink (C) exposes services, and peering (D) connects VPCs.

questions.question: Which actions are the responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)
options: Patching the operating system on Amazon EC2 instances
Enforcing a strict password policy for IAM users
Patching the operating system on Amazon RDS instances
Configuring security groups and network ACLs
questions.explanation: AWS secures the virtualization layer (A) and patches managed platforms such as RDS (D). EC2 guest OS patching (B), IAM password policies (C), and security groups (E) are customer duties.

questions.question: A company is storing data that will not be frequently accessed in the AWS Cloud. If the company needs to access the data, the data needs to be retrieved within 12 hours. The company wants a solution that is cost-effective for storage costs for each gigabyte. Which Amazon S3 storage class will meet these requirements?
options: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)
questions.explanation: Glacier Flexible Retrieval offers low-cost archival storage with retrieval in minutes to 12 hours. Standard (A) costs more, One Zone-IA (C) suits infrequent immediate access, and Standard-IA (D) suits frequent infrequent access.

questions.question: Which AWS service or resource can be used to identify services that have been used by a user within a specified date range?
options: AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer
questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer's unused-access findings identify services each user actually used in a date range for least-privilege reviews. S3 ACLs (A) grant object access, ACM (B) manages certificates, and Network Access Analyzer (C) audits network paths.

questions.question: A company needs to engage third-party consultants to help maintain and support its AWS environment and the company’s business needs. Which AWS service or resource will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: The AWS Partner Network (APN) connects customers with vetted third-party consultants for maintaining AWS environments. Support (A) provides AWS engineers, Organizations (B) manages accounts, and Service Catalog (C) publishes products.

questions.question: A company wants to create Amazon QuickSight dashboards every week by using its billing data. Which AWS feature or tool can the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: The Cost and Usage Report exports granular billing line items that QuickSight can ingest for weekly dashboards. Budgets (A) alerts on thresholds, Cost Explorer (B) visualizes interactively, and Anomaly Detection (D) flags spikes.

questions.question: A company is planning to move data backups to the AWS Cloud. The company needs to replace on-premises storage with storage that is cloud-based but locally cached. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Storage Gateway caches cloud storage locally on premises while backing it to AWS. Snowcone (B) ships edge data, Backup (C) centralizes backups, and EFS (D) is cloud file storage without local caching.

questions.question: A company needs to organize its resources and track AWS costs on a detailed level. The company needs to categorize costs by business department, environment, and application. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Access the AWS Cost Management console to organize resources, set an AWS budget, and receive notifications of unintentional usage.
Use tags to organize the resources. Activate cost allocation tags to track AWS costs on a detailed level.
Create Amazon CloudWatch dashboards to visually organize and track costs individually.
Access the AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard to organize and track resource consumption on a detailed level.
questions.explanation: Activating cost allocation tags groups spend by department, environment, and application for detailed tracking. Budgets (A) alert on limits, CloudWatch dashboards (C) monitor operations, and the billing dashboard (D) shows totals without tag taxonomy.

questions.question: A company needs to plan, schedule, and run hundreds of thousands of computing jobs on AWS. Which AWS service can the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS Batch plans, schedules, and runs hundreds of thousands of batch computing jobs across dynamic resources. Step Functions (A) orchestrates workflows, Service Catalog (B) publishes products, and SQS (C) queues messages.

questions.question: Which AWS services or features provide high availability and low latency by enabling failover across different AWS Regions? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Route 53 DNS failover (A) and Global Accelerator anycast routing (D) shift traffic across Regions for availability and low latency. Network and Application Load Balancers (B, E) distribute within Regions, and Transfer Acceleration (C) speeds S3 uploads.

questions.question: Which of the following is a way to use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups to scale capacity in the AWS Cloud?
options: Scale the number of EC2 instances in or out automatically, based on demand.
Scale the size of EC2 instances up or down automatically, based on demand.
Transfer unused CPU resources between EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: Auto Scaling groups scale EC2 instance count in and out automatically with demand policies. There are no serverless EC2 instances (B), size changes (C) need manual resizing, and CPU cannot transfer between instances (D).

questions.question: Which abilities are benefits of the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: Trade variable expenses for capital expenses.
Plan capacity in advance of deployments.
Take advantage of economies of scale.
questions.explanation: Cloud benefits include deploying globally in minutes (B) and economies of scale (D). Trading variable for capital expense (A) reverses the model, capacity is not planned in advance (C), and connectivity dependence remains (E).

questions.question: Which AWS security service protects applications from distributed denial of service attacks with always-on detection and automatic inline mitigations?
questions.explanation: AWS Shield provides always-on DDoS detection with automatic inline mitigations. Inspector (A) scans vulnerabilities, WAF (B) filters application requests, and ELB (C) distributes traffic.

questions.question: Which AWS service allows users to model and provision AWS resources using common programming languages?
questions.explanation: The AWS CDK models and provisions resources using TypeScript, Python, Java, C#, and Go. CloudFormation (A) uses JSON or YAML templates, CodePipeline (B) automates releases, and Systems Manager (D) manages operations.

questions.question: Which Amazon EC2 instance pricing model can provide discounts of up to 90%?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances use spare capacity at discounts of up to 90% off On-Demand. Reserved (A) discounts less, On-Demand (B) is full price, and Dedicated Hosts (C) cost more.

questions.question: Which of the following acts as an instance-level firewall to control inbound and outbound access?
questions.explanation: Security groups are stateful instance-level firewalls controlling inbound and outbound access. NACLs (A) filter subnets, Trusted Advisor (C) checks best practices, and virtual private gateways (D) terminate VPNs.

questions.question: A company must be able to develop, test, and launch an application in the AWS Cloud quickly. Which advantage of cloud computing will meet these requirements?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
questions.explanation: Speed and agility let teams develop, test, and launch quickly with instant resources. Capacity guessing (A), expense tradeoffs (B), and economies of scale (C) are separate benefits.

questions.question: A company has teams that have different job roles and responsibilities. The company’s employees often change teams. The company needs to manage permissions for the employees so that the permissions are appropriate for the job responsibilities. Which IAM resource should the company use to meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
questions.explanation: IAM user groups assign one policy set to many members, so team changes need only group membership updates. Roles (B) suit temporary access, instance profiles (C) attach roles to EC2, and per-user policies (D) multiply management overhead.

questions.question: Which AWS service can a company use to securely store and encrypt passwords for a database?
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager encrypts database passwords at rest with rotation and programmatic retrieval. Shield (A) mitigates DDoS, IAM (C) manages permissions rather than storing secrets, and Cognito (D) authenticates app users.

questions.question: What can a cloud practitioner use to retrieve AWS security and compliance documents and submit them as evidence to an auditor or regulator?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact hosts on-demand security and compliance documents for auditors and regulators. Certificate Manager (A) provisions TLS certificates, Systems Manager (B) manages operations, and Inspector (C) scans vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Which encryption types can be used to protect objects at rest in Amazon S3? (Choose two.)
options: Server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3)
Server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed keys (SSE-KMS)
questions.explanation: S3 at-rest encryption options include SSE-S3 with S3-managed keys (A) and SSE-KMS with KMS keys (B). TLS (C) and SSL (D) protect data in transit, and TDE (E) is a database feature rather than S3 encryption.

questions.question: A company wants to integrate its online shopping website with social media login credentials. Which AWS service can the company use to make this integration?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
questions.explanation: Cognito user pools federate social identity providers for shopping-site login. Directory Service (A) hosts directories, IAM (B) manages AWS permissions, and Identity Center (D) provides workforce SSO.

questions.question: Which AWS service is used to track, record, and audit configuration changes made to AWS resources?
questions.explanation: AWS Config records configuration changes to resources for tracking, recording, and auditing. Shield (A) mitigates DDoS, IAM (C) manages permissions, and Inspector (D) scans vulnerabilities.

questions.question: A customer runs an On-Demand Amazon Linux EC2 instance for 3 hours, 5 minutes, and 6 seconds. For how much time will the customer be billed?
questions.explanation: Linux EC2 bills per second with a one-minute minimum, so 3 hours 5 minutes 6 seconds bills exactly that duration. Hourly rounding (A, D) and minute rounding (C) do not apply to Linux per-second billing.

questions.question: A company website is experiencing DDoS attacks. Which AWS service can help protect the company website against these attacks?
questions.explanation: AWS Shield (Standard and Advanced) protects websites against DDoS attacks with always-on detection. Resource Access Manager (A) shares resources, Amplify (B) hosts apps, and GuardDuty (C) detects threats without mitigating volumetric attacks.

questions.question: A company wants a customized assessment of its current on-premises environment. The company wants to understand its projected running costs in the AWS Cloud. Which AWS service or tool will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Migration Evaluator builds customized assessments of on-premises environments with projected AWS running costs. Trusted Advisor (A) checks best practices, Inspector (B) scans vulnerabilities, and Control Tower (C) provisions landing zones.

questions.question: A company that has multiple business units wants to centrally manage and govern its AWS Cloud environments. The company wants to automate the creation of AWS accounts, apply service control policies (SCPs), and simplify billing processes. Which AWS service or tool should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations automates account creation, applies SCP governance, and consolidates billing centrally. Cost Explorer (B) visualizes spend, Budgets (C) alerts on thresholds, and Trusted Advisor (D) checks best practices.

questions.question: A company is hosting an application in the AWS Cloud. The company wants to verify that underlying AWS services and general AWS infrastructure are operating normally. Which combination of AWS services can the company use to gather the required information? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Personal Health Dashboard (A) shows account-specific service impacts while the Service Health Dashboard (D) shows general AWS service status. Systems Manager (B) manages operations, Trusted Advisor (C) checks best practices, and Service Catalog (E) publishes products.

questions.question: A company needs to migrate a PostgreSQL database from on-premises to Amazon RDS. Which AWS service or tool should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS DMS replicates PostgreSQL into RDS with minimal downtime. The Cloud Adoption Readiness Tool (A) assesses readiness, Migration Hub (B) tracks status, and Application Migration Service (D) rehosts servers.

questions.question: Which cloud concept is demonstrated by using AWS Compute Optimizer?
questions.explanation: Compute Optimizer analyzes utilization to recommend rightsized instance types, demonstrating the rightsizing concept. Security validation (A), elasticity (C), and global reach (D) are separate concepts.

questions.question: A company hosts a large amount of data in AWS. The company wants to identify if any of the data should be considered sensitive. Which AWS service will meet the requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie is a data-security service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover, classify, and report on sensitive data such as PII stored in Amazon S3, so it directly answers whether stored data should be considered sensitive. Amazon Inspector (A) scans EC2 workloads and container images for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure, not content classification; IAM (C) manages access permissions rather than analyzing data; and CloudWatch (D) is a monitoring and observability service with no sensitive-data discovery capability.

questions.question: A user has a stateful workload that will run on Amazon EC2 for the next 3 years. What is the MOST cost-effective pricing model for this workload?
questions.explanation: For a predictable, uninterrupted three-year workload, Reserved Instances offer the deepest discount (up to roughly 72%) compared with On-Demand because you commit to that instance family/Region for the full term, which is exactly the stateful, long-running scenario described. On-Demand (A) has no commitment but costs the most over three years; Spot Instances provide the largest discounts but can be interrupted with only two minutes' notice, which is unsuitable for a stateful workload that must keep running; and Dedicated capacity adds cost for isolation the workload does not require.

questions.question: Who enables encryption of data at rest for Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)?
questions.explanation: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, encryption of data at rest is a customer responsibility: customers enable EBS volume encryption (for example, account-level default encryption or per-volume settings), with AWS handling the underlying key storage infrastructure. AWS Support (A), KMS (C), and Trusted Advisor (D) do not enable it for you: KMS provides and manages the keys you choose, but turning encryption on for the EBS volume is an action the customer performs.

questions.question: What can a user accomplish using AWS CloudTrail?
options: Generate an IAM user credentials report.
Record API calls made to AWS services.
Assess the compliance of AWS resource configurations with policies and guidelines.
Ensure that Amazon EC2 instances are patched with the latest security updates.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail is the service that records API calls and account activity — who did what, when, and from where — across AWS services, storing them as events for governance, compliance, and troubleshooting. Generating an IAM credentials report (A) is an IAM feature; assessing configuration compliance (C) is AWS Config's purpose; and patching Amazon EC2 instances (D) is the customer's responsibility, handled with tools such as Systems Manager Patch Manager.

questions.question: A company is planning to host its workloads on AWS. Which AWS service requires the company to update and patch the guest operating system?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 is infrastructure-as-a-service: the customer rents virtual servers and remains responsible for guest operating system updates and patching under the shared responsibility model. DynamoDB (A), S3 (B), and Aurora (D) are fully managed services where AWS patches the underlying infrastructure, so the customer never updates a guest OS on those services.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature will search for and identify AWS resources that are shared externally?
questions.explanation: AWS IAM Access Analyzer continuously analyzes your AWS resource policies (S3 buckets, IAM roles, KMS keys, VPC endpoints, etc.) to identify resources shared with external principals — other accounts, organizations, or the public — and reports those findings. OpenSearch (A) is a search and analytics service; Control Tower (B) governs multi-account setup rather than finding shared resources; and Fargate (D) is a serverless container compute engine.

questions.question: A company is migrating its workloads to the AWS Cloud. The company must retain full control of patch management for the guest operating systems that host its applications. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 gives the customer full control of the guest operating system, including patch management, which matches the requirement to retain complete control of OS patching. DynamoDB (A) and RDS (D) are fully managed services where AWS patches the underlying platform, and Lambda (C) abstracts the operating system entirely — in none of those cases does the customer patch a guest OS.

questions.question: At what support level do users receive access to a support concierge?
questions.explanation: The AWS Support Concierge team is available only with the Enterprise Support plan, helping with billing and account guidance as a named part of that plan's offerings. Basic (A), Developer (B), and Business (C) plans do not include concierge access — Business adds a designated TAM and faster response times, but not the concierge team.

questions.question: Which AWS service can a company use to visually design and build serverless applications?
questions.explanation: AWS Application Composer is a visual designer that lets you drag and drop AWS resources onto a canvas and automatically generates the corresponding infrastructure-as-code (SAM/CloudFormation) template for building serverless applications. Lambda (A) runs code, AWS Batch (B) runs batch compute jobs, and App Runner (D) runs container web services — none of them provide visual design and build tooling for serverless apps.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate to AWS and use the same security software it uses on premises. The security software vendor offers its security software as a service on AWS. Where can the company purchase the security solution?
questions.explanation: AWS Marketplace is a curated digital catalog where independent software vendors sell their software-as-a-service and AMI offerings that run on AWS, so a company can purchase its existing security vendor's AWS-hosted security product there. Partner Solutions Finder (A) helps locate consulting partners, Support Center (B) is for support cases, and the Management Console (C) is the interface for managing your own AWS resources, none of which are purchase venues for third-party security software.

questions.question: A company has deployed an Amazon EC2 instance. Which option is an AWS responsibility under the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Installing updates and security patches of guest operating system
Configuration of security groups on each instance
questions.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, configuration of the underlying infrastructure devices (routers, switches, storage systems, the physical and virtualized control plane) is always an AWS responsibility ('security OF the cloud'). Encrypting application data (A), patching the guest OS (B), and configuring security groups on each instance (D) are all customer responsibilities ('security IN the cloud').

questions.question: A company wants to migrate its PostgreSQL database to AWS. The company does not use the database frequently. Which AWS service or resource will meet these requirements with the LEAST management overhead?
questions.explanation: Aurora Serverless is an on-demand, auto-scaling configuration for Aurora PostgreSQL/MySQL that scales capacity with application demand and can be paused when idle, giving the least management overhead for an infrequently used database — you never manage instance sizing yourself. PostgreSQL on EC2 (A) requires you to install, patch, and back up everything; RDS for PostgreSQL (B) and provisioned Aurora (C) still require choosing and paying for a continuously running instance size even when the database is barely used.

questions.question: A company is using Amazon DynamoDB for its application database. Which tasks are the responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)
options: Provide public endpoints to store and retrieve data.
Manage the infrastructure layer and the operating system.
questions.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model for a managed service like DynamoDB, AWS operates and manages the infrastructure and OS of the service (E) and provides the public service endpoints used to store and retrieve data (D). Classifying data (A), configuring access permissions (B), and managing the encryption options chosen for the data (C) are all customer responsibilities — 'security IN the cloud'.

questions.question: A company wants to create a globally accessible ecommerce platform for its customers. The company wants to use a highly available and scalable DNS web service to connect users to the platform. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable DNS web service that routes end users to internet applications by domain name, meeting the global-accessible DNS requirement for the ecommerce platform. Amazon EC2 (A) provides virtual servers, VPC (B) provides isolated network infrastructure, and RDS (D) is a relational database — none of them perform DNS resolution or routing.

questions.question: Which maintenance task is the customer’s responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Amazon EC2 updates and security patches
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 updates and security patches (guest OS patching) are the customer's responsibility under the shared responsibility model — 'security IN the cloud'. Physical connectivity among Availability Zones (A), network switch maintenance (B), and hardware/firmware updates (C) are all exclusively AWS responsibilities — 'security OF the cloud'.

questions.question: A company wants to improve its security posture by reviewing user activity through API calls. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records user activity and API calls across the AWS account, which is exactly what is needed to review user activity through API calls for security analysis. AWS WAF (A) is a web application firewall that filters HTTP traffic; Amazon Detective (B) analyzes and visualizes security findings after they exist rather than recording the raw API activity itself; and CloudWatch (C) collects monitoring metrics and logs, not a complete API-call audit trail.

questions.question: A company is migrating to the AWS Cloud and plans to run experimental workloads for 3 to 6 months on AWS. Which pricing model will meet these requirements?
options: Use Savings Plans for a 3-year term.
questions.explanation: Experimental workloads lasting only 3 to 6 months are a poor fit for commitment-based discounts, so On-Demand Instances — pay-as-you-go with no term commitment and no upfront cost — are the right model. A 3-year Savings Plan (A) and Reserved Instances (C) both lock in a multi-year commitment for a workload explicitly expected to be temporary, and Dedicated Hosts (B) add physical-server isolation and cost that experimental workloads do not need.

questions.question: A company that has AWS Enterprise Support is launching a new version of a popular product in 2 months. The company expects a large increase in traffic to its website. The website is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances. Which action should the company take to assess its readiness to scale for this launch?
options: Replace the EC2 instances with AWS Lambda functions.
Use AWS Infrastructure Event Management (IEM) support.
Submit a request on AWS Marketplace to monitor the event.
Review the coverage reports in the AWS Cost Management console.
questions.explanation: AWS Infrastructure Event Management (IEM) is a support offering where AWS works with you before, during, and after a planned high-traffic event — such as a product launch — to assess readiness and help your architecture scale, which matches this scenario exactly.
