Replacing EC2 with Lambda (A) is an unrequested re-architecture, AWS Marketplace (C) is for purchasing third-party software, and Cost Management coverage reports (D) address spending, not scalability readiness.

questions.question: A company wants to launch multiple workloads on AWS. Each workload is related to a different business unit. The company wants to separate and track costs for each business unit. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Use AWS Organizations and create one account for each business unit.
Use a spreadsheet to control the owners and cost of each resource.
Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to record costs for each business unit.
Use the AWS Billing console to assign owners to resources and track costs.
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations lets you create separate AWS accounts per business unit and consolidate billing, so each business unit's costs are naturally isolated and reported per account with essentially no operational overhead. Maintaining a spreadsheet (B) or a DynamoDB table (C) of costs is manual, error-prone bookkeeping; and assigning owners to individual resources in the Billing console (D) does not scale cleanly across many resources compared to account-level separation.

questions.question: A company wants a time-series database service that makes it easier to store and analyze trillions of events each day. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Timestream is AWS's purpose-built time-series database designed to store and query trillions of time-stamped events per day with automatic data lifecycle tiering, matching the requirement exactly. Neptune (A) is a graph database, Forecast (C) is a forecasting/ML service rather than a general time-series store, and DocumentDB (D) is a document database with MongoDB compatibility — none are time-series databases for event analytics.

questions.question: Which option is a shared control between AWS and the customer, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
questions.explanation: Configuration management is a shared responsibility in the AWS shared responsibility model: the customer configures their own resources and guest OS, while AWS configures and manages the cloud infrastructure and the managed services it operates. Physical and environmental controls (B) are exclusively AWS's responsibility; data integrity/authentication (C) and identity and access management (D) are customer responsibilities for resources and data in the cloud.

questions.question: A company often does not use all of its current Amazon EC2 capacity to run stateless workloads. The company wants to optimize its EC2 costs. Which EC2 instance type will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Stateless workloads that can tolerate interruption are ideal for Spot Instances, which offer up to a 90% discount compared with On-Demand in exchange for AWS reclaiming capacity when needed — the best way to optimize cost on capacity the company doesn't always use. Dedicated Instances (B) and Reserved Instances (C) both commit you to paying for capacity regardless of use, and On-Demand (D) is the full-price baseline with no discount.

questions.question: A company wants to store data in Amazon S3. The company rarely access the data, and the data can be regenerated if necessary. The company wants to store the data in the most cost-effective storage class. Which S3 storage class will meet this requirement?
options: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)
questions.explanation: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access stores objects in a single Availability Zone at the lowest storage cost among the frequent-access-avoiding classes, which is appropriate for data that is rarely accessed and — per the question — can be regenerated if lost, so the redundancy of multi-AZ classes isn't needed. S3 Standard (A) is for frequently accessed, hot data; S3 Intelligent-Tiering (B) automatically moves objects between tiers but charges a small monitoring fee and is aimed at unknown or changing access patterns; and S3 Standard-IA (C) replicates across multiple AZs, costing more than necessary for regenerable data.

questions.question: A company has migrated its workloads to AWS. The company wants to adopt AWS at scale and operate more efficiently and securely. Which AWS service or framework should the company use for operational support?
questions.explanation: AWS Managed Services (AMS) provides ongoing operational support for operating AWS at scale — managing patches, configuration, security compliance, and routine operations — so the company can adopt AWS more efficiently and securely without building a full operations team. AWS Support (A) answers support cases rather than operating your environment; AWS CAF (B) is a planning framework for cloud transformation journeys; and the Well-Architected Framework (D) is a set of review best practices, not an operational managed service.

questions.question: A company wants to provision and manage its AWS infrastructure by using the common programming languages Typescript, Python, Java, and .NET. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: The AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) lets you define cloud infrastructure programmatically in TypeScript, Python, Java, and .NET, synthesizing the code into CloudFormation templates for provisioning. CodeBuild (A) runs build jobs, CloudFormation (B) deploys templates but is itself a JSON/YAML template language rather than a general programming language interface, and the CLI (C) is a command-line tool rather than a typed programming-language SDK for infrastructure.

questions.question: Which Amazon EC2 pricing model provides the MOST cost savings for an always-up, right-sized database server running for a project that will last 1 year?
questions.explanation: A Standard Reserved Instance with a 1-year term gives the largest savings for an always-on, steady-state database server over a 1-year project (up to ~72% off On-Demand), because the commitment exactly matches the project duration with no exchange flexibility to pay for. On-Demand (A) has no discount at all; Convertible RIs (B) offer a smaller discount in exchange for instance-family convertibility that isn't needed here; and Spot Instances (C) can be interrupted, which is inappropriate for an always-up database server.

questions.question: A company has a physical tape library to store data backups. The tape library is running out of space. The company needs to extend the tape library's capacity to the AWS Cloud. Which AWS service should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway is a hybrid cloud storage service that lets you extend on-premises storage into AWS; its Tape Gateway creates virtual tape libraries backed by S3/Archive, directly extending an existing physical tape backup workflow into the cloud without replacing it. EFS (A) is a managed NFS file system, EBS (B) is network-attached block storage for EC2, and S3 (C) is an object store — none of them integrate with an existing physical tape library as a drop-in capacity extension.

questions.question: A company is using the AWS Free Tier for several AWS services for an application. What will happen if the Free Tier usage period expires or if the application use exceeds the Free Tier usage limits?
options: The company will be charged the standard pay-as-you-go service rates for the usage that exceeds the Free Tier usage.
AWS Support will contact the company to set up standard service charges.
The company will be charged for the services it consumed during the Free Tier period, plus additional charges for service consumption after the Free Tier period.
The company's AWS account will be frozen and can be restarted after a payment plan is established.
questions.explanation: AWS Free Tier is a usage allowance that lapses after its period (or once limits are exceeded), after which any usage beyond it is billed at standard pay-as-you-go rates — there is no retroactive charge for usage inside the Free Tier window. AWS does not contact you first to set up charges (B), it does not charge for properly Free-Tier-consumed usage retroactively (C), and accounts are not frozen for exceeding free tier (D); overage simply accrues as normal charges.

questions.question: A company wants to monitor its workload performance. The company wants to ensure that the cloud services are delivered at a level that meets its business needs. Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) perspective will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: The Operations perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) focuses on how well workloads are delivered and supported in the cloud — monitoring, performance, availability, and aligning cloud service delivery with business needs — matching the requirement. Business (A) focuses on strategy and ROI, Governance (B) on portfolio and compliance management, and Platform (C) on the cloud infrastructure and workload architecture itself.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate its applications to the AWS Cloud. The company plans to identify and prioritize any business transformation opportunities and evaluate its AWS Cloud readiness. Which AWS service or tool should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) is specifically designed to help organizations identify and prioritize business transformation opportunities and assess their readiness for cloud adoption, using perspectives that organize stakeholders across the journey. AWS Managed Services (B) operates your environment after migration rather than planning it; the Well-Architected Framework (C) reviews workload design quality; and Migration Hub (D) tracks individual migration projects rather than assessing overall business transformation readiness.

questions.question: A company need an AWS service that provides a clear baseline of what the company runs in its on-premises data centers. The company needs the projected cost to run its on-premises workloads in the AWS Cloud. What AWS service or tool will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Migration Evaluator is the AWS service that builds a data-driven inventory (baseline) of your on-premises estate and produces projected AWS cost estimates for running those workloads in the cloud, matching both requirements — baseline plus projected cost. Compute Optimizer (A) recommends instance sizing for existing AWS resources, Cost Explorer (B) visualizes historical and current AWS spend rather than on-premises baselines, and the SSM Agent (C) is a local agent for managing EC2 instances, not a migration assessment tool.

questions.question: A company acquired another corporation. The company now has two AWS accounts. Which AWS service or tool can the company use to consolidate the billing for these two accounts?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations is designed to centrally manage multiple AWS accounts and consolidate their billing into a single paying account, giving the company one combined bill for both acquired accounts. Systems Manager (A) operates resources, License Manager (C) tracks software licenses, and Cost Explorer (D) analyzes cost data but cannot consolidate billing across accounts — only Organizations produces a consolidated bill.

questions.question: A company wants to set up its workloads to perform their intended functions and recover quickly from failure. Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework aligns with these goals?
questions.explanation: The Reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework is about workloads performing their intended function correctly and consistently and recovering quickly from failure (through redundancy, scalability, and disaster recovery testing). Performance efficiency (A) is about using resources efficiently as demand changes, Sustainability (B) focuses on minimizing environmental footprint, and Security (D) focuses on protecting data and assets — none center on performing intended functions and recovering quickly from failure.

questions.question: Which of the following is a managed AWS service that is used specifically for extract, transform, and load (ETL) data?
questions.explanation: AWS Glue is a serverless data integration service purpose-built for extract, transform, and load (ETL) jobs, with built-in job scheduling and a data catalog. Amazon Athena (A) is an interactive SQL query engine for data already in S3, Amazon S3 (C) is object storage rather than a processing engine, and AWS Snowball Edge (D) is an edge device for offline data transfer and local compute.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate petabytes of data from its on-premises data center to AWS. The company does not want to use an internet connection to perform the migration. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Snowmobile is an exabyte-scale offline transfer service (a truck that comes on premises) designed for petabyte-scale migrations with no network use. AWS DataSync (A) and AWS Direct Connect (D) both require a network connection, and Amazon Connect (B) is a contact-center service unrelated to data migration.

questions.question: A company wants to receive alerts to monitor its overall operating costs for its AWS public cloud infrastructure. Which AWS offering will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets lets you set cost and usage budgets and sends alerts when actual or forecasted spend exceeds thresholds, which is exactly cost monitoring. Amazon EventBridge (A) routes application events, Compute Savings Plans (B) commit spend for discounts rather than monitoring it, and Migration Evaluator (D) estimates migration costs, it does not alert on ongoing spend.

questions.question: How does the AWS Enterprise Support Concierge team help users?
options: Answering questions regarding technical support cases
questions.explanation: Per AWS documentation, the Enterprise Support Concierge team specializes in billing and account inquiries, helping with invoices, cost optimization guidance, and account issues. Application development (A) and architecture guidance (B) come from TAMs and Solutions Architects, while technical support cases (D) are handled by support engineers.

questions.question: A company wants to run a simulation for 3 years without interruptions. Which Amazon EC2 instance purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: Standard Reserved Instances with a 3-year term give the steepest discount for a steady, uninterrupted multi-year workload. Spot Instances (A) can be interrupted with two minutes notice, Dedicated Hosts (C) add physical-server control at a premium rather than savings, and On-Demand (D) has no commitment discount.

questions.question: Which AWS service or resource can provide discounts on some AWS service costs in exchange for a spending commitment?
questions.explanation: Savings Plans exchange a one- or three-year hourly spend commitment for discounted rates on compute usage such as EC2, Fargate, and Lambda. Amazon Detective (A) is a security investigation service, the Pricing Calculator (B) only estimates costs, and Basic Support (D) is a support plan with no discount mechanism.

questions.question: Which of the following are pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The six AWS Well-Architected Framework pillars are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability, so performance efficiency (B) and cost optimization (C) are correct. High availability (A) is a reliability outcome rather than a named pillar, and going global in minutes (D) and continuous development (E) are cloud benefits and practices, not pillars.

questions.question: A company wants to use Amazon EC2 instances to provide a static website to users all over the world. The company needs to minimize latency for the users. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Use EC2 instances in multiple edge locations.
Use EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone but in different AWS Regions.
Use Amazon CloudFront with the EC2 instances configured as the source.
Use EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone but in different AWS accounts.
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a global content delivery network that caches the EC2-hosted static content at edge locations near users, minimizing latency worldwide. EC2 instances cannot run in edge locations (A), and simply spreading instances across AZs, Regions, or accounts (B, D) without a CDN still serves every request from a distant origin.

questions.question: A team of researchers is going to collect data at remote locations around the world. Many locations do not have internet connectivity. The team needs to capture the data in the field, and transfer it to the AWS Cloud later. Which AWS service will support these requirements?
questions.explanation: The AWS Snow Family (Snowcone, Snowball) provides rugged edge devices that capture and store data offline in the field for later transfer to AWS. AWS Outposts (A) extends AWS infrastructure on premises permanently, Transfer Family (B) needs a network connection for file transfers, and Migration Hub (D) only tracks migrations.

questions.question: Which of the following are benefits that a company receives when it moves an on-premises production workload to AWS? (Choose two.)
options: AWS trains the company's staff on the use of all the AWS services.
AWS manages all security in the cloud.
AWS offers free support from technical account managers (TAMs).
questions.explanation: Moving to AWS gives high availability through multiple AZs and Regions (D) and economies of scale from shared massive infrastructure (E). AWS does not train all customer staff (A), security remains shared rather than fully AWS-managed (B), and TAM access (C) requires a paid Business or Enterprise support plan.

questions.question: A company has decided to adopt Amazon EC2 infrastructure and wants to scale various stateless services for short-term usage. Which EC2 pricing model is MOST cost-efficient to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances offer spare EC2 capacity at up to 90% off and suit short-lived, stateless, interrupt-tolerant workloads that can scale in and out. On-Demand (B) costs more with no interruption risk, Reserved Instances (C) need a one- or three-year commitment unsuited to short-term use, and Dedicated Hosts (D) reserve whole physical servers at a premium.

questions.question: Which of the following are benefits of AWS Trusted Advisor? (Choose two.)
options: Access to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS)
Hourly refresh of the service limit checks
AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) approval management
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor checks cover five categories, including cost optimization recommendations such as idle resources (B) and security checks such as open security groups and MFA on root (D). It does not grant SQS access (A), hourly refresh applies only to some checks with higher support plans (C), and it has nothing to do with IAM approval workflows (E).

questions.question: A company wants to save costs by archiving data that is no longer frequently accessed by end users. Which Amazon S3 feature will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: S3 Lifecycle rules automatically transition objects to cheaper archival classes (Standard-IA, Glacier) or expire them based on age, which is the native cost-saving mechanism for infrequently accessed data. Versioning (A) keeps multiple copies and raises cost, Object Lock (C) enforces immutability for compliance, and Inventory (D) only reports on objects.

questions.question: Which cloud computing advantage is a company applying when it uses AWS Regions to increase application availability to users in different countries?
questions.explanation: Global reach is the cloud advantage of deploying in AWS Regions around the world so users everywhere get low-latency, available access. Pay-as-you-go (A), capacity forecasting (B), and economies of scale (C) are separate advantages about pricing and scale, not geographic presence.

questions.question: A company wants an AWS service to collect and process 10 TB of data locally and transfer the data to AWS. The company has intermittent connectivity. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Snowball Edge provides rugged devices with local storage and compute that collect and process data offline, then ship back to AWS, tolerating intermittent connectivity. AWS DMS (A) migrates databases over a network, DataSync (B) needs connectivity, and AWS Backup (C) backs up AWS resources rather than collecting on-premises data offline.

questions.question: Which of the following is an AWS Well-Architected Framework design principle for operational excellence in the AWS Cloud?
options: Implement a strong foundation of identity and access management
Stop spending money on hardware infrastructure for data center operations.
questions.explanation: The operational excellence pillar's design principles include making frequent, small, reversible changes so failures are limited and recovery is fast. Going global in minutes (A) is a cloud benefit, identity foundations (C) belong to the security pillar, and stopping data-center spend (D) is a cost benefit.

questions.question: What is a benefit of using AWS serverless computing?
options: Application deployment and management are not required.
Application security will be fully managed by AWS.
Monitoring and logging are not needed.
Management of infrastructure is offloaded to AWS.
questions.explanation: With serverless, AWS provisions, patches, and scales the underlying infrastructure so developers focus on code. Applications still must be deployed and managed (A), security follows the shared responsibility model (B), and monitoring and logging remain the customer's job (C).

questions.question: A developer wants AWS users to access AWS services by using temporary security credentials. Which AWS service or feature should the developer use to provide these credentials?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
questions.explanation: AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) issues short-lived temporary credentials for federated users, roles, and cross-account access. IAM policies (A) and user groups (B) define permissions for long-lived identities, and IAM Identity Center (D) manages workforce SSO access rather than issuing temporary API credentials directly.

questions.question: A global company wants to use a managed security service for protection from SQL injection attacks. The service also must provide detailed logging information about access to the company's ecommerce applications. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF is a managed web application firewall with SQL-injection match rules and detailed access logging for web applications. Network Firewall (A) filters L3/L4 network traffic, RDS for SQL Server (B) is a database engine, and GuardDuty (D) detects threats but does not block web exploits.

questions.question: A company is migrating its on-premises server to an Amazon EC2 instance. The server must stay active at all times for the next 12 months. Which EC2 pricing option is the MOST cost-effective for the company's workload?
questions.explanation: A steady always-on server for 12 months fits a 1-year Reserved Instance, which discounts the hourly rate far below On-Demand. On-Demand (A) has no commitment discount, Spot (C) can be interrupted, and Dedicated Hosts (B) add physical-server isolation at extra cost.

questions.question: Which of the following is the customer's responsibility under the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)
options: Maintain the configuration of infrastructure devices.
Maintain patching and updates within the hardware infrastructure.
Maintain the configuration of guest operating systems and applications.
questions.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS owns the physical infrastructure, hardware patching, and infrastructure-device configuration (A, B, E), while the customer configures guest operating systems and applications (C) and decides on data protection such as encryption (D).

questions.question: A company wants to verify if multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled for all users within its AWS accounts. Which AWS service or resource will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: An IAM credential report lists every IAM user with MFA status, password age, and access-key age, making it the direct tool for auditing MFA enrollment. The Cost and Usage Report (A) tracks billing, Artifact (C) hosts compliance documents, and CloudFront reports (D) cover CDN traffic.

questions.question: A company uses AWS security services and tools. The company needs a service to help manage the security alerts and must organize the alerts into a single dashboard. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Security Hub aggregates findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and other services into one centralized dashboard with standardized severity. GuardDuty (A), Inspector (B), and Macie (C) each generate findings in their own domain but do not consolidate alerts across services.

questions.question: A company wants to run its workloads in the AWS Cloud effectively, reduce management overhead, and improve processes. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar represents these requirements?
questions.explanation: The operational excellence pillar covers running workloads effectively day to day, with less management overhead and better processes. Reliability (A) is about withstanding failure, performance efficiency (C) about using resources efficiently, and cost optimization (D) about avoiding unnecessary spend.

questions.question: A company uses Amazon S3 to store records that can contain personally identifiable information (PII). The company wants a solution that can monitor all S3 buckets for PII and immediately alert staff about vulnerabilities. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning to discover and classify PII across S3 buckets and raises findings when sensitive data is exposed. GuardDuty (A) detects threats, Detective (B) investigates them, and Shield (D) protects against DDoS, none of which scan bucket contents for PII.

questions.question: Which AWS service allows users to download security and compliance reports about the AWS infrastructure on demand?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for downloading AWS security and compliance reports such as SOC, PCI, and ISO certifications on demand. GuardDuty (A) and Security Hub (B) manage threat findings, and Shield (D) provides DDoS protection.

questions.question: An external auditor has requested that a company provide a list of all its IAM users, including the status of users' credentials and access keys. What is the SIMPLEST way to provide this information?
options: Create an IAM user account for the auditor, granting the auditor administrator permissions.
Take a screenshot of each user's page in the AWS Management Console, then provide the screenshots to the auditor.
Download the IAM credential report, then provide the report to the auditor.
Download the AWS Trusted Advisor report, then provide the report to the auditor.
questions.explanation: The IAM credential report is a downloadable CSV covering all users with credential and key status, the simplest evidence for an auditor. Creating an admin auditor account (A) is excessive, screenshots (B) do not scale, and Trusted Advisor (D) samples only a subset of checks.

questions.question: Which task can a company perform by using security groups in the AWS Cloud?
options: Allow access to an Amazon EC2 instance through only a specific port.
Deny access to malicious IP addresses at a subnet level.
Protect data that is cached by Amazon CloudFront.
Apply a stateless firewall to an Amazon EC2 instance.
questions.explanation: Security groups are stateful instance-level firewalls whose inbound rules open specific ports (for example 443) to chosen sources. Denying subnet-level IPs is done with NACLs (B), CloudFront caching protection with WAF or signed URLs (C), and security groups cannot be stateless (D).

questions.question: A company plans to run a compute-intensive workload that uses graphics processing units (GPUs). Which Amazon EC2 instance type should the company use?
questions.explanation: Accelerated computing instances (P, G, Inf families) provide GPUs and other hardware accelerators for graphics, ML, and HPC. Compute optimized (B) targets CPU-bound work, storage optimized (C) targets high I/O, and general purpose (D) balances all three without accelerators.

questions.question: Which of the following are features of network ACLs as they are used in the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: They evaluate all rules before allowing traffic.
They process rules in order, starting with the lowest numbered rule, when deciding whether to allow traffic.
They operate at the instance level.
questions.explanation: Network ACLs are stateless subnet firewalls that evaluate numbered rules in ascending order and apply the first match, returning traffic needs an explicit outbound rule. They are not stateful (B), they stop at the first match rather than evaluating all rules (C), and they attach to subnets, not instances (E).

questions.question: Which capabilities are in the platform perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The CAF platform perspective covers cloud infrastructure delivery, including data engineering for analytics platforms (B) and CI/CD practices (C). Performance management (A) and change management (E) sit in the operations perspective, while infrastructure protection (D) is a security perspective capability.

questions.question: According to the AWS shared responsibility model, the customer is responsible for applying the latest security updates and patches for which of the following?
questions.explanation: EC2 gives the customer full control of the guest OS, so OS patching is the customer's job. DynamoDB (A), RDS (C), and S3 (D) are managed services where AWS patches the underlying platform.

questions.question: Which Amazon S3 storage class is MOST cost-effective for unknown access patterns?
options: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)
questions.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors access patterns and moves objects between frequent and infrequent tiers automatically, making it cheapest when patterns are unknown. Standard (A) charges full price always, while Standard-IA (B) and One Zone-IA (C) add retrieval fees that penalize unexpectedly frequent access.

questions.question: Which options are AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) security perspective capabilities? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The CAF security perspective includes incident response processes (C) and infrastructure protection controls (D). Observability (A) is a platform capability, incident and problem management (B) belongs to operations, and availability and continuity (E) is a reliability concern.

questions.question: A company has a managed IAM policy that does not grant the necessary permissions for users to accomplish required tasks. How can this be resolved?
options: Use a third-party web application firewall (WAF) managed rule from the AWS Marketplace.
Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to create a customer-managed key.
questions.explanation: AWS-managed policies cannot be edited, so when one lacks permissions you author a customer-managed (custom) IAM policy granting exactly the needed actions. Shield Advanced (A) is DDoS protection, Marketplace WAF rules (C) filter web traffic, and KMS keys (D) handle encryption.

questions.question: Who is responsible for managing IAM user access and secret keys according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: IAM access and secret keys are static, so there is no need to rotate them.
The customer is responsible for rotating keys.
AWS will rotate the keys whenever required.
The AWS Support team will rotate keys when requested by the customer.
questions.explanation: IAM access keys are long-lived credentials owned by the customer, and AWS documentation makes rotation the customer's duty. There is no automatic AWS rotation (C), keys are not static-forever (A), and Support does not rotate them for you (D).

questions.question: A company needs to run a pre-installed third-party firewall on an Amazon EC2 instance. Which AWS service or feature can provide this solution?
questions.explanation: AWS Marketplace sells pre-built third-party AMIs and software, including firewall appliances ready to launch on EC2. NACLs (A) and security groups (B) are packet filters rather than full firewall products, and Trusted Advisor (D) only recommends best practices.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud benefit gives a company the ability to quickly deploy cloud resources to access compute, storage, and database infrastructures in a matter of minutes?
questions.explanation: Agility is the ability to provision compute, storage, and databases in minutes and experiment quickly. Elasticity (A) scales with demand, cost savings (B) cut spend, and reliability (D) withstands failure.

questions.question: Which of the following is entirely the responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Development of an IAM password policy
Patching of the guest operating system
questions.explanation: Physical and environmental controls for AWS data centers (power, cooling, physical access) are entirely AWS's responsibility. IAM policies (B) and security training (A) are customer duties, and guest OS patching (C) is the customer's job on EC2.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of the AWS account root user?
options: The root user is the only user that can be configured with multi-factor authentication (MFA).
The root user is the only user that can access the AWS Management Console.
The root user is the first sign-in identity that is available when an AWS account is created.
The root user has a password that cannot be changed.
questions.explanation: The root user is the initial sign-in identity created with the AWS account, with unrestricted access to all resources. It is not the only identity that can use MFA (A) or the console (B), and its password can and should be changed and protected with MFA (D).

questions.question: An Amazon EC2 instance previously used for development is inaccessible and no longer appears in the AWS Management Console. Which AWS service should be used to determine what action made this EC2 instance inaccessible?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records API calls that create, modify, or terminate resources, so its event history shows who terminated the EC2 instance and when. CloudWatch Logs (A) holds application logs, Security Hub (B) aggregates findings, and Inspector (C) scans for vulnerabilities, none of which audit control-plane actions.

questions.question: A company's application developers need to quickly provision and manage AWS services by using scripts. Which AWS offering should the developers use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: The AWS CLI lets developers script provisioning and management of AWS services from the shell or CI jobs. CodeBuild (B) runs builds, the CAF (C) is an adoption guidance framework, and Session Manager (D) opens shell sessions to instances, none of which are general scripting CLIs.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate unstructured data to AWS. The data needs to be securely moved with inflight encryption and end-to-end data validation. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS DataSync moves unstructured file and object data with TLS in-flight encryption, integrity validation, and scheduling. Application Migration Service (A) rehosts servers, EFS (B) is a destination file system rather than a migration engine, and Migration Hub (D) only tracks migrations.

questions.question: A development team wants to deploy multiple test environments for an application in a fast, repeatable manner. Which AWS service should the team use?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation templates define whole environments as code, so test stacks can be launched and torn down repeatedly and identically. EC2 alone (A) needs manual setup, QuickSight (C) is BI dashboards, and ECS (D) orchestrates containers but does not template the full environment.

questions.question: A company wants to quickly implement a continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS CodeStar provisions a complete CI/CD toolchain (CodeCommit, CodeBuild, CodePipeline, CodeDeploy) from project templates for fast setup. Config (A) audits configuration, Cognito (B) handles auth, and DataSync (C) moves data.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud deployment model uses AWS Outposts as part of the application deployment infrastructure?
questions.explanation: AWS Outposts places AWS-designed racks on premises that extend the same APIs, which is the hybrid model combining cloud and on-premises infrastructure. Pure on-premises (A) uses no AWS cloud, serverless (B) abstracts servers entirely, and cloud-native (C) runs fully in the cloud.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fully managed graph database service on AWS?
questions.explanation: Amazon Neptune is the fully managed graph database for relationship-heavy data. Aurora (A) is relational, FSx (B) is file storage, and DynamoDB (C) is key-value/document.

questions.question: Which AWS service could an administrator use to provide desktop environments for several employees?
questions.explanation: Amazon WorkSpaces delivers managed virtual Windows or Linux desktops to users. Organizations (A) manages accounts, Fargate (B) runs containers, and WAF (C) filters web traffic.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature gives users the ability to capture information about network traffic in a VPC?
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs record source, destination, and port metadata for network traffic in a VPC. Inspector (B) scans workloads for vulnerabilities, route tables (C) direct traffic, and CloudTrail (D) logs API calls rather than packets.

questions.question: Which type of AWS storage is ephemeral and is deleted when an Amazon EC2 instance is stopped or terminated?
questions.explanation: EC2 instance store volumes are physically attached to the host and their data is lost on stop or termination, making them ephemeral. EBS (A) persists independently, EFS (C) is a persistent shared file system, and S3 (D) is durable object storage.

questions.question: A company wants to provide access to Windows file shares in AWS from its on-premises workloads. The company does not want to provision any additional infrastructure or applications in its data center. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon FSx File Gateway presents cloud file shares over SMB/NFS to on-premises users without installing new on-premises infrastructure. DataSync (B) migrates data rather than serving live shares, S3 (C) is object storage without native SMB, and the Snow Family (D) ships offline data.

questions.question: A company wants durable storage for static content and infinitely scalable data storage infrastructure at the lowest cost. Which AWS service should the company choose?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 offers 11 nines of durability, unlimited scale, and the lowest per-GB cost for static content. EBS (A) attaches to single instances at higher cost, Storage Gateway (C) bridges on-premises to cloud, and EFS (D) is a higher-cost shared file system.

questions.question: An ecommerce company wants to use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to add and remove EC2 instances based on CPU utilization. Which AWS service or feature can initiate an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling action to achieve this goal?
questions.explanation: A CloudWatch alarm on CPU utilization triggers Auto Scaling step and target-tracking policies to add or remove instances. SQS (A) queues messages, SNS (B) sends notifications, and Systems Manager (C) manages instances, none of which evaluate metrics and fire scaling actions.

questions.question: A company wants to transform its workforce by attracting and developing a digitally fluent high-performance workforce. The company wants to attract a diverse and inclusive workforce with appropriate mix of technical and non-technical skills. Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) perspective will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: The CAF people perspective covers workforce transformation, culture, training, and diversity. Business (A) covers business value, platform (C) covers infrastructure delivery, and operations (D) covers running workloads.

questions.question: A company wants to move its on-premises databases to managed cloud database services by using a simplified migration process. Which AWS service or tool can help the company meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replicates on-premises databases to managed services such as RDS and Aurora with minimal downtime. Storage Gateway (A) bridges storage, Application Migration Service (B) rehosts servers, and DataSync (C) moves files rather than databases.

questions.question: A company needs a fully managed file server that natively supports Microsoft workloads and file systems. The file server must also support the SMB protocol. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
options: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
questions.explanation: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a managed Windows file server with native SMB and Active Directory support. EFS (A) serves NFS for Linux, FSx for Lustre (B) targets HPC scratch storage, and EBS (C) is block storage.

questions.question: A company has been storing monthly reports in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company exports the report data into comma-separated values (.csv) files. A developer wants to write a simple query that can read all of these files and generate a summary report. Which AWS service or feature should the developer use to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena runs serverless SQL directly against CSV files in S3 with no infrastructure to manage. S3 Select (A) queries within a single object, Redshift (C) needs a provisioned warehouse, and EC2 (D) needs servers and query engines.

questions.question: Which AWS feature provides a no-cost platform for AWS users to join community groups, ask questions, find answers, and read community-generated articles about best practices?
questions.explanation: AWS re:Post is the free community Q&A platform for asking questions and sharing best-practice articles. Knowledge Center (A) hosts official FAQs, IQ (C) is paid expert help, and Enterprise Support (D) is a paid support plan.

questions.question: A company needs to search for text in documents that are stored in Amazon S3. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Kendra is a managed intelligent search service that indexes S3 documents for natural-language text search. Rekognition (B) analyzes images and video, Polly (C) converts text to speech, and Lex (D) builds chatbots.

questions.question: Which AWS services make use of global edge locations? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront serves cached content from global edge locations, and AWS Global Accelerator routes traffic through edge locations to the nearest healthy endpoint. Fargate (A) runs containers in Regions, Wavelength (D) embeds compute in telecom networks, and VPC (E) is a regional network.

questions.question: A user needs a relational database but does not have the resources to manage the hardware, resiliency, and replication. Which AWS service option meets the user's requirements?
options: Run MySQL on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS for MySQL is a managed relational database where AWS handles hardware, patching, failover, and replication. Running MySQL on ECS (A) or EC2 (B) leaves management to you, and ElastiCache for Redis (D) is an in-memory cache rather than a relational database.

questions.question: A company needs to deploy applications in the AWS Cloud as quickly as possible. The company also needs to minimize the complexity that is related to the management of AWS resources. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk provisions and manages the underlying EC2, load balancing, and scaling from uploaded code, minimizing resource-management complexity. Config (A) audits resources, EC2 (C) is raw infrastructure, and Personalize (D) builds recommendations.

questions.question: Which mechanism allows developers to access AWS services from application code?
questions.explanation: AWS SDKs provide language-specific libraries for calling AWS service APIs from application code. The Management Console (B) is a browser UI, CodePipeline (C) automates releases, and Config (D) audits configuration.

questions.question: A company is migrating to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to understand and identify potential security misconfigurations or unexpected behaviors. The company wants to prioritize any protective controls it might need. Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) security perspective capability will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: The CAF security perspective's threat detection capability covers identifying misconfigurations and unexpected behavior to prioritize protections. Identity and access management (A) governs who can access what, platform engineering (C) is a platform capability, and availability management (D) covers continuity.

questions.question: A company wants to establish a private network connection between AWS and its corporate network. Which AWS service or feature will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes a private dedicated network link between on-premises and AWS, bypassing the public internet. Connect (A) is a contact center, Route 53 (B) is DNS, and VPC peering (D) connects two VPCs rather than on-premises.

questions.question: Which AWS services or features give users the ability to create a network connection between two VPCs? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: VPC peering (C) directly connects two VPCs, and Transit Gateway (E) hubs many VPCs together. VPC endpoints (A) reach AWS services privately, Route 53 (B) resolves DNS, and Direct Connect (D) links on-premises to AWS.

questions.question: Which AWS service converts text to lifelike voices?
questions.explanation: Amazon Polly is a managed text-to-speech service producing lifelike voices. Transcribe (A) converts speech to text, Rekognition (B) analyzes images and video, and Textract (D) extracts text from documents.

questions.question: A company wants to use application stacks to run a workload in the AWS Cloud. The company wants to use pre-configured instances. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Lightsail offers pre-configured VPS bundles with OS, storage, and networking for simple stacks. Athena (B) queries S3 with SQL, Outposts (C) extends AWS on premises, and EC2 (D) needs manual configuration.

questions.question: Which AWS services are supported by Savings Plans? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Savings Plans discount EC2 compute usage (A) and SageMaker ML usage (C) under hourly commitments. RDS (B), Redshift (D), and DynamoDB (E) use Reserved Instances or their own discount models rather than Savings Plans.

questions.question: Which AWS service or tool can provide rightsizing recommendations for Amazon EC2 resources at no additional cost?
questions.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer's rightsizing recommendations analyze CloudWatch utilization to suggest smaller EC2 types at no extra charge. The Well-Architected Tool (A) reviews best practices, CloudWatch (B) only supplies raw metrics, and S3 analytics (D) optimizes storage classes.

questions.question: A company operates a petabyte-scale data warehouse to analyze its data. The company wants a solution that will not require manual hardware and software management. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift is a managed petabyte-scale data warehouse with no hardware or software to manage. DocumentDB (A) is a document database, Neptune (C) is a graph database, and ElastiCache (D) is an in-memory cache.

questions.question: A library wants to automate the classification of electronic books based on the contents of the books. Which AWS service should the library use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend uses NLP to classify documents by topic, sentiment, and entities. Redshift (A) warehouses structured data, CloudSearch (B) indexes text for search without classifying it, and Aurora (D) is a relational database.

questions.question: Which task is a responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
questions.explanation: Protecting data-center networks, power, and physical access is entirely AWS's responsibility. Encrypting application data (A), authenticating users (B), and configuring firewalls (D) are customer duties under shared responsibility.

questions.question: Which options are AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) cloud transformation journey recommendations? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The CAF transformation journey starts with the Envision phase (A) to define vision and the Align phase (B) to align stakeholders before launching. Assess, mobilize, migrate, and modernize (C, D, E) describe migration-plan activities rather than the named journey phases.

questions.question: A company wants to generate a list of IAM users. The company also wants to view the status of various credentials that are associated with the users, such as password, access keys, and multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices. Which AWS service or feature will meet these requirements?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer
questions.explanation: The IAM credential report lists all users with password, access-key, and MFA-device status in one CSV. Identity Center (B) manages SSO access, Access Analyzer (C) finds over-permissive policies, and the Cost and Usage Report (D) tracks billing.

questions.question: A company is designing its AWS workloads so that components can be updated regularly and so that changes can be made in small, reversible increments. Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework does this design support?
questions.explanation: Regular small reversible updates are the operational excellence pillar's change-management principle. Security (A) protects data, performance efficiency (B) uses resources efficiently, and reliability (D) withstands failure.

questions.question: A company wants to track tags, buckets, and prefixes for its Amazon S3 objects. Which S3 feature will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: S3 Inventory generates scheduled CSV or Parquet reports listing objects with tags, buckets, prefixes, and encryption status. Lifecycle (B) transitions objects, Versioning (C) keeps prior versions, and ACLs (D) grant access.

questions.question: A company wants to allow users to authenticate and authorize multiple AWS accounts by using a single set of credentials. Which AWS service or resource will meet this requirement?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
questions.explanation: IAM Identity Center provides workforce SSO so one set of credentials accesses multiple AWS accounts. Organizations (A) manages accounts and policies, an IAM user (B) exists in one account, and Control Tower (D) provisions landing zones.

questions.question: A company created an Amazon EC2 instance. The company wants to control the incoming and outgoing network traffic at the instance level. Which AWS resource or service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Security groups are stateful virtual firewalls attached to instances that control inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level. Shield (A) mitigates DDoS, Network Access Analyzer (C) audits paths, and VPC endpoints (D) reach services privately.

questions.question: A company wants to use the AWS Cloud to deploy an application globally. Which architecture deployment model should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: A multi-Region architecture deploys applications in two or more AWS Regions for global availability and disaster recovery. Single-Region (B) and single-AZ (D) concentrate risk, and multi-AZ (C) protects within one Region only.

questions.question: A company wants a web application to interact with various AWS services. Which AWS service or resource will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: This question's intended answer (Management Console) is a browser-based UI for interacting with services, though the wording overlaps with programmatic tools. CloudShell (A) is a shell environment, Marketplace (B) sells software, and the CLI (D) is command-line rather than web interaction.

questions.question: A company is migrating its applications from on-premises to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to ensure that the applications are assigned only the minimum permissions that are needed to perform all operations. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: IAM policies enforce least privilege by granting only the actions each application needs on specific resources. CloudWatch (B) monitors metrics, Macie (C) finds PII, and GuardDuty (D) detects threats, none of which assign permissions.

questions.question: Which options are AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) governance perspective capabilities? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The CAF governance perspective covers cloud financial management or FinOps (B) and application portfolio management (C). Identity management (A) is a security capability, while innovation and product management (D, E) belong to the business perspective.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a single location to track the progress of application migrations?
questions.explanation: AWS Migration Hub centralizes migration status across Discovery, Application Migration Service, DMS, and partner tools in one dashboard. Discovery Service (A) inventories servers, Application Migration Service (B) rehosts them, and Service Catalog (C) publishes approved products.

questions.question: A company launched an Amazon EC2 instance with the latest Amazon Linux 2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI). Which actions can a system administrator take to connect to the EC2 instance? (Choose two.)
options: Use a Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) connection.
Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager.
questions.explanation: EC2 Instance Connect (A) opens browser-based SSH to Linux instances and Session Manager (D) provides agent-based shell access without open ports. RDP (B) targets Windows rather than Linux, Batch (C) runs batch jobs, and Connect (E) is a contact center.

questions.question: Which architecture concept describes the ability to deploy resources on demand and release resources when they are no longer needed?
questions.explanation: Elasticity is provisioning resources on demand and releasing them when unneeded. High availability (A) keeps systems running, decoupled architecture (B) isolates components, and resilience (C) recovers from failure.

questions.question: Which task requires a user to sign in as the AWS account root user?
options: The deletion of an AWS account
The creation of an organization in AWS Organizations
The deletion of Amazon EC2 instances
questions.explanation: Closing or deleting an AWS account requires root-user credentials as a safety control. Deleting IAM users (A), creating organizations (C), and deleting EC2 instances (D) can all be done by authorized IAM principals.

questions.question: What does the Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class offer?
options: Payment flexibility by reserving storage capacity
Long-term retention of data by copying the data to an encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume
Automatic cost savings by moving objects between tiers based on access pattern changes
Secure, durable, and lowest cost storage for data archival
questions.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent, infrequent, archive, and deep-archive tiers as access patterns change, saving cost with no manual policy. It does not reserve capacity (A), copy to EBS (B), or serve as the cheapest archive tier itself (D).

questions.question: A company needs Amazon EC2 instances for a workload that can tolerate interruptions. Which EC2 instance purchasing option meets this requirement with the LARGEST discount compared to On-Demand prices?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances use spare capacity at up to 90% off On-Demand, the largest discount, in exchange for possible interruption. Reserved Instances (B, C) discount steady use, and Dedicated Hosts (D) cost more for physical isolation.

questions.question: A company is planning to migrate to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to identify measurable business outcomes that will explain the value of the company's decision to migrate. Which phase of the cloud transformation journey includes these activities?
questions.explanation: The CAF Envision phase defines the business vision and measurable outcomes for cloud migration. Align (B) secures stakeholder buy-in, while scale and launch describe migration execution stages rather than outcome definition.

questions.question: Which AWS service or component allows inbound traffic from the internet to access a VPC?
questions.explanation: An internet gateway attaches to a VPC and routes inbound and outbound traffic between VPC resources and the internet. A NAT gateway (B) allows outbound-only access, WAF (C) filters web requests, and VPC peering (D) connects VPCs privately.

questions.question: Which AWS service can companies use to create infrastructure from code?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation defines infrastructure as JSON or YAML templates deployed as stacks. EKS (A) runs Kubernetes, Outposts (B) extends AWS on premises, and CodePipeline (C) automates software releases.

questions.question: Which guideline is a well-architected design principle for building cloud applications?
options: Keep static data closer to compute resources.
Design for automated recovery from failure.
questions.explanation: Designing for automated recovery with health checks, failover, and self-healing is a core reliability principle. Keeping static data near compute (A) is vague, provisioning for peak (B) wastes capacity, and tight coupling (D) is an anti-pattern.

questions.question: A company needs to move 75 petabytes of data from its on-premises data centers to AWS. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: AWS Snowmobile moves up to 100 PB per truck offline, making it the cost-effective choice for 75 PB. Snowball Edge devices (A) each hold about 80 TB and would need hundreds of units, Direct Connect (C) transfers over the network slowly at this scale, and Storage Gateway (D) bridges ongoing storage rather than bulk migration.

questions.question: Which of the following are pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The six Well-Architected pillars include performance efficiency (B) and operational excellence (E). Resource scalability (A) and system elasticity (C) are design properties, and agile development (D) is a methodology, not pillars.

questions.question: A company needs to connect its on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The company needs a dedicated, low-latency connection with consistent network performance. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Direct Connect provisions a private dedicated line with consistent low latency. Global Accelerator (A) optimizes internet routing, CloudFront (B) caches content, and Managed VPN (D) traverses the public internet with variable performance.

questions.question: Which design principles should a company apply to AWS Cloud workloads to maximize sustainability and minimize environmental impact? (Choose two.)
options: Maximize utilization of Amazon EC2 instances.
Minimize utilization of Amazon EC2 instances.
Force frequent application reinstallations by users.
Reduce the need for users to reinstall applications.
questions.explanation: Sustainability guidance says maximize instance utilization to avoid idle capacity (A) and use managed services plus efficient software delivery so users rarely reinstall (E). Minimizing utilization (B), avoiding managed services (C), and forcing reinstalls (D) all waste resources.

questions.question: In which ways does the AWS Cloud offer lower total cost of ownership (TCO) of computing resources than on-premises data centers? (Choose two.)
options: AWS replaces upfront capital expenditures with pay-as-you-go costs.
AWS is designed for high availability, which eliminates user downtime.
AWS eliminates the need for on-premises IT staff.
AWS uses economies of scale to continually reduce prices.
AWS offers a single pricing model for Amazon EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: AWS lowers TCO by replacing capital expenditure with pay-as-you-go pricing (A) and passing economies of scale through as continual price cuts (D). High availability (B) improves uptime rather than TCO math, staff (C) is still needed in new roles, and EC2 has multiple pricing models (E).

questions.question: A company wants to deploy some of its resources in the AWS Cloud. To meet regulatory requirements, the data must remain local and on premises. There must be low latency between AWS and the company resources. Which AWS service or feature can be used to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Outposts keeps data local on premises while extending AWS APIs with low-latency access. Local Zones (A) extend Regions to cities, AZs (B) sit inside Regions, and Wavelength (D) embeds compute in telecom networks.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services are serverless? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: AWS Fargate runs containers without managing servers and AWS Lambda runs event-driven functions, both fully serverless. Outposts (A) is on-premises hardware, EC2 (B) needs server management, and EKS (C) still requires nodes or Fargate underneath.

questions.question: When a user wants to utilize their existing per-socket, per-core, or per-virtual machine software licenses for a Microsoft Windows server running on AWS, which Amazon EC2 instance type is required?
questions.explanation: Dedicated Hosts provide visible physical servers so existing per-socket, per-core, or per-VM licenses can be applied under BYOL rules. Spot (A) and Reserved (D) are pricing models, and Dedicated Instances (B) isolate hardware without exposing sockets for license mapping.

questions.question: A solutions architect needs to maintain a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances so that any impaired instances are replaced with new ones. Which AWS service should the solutions architect use?
questions.explanation: AWS Auto Scaling with EC2 Auto Scaling health checks replaces impaired instances automatically to maintain fleet capacity. ECS (A) orchestrates containers, GuardDuty (B) detects threats, and Shield (C) mitigates DDoS.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides on-premises applications with low-latency access to data that is stored in the AWS Cloud?
questions.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway caches cloud data locally on premises for low-latency file, volume, and tape access. CloudFront (A) delivers content outward to users, Backup (C) centralizes backups, and DataSync (D) migrates data rather than serving live low-latency access.

questions.question: What does Amazon CloudFront provide?
options: Automatic scaling for all resources to power an application from a single unified interface
Secure delivery of data, videos, applications, and APIs to users globally with low latency
Ability to directly manage traffic globally through a variety of routing types, including latency-based routing, geo DNS, geoproximity, and weighted round robin
Automatic distribution of incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as Amazon EC2 instances, containers, IP addresses, and AWS Lambda functions
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a CDN that securely delivers data, video, apps, and APIs worldwide at low latency from edge locations. Auto scaling (A) describes Auto Scaling, global traffic routing (C) describes Route 53, and traffic distribution (D) describes load balancers.

questions.question: Which AWS service supports the deployment and management of applications in the AWS Cloud?
questions.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk deploys and manages applications, provisioning EC2, load balancing, and scaling from uploaded code. CodeGuru (A) reviews code, Fargate (B) runs containers, and CodeCommit (C) hosts Git repositories.

questions.question: A company wants to integrate natural language processing (NLP) into business intelligence (BI) dashboards. The company wants to ask questions and receive answers with relevant visualizations. Which AWS service or tool will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon QuickSight Q adds natural-language querying to BI dashboards, answering questions with auto-generated visuals. Macie (A) finds PII, Rekognition (B) analyzes images, and Lex (D) builds chatbots.

questions.question: Which Amazon S3 feature or storage class uses the AWS backbone network and edge locations to reduce latencies from the end user to Amazon S3?
questions.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations over the AWS backbone to the bucket, cutting long-distance latency. Cross-Region Replication (A) copies objects, Event Notifications (C) trigger workflows, and Standard-IA (D) is a cheaper storage tier.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides the ability to host a NoSQL database in the AWS Cloud?
questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is the managed NoSQL key-value and document database. Aurora (A) and RDS (C) are relational, and Redshift (D) is a data warehouse.

questions.question: Which AWS service is a relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL?
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora is MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible with cloud-native performance and replication. Redshift (A) is a warehouse, DynamoDB (B) is NoSQL, and Neptune (D) is a graph database.

questions.question: Which architecture design principle describes the need to isolate failures between dependent components in the AWS Cloud?
options: Design for single points of failure.
questions.explanation: Loosely coupling isolates failures so one component's outage does not cascade, using queues and independent scaling. Monolithic design (A) concentrates failure, automation (B) speeds recovery but does not isolate, and single points of failure (C) are the anti-pattern.

questions.question: Which benefit of cloud computing gives a company the ability to deploy applications to users all over the world through a network of AWS Regions, Availability Zones, and edge locations?
questions.explanation: Global reach deploys apps to users worldwide via Regions, AZs, and edge locations. Economy of scale (A) cuts cost, agility (C) speeds provisioning, and high availability (D) keeps systems running.

questions.question: Which AWS service makes it easier to monitor and troubleshoot application logs and cloud resources?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch collects logs, metrics, and alarms for monitoring and troubleshooting resources. EC2 (A) provides compute, IAM (B) manages access, and CloudTrail (D) audits API calls rather than application logs.

questions.question: Which AWS service uses AWS Compute Optimizer to provide sizing recommendations based on workload metrics?
questions.explanation: Compute Optimizer analyzes CloudWatch workload metrics to recommend optimal EC2 instance types and sizes. RDS (B), Lightsail (C), and Step Functions (D) are separate services that do not surface Compute Optimizer EC2 sizing guidance.

questions.question: Which AWS service will help a company plan a migration to AWS by collecting the configuration, usage, and behavior data of on-premises data centers?
questions.explanation: AWS Application Discovery Service collects on-premises server configuration, usage, and behavior for migration planning. Resource Groups (A) organize resources, Service Catalog (C) publishes products, and Systems Manager (D) manages operations.

questions.question: Which AWS service uses a combination of publishers and subscribers?
questions.explanation: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub messaging service where publishers send to topics and subscribers receive via protocols like email and Lambda. Lambda (A) runs code, CloudWatch (B) monitors, and CloudFormation (C) provisions infrastructure.

questions.question: A company is in the early stages of planning a migration to AWS. The company wants to obtain the monthly predicted total AWS cost of ownership for future Amazon EC2 instances and associated storage. Which AWS service or tool should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: The AWS Pricing Calculator estimates future monthly total cost of ownership for planned EC2 and storage before migrating. Compute Optimizer (B) rightsizes existing workloads, Trusted Advisor (C) checks best practices, and Application Migration Service (D) rehosts servers.

questions.question: Which AWS service or tool will monitor AWS resources and applications in real time?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics, logs, and events in real time with alarms and dashboards. Trusted Advisor (A) gives periodic best-practice checks, CloudTrail (C) audits API history, and Cost Explorer (D) analyzes spend.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) capability belongs to the business perspective?
questions.explanation: Data science, including analytics and ML value realization, sits in the CAF business perspective. Program management (A) is governance, observability (C) is platform, and change management (D) is operations.

questions.question: Which AWS resource can help a company reduce its costs in exchange for a usage commitment when using Amazon EC2 instances?
questions.explanation: Compute Savings Plans commit hourly spend for one or three years in exchange for discounted EC2 rates. Auto Scaling (B) adjusts capacity, On-Demand (C) has no commitment discount, and instance store (D) is ephemeral disk.

questions.question: Which perspective in the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) includes a capability for well-designed data and analytics architecture?
questions.explanation: The CAF platform perspective designs data and analytics architectures alongside infrastructure delivery. Security (A) protects assets, governance (B) oversees programs, and operations (C) runs workloads.

questions.question: Which options are AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) people perspective capabilities? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The CAF people perspective covers organizational alignment on roles and responsibilities (A) and organization design for cloud operating models (C). Portfolio and risk management (B, D) are governance, and modern development (E) is platform.

questions.question: A company needs a bridge between technology and business to help evolve to a culture of continuous growth and learning. Which perspective in the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) serves as this bridge?
questions.explanation: The CAF people perspective bridges technology and business by driving culture, training, and organizational change. Governance (B) oversees portfolios, operations (C) runs workloads, and security (D) protects assets.

questions.question: Which option is a responsibility of AWS under the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Patch management for applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances
Patch management of the underlying infrastructure for managed services
questions.explanation: AWS patches the underlying infrastructure for managed services such as RDS and Lambda. Application data (A), EC2 application patching (B), and application IAM (D) remain customer duties.

questions.question: Which AWS service or resource can identify and provide reports on IAM resources in one AWS account that is shared with another AWS account?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer
questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer identifies resources such as roles and buckets shared cross-account and reports unintended external access. Credential reports (A) audit keys and MFA, Identity Center (B) manages SSO, and Cognito pools (D) authenticate app users.

questions.question: Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar focuses on structured and streamlined allocation of computing resources?
questions.explanation: Performance efficiency focuses on selecting the right resource types and sizes and allocating them efficiently. Reliability (A) withstands failure, operational excellence (B) runs workloads well, and sustainability (D) minimizes environmental impact.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) capabilities belong to the governance perspective? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The CAF governance perspective includes program and project management (A) and risk management (D). Product and portfolio management (B, C) are business capabilities, and event management (E) is operations.

questions.question: A company wants to use AWS Managed Services (AMS) for operational support and wants to understand the scope of AMS. Which AMS feature will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Managed Services operates customer landing zones and networks with patching, monitoring, and incident response. It does not develop customer applications (B), build DevSecOps pipelines (C), or monitor application-level logs (D).

questions.question: A company wants to migrate its on-premises NoSQL workload to Amazon DynamoDB. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS DMS replicates NoSQL and relational databases, including migrations into DynamoDB targets. Migration Hub (A) tracks status, Migration Evaluator (C) builds business cases, and Application Migration Service (D) rehosts servers.

questions.question: A company is in the process of finding correct Amazon EC2 instance types and sizes to meet its performance and capacity requirements. The company wants to find the lowest possible cost. Which option accurately characterizes the company's actions?
questions.explanation: Rightsizing matches instance types and sizes to actual performance needs at the lowest cost. Auto Scaling (A) adjusts count, storage tiering (B) moves data classes, and instance scheduling (D) stops instances on timetables.

questions.question: A company wants to manage sign-in security for workforce users. The company needs to create workforce users and centrally manage their access across all the company's AWS accounts and applications. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
questions.explanation: IAM Identity Center centrally creates workforce users and manages their SSO access across accounts and applications. Audit Manager (A) assesses controls, Cognito (B) authenticates app end users, and Security Hub (C) aggregates findings.

questions.question: A company wants a report that lists the status of multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices that all users in the company's AWS account use. Which AWS feature or service will meet this requirement?
options: Detailed Billing Reports - D AWS Cost Explorer reports
questions.explanation: IAM credential reports list every user with MFA-device, password, and access-key status in one CSV. Cost and Usage Reports (A) track billing, and Cost Explorer (D) analyzes spend.

questions.question: A company wants to use machine learning capabilities to analyze log data from its Amazon EC2 instances and efficiently conduct security investigations. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Detective uses machine learning to correlate log and event data into visual investigations of EC2-related security issues. Inspector (A) scans vulnerabilities, QuickSight (B) dashboards BI data, and GuardDuty (D) generates the underlying threat findings.

questions.question: A company is launching a mobile app in the AWS Cloud. The company wants the app's users to sign in through social media identity providers (IdPs). Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Cognito user pools federate sign-in with social providers such as Google, Facebook, and Amazon. Lambda (A) runs code, Secrets Manager (C) stores secrets, and CloudFront (D) delivers content.

questions.question: Which complimentary AWS service or tool creates data-driven business cases for cloud planning?
questions.explanation: Migration Evaluator builds data-driven business cases with projected cloud costs for planning. Billing Conductor (B) customizes bills, the Billing Console (C) views spend, and Forecast (D) predicts time-series metrics.

questions.question: Which cloud concept is demonstrated by using AWS Cost Explorer?
questions.explanation: Cost Explorer visualizes spend and usage to identify over-provisioned resources, demonstrating rightsizing analysis. Reliability (B), resilience (C), and modernization (D) are architectural outcomes rather than cost-analysis concepts.

questions.question: A company wants to deploy a non-containerized Java-based web application on AWS. The company wants to use a managed service to quickly deploy the application. The company wants the service to automatically provision capacity, load balance, scale, and monitor application health. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk deploys non-containerized web apps (Java, Python, .NET) while provisioning capacity, load balancing, scaling, and health monitoring automatically. ECS (A) and EKS (C) run containers, and Lambda (B) runs event functions.

questions.question: Which AWS service or tool gives users the ability to connect with AWS and deploy resources programmatically?
questions.explanation: AWS SDKs let developers connect programmatically and deploy resources from code. QuickSight (A) dashboards data, PrivateLink (B) reaches services privately, and Direct Connect (C) links networks.

questions.question: A company has deployed a web application to Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances have low usage. Which AWS service or feature should the company use to rightsize the EC2 instances?
