questions.explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes CloudWatch metrics of underused instances and recommends smaller types. Config (A) audits configuration, Cost Anomaly Detection (B) flags spend spikes, and Budgets (C) alerts on thresholds.

questions.question: A company wants to define a central data protection policy that works across AWS services for compute, storage, and database resources. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS Backup defines central backup policies across compute, storage, and database services with lifecycle management. Batch (A) runs batch jobs, Elastic Disaster Recovery (B) replicates servers for failover, and FSx (D) serves file storage.

questions.question: A company needs to categorize and track AWS usage cost based on business categories. Which AWS service or feature should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Cost allocation tags label resources by business categories such as cost center or project, letting bills and Cost Explorer group spend accordingly. Organizations (B) consolidates accounts, Security Hub (C) aggregates findings, and CUR (D) exports raw line items without the tagging taxonomy itself.

questions.question: Which AWS service can migrate data between AWS storage services?
questions.explanation: AWS DataSync migrates and syncs data between AWS storage services (S3, EFS, FSx) as well as on-premises to cloud. Direct Connect (B) is a network link, Lake Formation (C) governs data lakes, and S3 (D) is a storage destination rather than a migration engine.

questions.question: Which statements represent the cost-effectiveness of the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: Users can trade fixed expenses for variable expenses.
Users can deploy all over the world in minutes.
AWS offers increased speed and agility.
AWS is responsible for patching the infrastructure.
Users benefit from economies of scale.
questions.explanation: Trading fixed capex for variable pay-as-you-go spend (A) and benefiting from AWS economies of scale (E) are the two cost-effectiveness tenets. Global deployment (B) and speed (C) are agility benefits, and AWS patching (D) is a managed-service responsibility.

questions.question: A company wants to design its cloud architecture so that it can support development innovations, and continuously improve processes and procedures. This is an example of which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
questions.explanation: Supporting innovation with continual process improvement is the operational excellence pillar. Security (A) protects data, performance efficiency (B) uses resources well, and reliability (D) withstands failure.

questions.question: A company needs to consolidate the billing for multiple AWS accounts. The company needs to use one account to pay on behalf of all the other accounts. Which AWS service or tool should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations with consolidated billing rolls charges from member accounts into one payer account. Trusted Advisor (A) checks best practices, Budgets (C) alerts on spend, and Service Catalog (D) publishes approved products.

questions.question: A company is moving some of its on-premises IT services to the AWS Cloud. The finance department wants to see the entire bill so it can forecast spending limits. Which AWS service can the company use to set spending limits and receive notifications if those limits are exceeded?
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets sets cost or usage limits and notifies when actual or forecasted spend exceeds them. CUR (A) exports line items, consolidated billing (C) combines accounts, and Cost Explorer (D) visualizes past spend.

questions.question: Which AWS Support plans provide access to an AWS technical account manager (TAM)? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: A Technical Account Manager is included with Enterprise On-Ramp (D) and Enterprise Support (E). Basic (A) offers billing support only, Developer (B) business-hours guidance, and Business (C) full 24/7 support without a TAM.

questions.question: Where can users find examples of AWS Cloud solution designs?
questions.explanation: The AWS Architecture Center publishes reference architectures and solution diagrams. Marketplace (A) sells software, Service Catalog (B) distributes approved products, and Trusted Advisor (D) checks account best practices.

questions.question: Which task is the responsibility of a company that is using Amazon RDS?
options: Create IAM policies to control administrative access to the service.
Install the cables to connect the hardware for compute and storage.
Install and patch the RDS operating system.
questions.explanation: On RDS, AWS provisions hardware and patches the OS while the customer controls access via IAM policies. Provisioning infrastructure (A), cabling (C), and OS patching (D) are AWS duties.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage that the AWS Cloud provides to users?
options: Users eliminate the need to guess about infrastructure capacity requirements.
Users decrease their variable costs by maintaining sole ownership of IT hardware.
Users maintain control of underlying IT infrastructure hardware.
Users maintain control of operating systems for managed services.
questions.explanation: Elasticity removes capacity guessing by scaling resources up and down with demand. Owning hardware (B), controlling physical infrastructure (C), and managing OSes for managed services (D) are the on-premises burdens cloud removes.

questions.question: Which feature of Amazon RDS provides the ability to automatically create a primary database instance and to synchronously replicate data to an instance in another Availability Zone?
questions.explanation: RDS Multi-AZ deploys a primary with synchronous standby replication in another AZ for automatic failover. Read replicas (A) are asynchronous for scaling reads, blue/green (B) stages upgrades, and Reserved Instances (D) are a pricing model.

questions.question: A company needs to check for IAM access keys that have not been rotated recently. Which AWS service should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Trusted Advisor's security checks flag IAM keys that have not been rotated. WAF (A) filters web traffic, Shield (B) mitigates DDoS, and Cognito (C) authenticates app users.

questions.question: A company runs many Amazon EC2 instances in its VPC. The company wants to use a native AWS security resource to control network traffic between certain EC2 instances. Which AWS service or feature will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Security groups are stateful instance-level firewalls ideal for controlling traffic between EC2 instances. NACLs (A) filter at the subnet level, WAF (B) protects web apps, and GuardDuty (C) detects threats.

questions.question: Which of the following can be components of a VPC in the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Internet gateways (D) connect a VPC to the internet and subnets (E) partition its IP space, both native VPC components. API Gateway (A), S3 objects (B), and Storage Gateway (C) are services that integrate with VPCs but are not VPC components.

questions.question: A company is building a new application on AWS. The company needs the application to remain available if an individual application component fails. Which design principle should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Loose coupling with queues and independent services lets the application survive individual component failures. Disposable resources (A) aid experimentation, automation (B) speeds recovery, and rightsizing (C) optimizes cost.

questions.question: A company wants to use a managed service to identify and protect sensitive data that is stored in Amazon S3. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data such as PII in S3 and protects it with findings and alerts. Access Analyzer (A) audits sharing, GuardDuty (B) detects threats, and Inspector (C) scans vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature can a user configure to limit network access at the subnet level?
questions.explanation: Network ACLs are stateless subnet-level firewalls for limiting traffic in and out of subnets. Shield (A) mitigates DDoS, WAF (B) filters web requests, and security groups (D) filter at the instance level.

questions.question: Which AWS service can a company use to manage encryption keys in the cloud?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules for managing encryption keys in the cloud. License Manager (A) tracks licenses, ACM (B) provisions TLS certificates, and Directory Service (D) hosts directories.

questions.question: A company wants to enhance security by launching a third-party ISP intrusion detection system from its AWS account. Which AWS service or resource should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS Marketplace sells third-party security appliances such as IDS/IPS ready to launch in your account. Security Hub (A) aggregates findings, Quick Starts (C) deploy reference architectures, and there is no AWS Security Center service (D).

questions.question: How does the AWS Cloud help companies build agility into their processes and cloud infrastructure?
options: Companies can avoid provisioning too much capacity when they do not know how much capacity is required.
Companies can expand into new geographic regions.
Companies can access a range of technologies to experiment and innovate quickly.
Companies can pay for IT resources only when they use the resources.
questions.explanation: Breadth of services lets teams experiment and innovate quickly, which is agility. Avoiding over-provisioning (A) is elasticity, geographic expansion (B) is global reach, and paying only for use (D) is pay-as-you-go pricing.

questions.question: Which AWS service or tool gives a company the ability to release application changes in an automated way?
questions.explanation: AWS CodeDeploy automates application deployments to EC2, Lambda, and ECS with strategies such as in-place and blue/green. AppFlow (A) moves SaaS data, PrivateLink (C) connects VPCs privately, and EKS Distro (D) distributes Kubernetes.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) perspective focuses on managing identities and permissions at scale?
questions.explanation: The CAF security perspective governs identity and access management at scale. Operations (A) runs workloads, platform (B) delivers infrastructure, and governance (C) oversees portfolios and risk.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature allows users to securely store encrypted credentials and retrieve these credentials when required?
questions.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager stores encrypted credentials and retrieves them programmatically with rotation support. The Encryption SDK (A) is a client-side library, Security Hub (B) aggregates findings, and Artifact (C) hosts compliance reports.

questions.question: Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework aligns with the ability to make frequent, small, and reversible changes to AWS Cloud architecture?
questions.explanation: Frequent small reversible changes are the operational excellence pillar's change principle. Security (A) protects data, cost optimization (B) avoids waste, and performance efficiency (D) uses resources efficiently.

questions.question: Which AWS service or resource can a company use to deploy AWS WAF rules?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF rules attach to Application Load Balancers (as well as CloudFront and API Gateway) to filter HTTP traffic. EC2 (A) runs compute, Trusted Advisor (C) checks best practices, and Network Load Balancer (D) passes through TCP without WAF inspection.

questions.question: A company hosts its website on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to ensure that the website reaches a global audience and provides minimum latency to users. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: CloudFront caches the website at edge locations worldwide for minimum latency. Route 53 (A) routes DNS, load balancing (C) distributes within Regions, and Lambda (D) runs code.

questions.question: Which AWS design principle emphasizes the reduction of interdependencies between components of an application?
questions.explanation: Loose coupling reduces interdependencies so components evolve and fail independently. Scalability (A) handles load, automation (C) speeds operations, and caching (D) improves performance.

questions.question: A company wants to provide one of its employees with access to Amazon RDS. The company also wants to limit the interaction to only the AWS CLI and AWS software development kits (SDKs). Which combination of actions should the company take to meet these requirements while following the principles of least privilege? (Choose two.)
options: Create an IAM user and provide AWS Management Console access only.
Create an IAM user and provide programmatic access only.
Create an IAM role and provide AWS Management Console access only.
Create an IAM policy with administrator access and attach it to the IAM user.
Create an IAM policy with Amazon RDS access and attach it to the IAM user.
questions.explanation: Least privilege for CLI/SDK-only RDS access means an IAM user with programmatic credentials only (B) plus a policy granting just RDS actions (E). Console access (A, C) is unnecessary, and administrator access (D) violates least privilege.

questions.question: A company is running a reporting web server application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application runs once every week and once again at the end of the month. The EC2 instances can be shut down when they are not in use. What is the MOST cost-effective billing model for this use case?
questions.explanation: Intermittent weekly and monthly runs with shutdowns between fit On-Demand Instances, paying only for hours used with no commitment. Reserved Instances (A, B) need steady use, and Capacity Reservations (C) hold capacity at a premium whether or not it runs.

questions.question: A company wants to discover, prepare, move, and integrate data from multiple sources for data analytics and machine learning. Which AWS serverless data integration service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Glue is a serverless data-integration service for discovering, preparing, moving, and cataloging analytics data. Data Exchange (B) licenses third-party datasets, Athena (C) queries S3 with SQL, and EMR (D) runs managed big-data clusters.

questions.question: A company is moving its development and test environments to AWS to increase agility and reduce cost. Because these are not production workloads and the servers are not fully utilized, occasional unavailability is acceptable. What is the MOST cost-effective Amazon EC2 pricing model that will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances offer the deepest discount for dev and test workloads that tolerate occasional interruption. Reserved (A) needs steady commitment, On-Demand (B) costs more, and Dedicated Hosts (D) reserve whole servers at a premium.

questions.question: A company deploys its application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application occasionally experiences sudden increases in demand. The company wants to ensure that its application can respond to changes in demand at the lowest possible cost. Which AWS service or concept will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Auto Scaling adds and removes capacity with demand spikes, keeping cost minimal by paying only for needed instances. Compute Optimizer (B) recommends sizes, Cost Explorer (C) analyzes spend, and the Well-Architected Framework (D) is guidance rather than a scaling mechanism.

questions.question: A company wants to organize its users so that the company can grant permissions to the users as a group. Which AWS service or tool can the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: IAM groups collect users so one attached policy grants permissions to all members at once. Security groups (A) filter network traffic, resource groups (C) organize resources, and Security Hub (D) aggregates findings.

questions.question: A company wants to build an application that uses AWS Lambda to run Python code. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which tasks will be the company’s responsibility? (Choose two.)
options: Installation of the computer language runtime.
Providing AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) access to the Lambda service.
questions.explanation: On Lambda, AWS manages infrastructure, OS, and runtimes (A, B, D) while the customer writes business-logic code (C) and grants IAM access to invoke and manage functions (E).

questions.question: A company needs to identify who accessed an AWS service and what action was performed for a given time period. Which AWS service should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail logs who called which API on which service and when, the audit trail for access history. CloudWatch (A) monitors metrics and logs, Security Hub (C) aggregates findings, and Inspector (D) scans vulnerabilities.

questions.question: A company wants to use a centralized AWS service to enforce compliance with the organizational business standards. The company wants to use an AWS service that can govern and control who can deploy, manage, and decommission AWS resources. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Service Catalog publishes approved product portfolios so central teams govern who can deploy and manage resources. CloudWatch (A) monitors, GuardDuty (C) detects threats, and Security Hub (D) aggregates findings.

questions.question: What does "security of the cloud” refer to in the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Availability of AWS services such as Amazon EC2
Security of the cloud infrastructure that runs all the AWS services
Implementation of password policies for IAM users
Security of customer environments by using AWS Network Firewall partners
questions.explanation: Security OF the cloud is AWS protecting the physical infrastructure, hypervisors, and managed platforms. IAM password policies (C) and customer firewall configs (D) are security IN the cloud, the customer's duty.

questions.question: A company has an application that produces unstructured data continuously. The company needs to store the data so that the data is durable and easy to query. Which AWS service can the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB stores schemaless unstructured data durably at scale with queryable keys. RDS (A) and Aurora (B) are relational, and QuickSight (C) visualizes data rather than storing it.

questions.question: Which options are AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) perspectives? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The six CAF perspectives are business, people, governance, platform, security, and operations, so security (B) and business (E) are correct. Cloud fluency (A) and change acceleration (C) are transformation outcomes, and architecture (D) is not a named perspective.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate a company’s on-premises container infrastructure to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to prevent unplanned administration and operation cost and adapt to a serverless architecture. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Fargate runs containers serverlessly with no servers to administer, fitting a move from self-managed container hosts. Connect (A) is a contact center, Lightsail (C) bundles VPS instances, and EC2 (D) still needs server administration.

questions.question: A company wants its Amazon EC2 instances to be in different locations but share the same geographic area. The company also wants to use multiple power grids and independent networking connectivity for the EC2 instances. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Use EC2 instances in multiple edge locations in the same AWS Region.
Use EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones in the same AWS Region.
Use EC2 instances in multiple Amazon Connect locations in the same AWS Region.
Use EC2 instances in multiple AWS Artifact locations in the same AWS Region.
questions.explanation: Availability Zones are isolated locations within one Region with separate power and networking, so spreading EC2 across AZs meets the same-area plus independent infrastructure requirement. Edge locations (A) serve cached content, and Connect (C) and Artifact (D) are unrelated services with no locations.

questions.question: An ecommerce company has deployed a new web application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to distribute incoming HTTP traffic evenly across all running instances. Which AWS service or resource will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: An Application Load Balancer distributes HTTP and HTTPS traffic evenly across EC2 targets. Auto Scaling (A) adjusts capacity, Gateway Load Balancer (C) routes to virtual appliances, and Network Load Balancer (D) handles TCP/UDP rather than HTTP routing.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature gives users the ability to connect VPCs and on-premises networks to a central hub?
questions.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway hubs VPCs and on-premises networks together with central routing. Virtual private and customer gateways (A, D) terminate VPNs, and an internet gateway (C) reaches the internet.

questions.question: A company wants to run CPU-intensive workload across multiple Amazon EC2 instances. Which EC2 instance type should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Compute optimized instances (C family) provide the highest vCPU performance per dollar for CPU-intensive work. General purpose (A) balances all resources, memory optimized (C) suits in-memory workloads, and storage optimized (D) suits high I/O.

questions.question: A company is connecting multiple VPCs and on-premises networks. The company needs to use an AWS service as a cloud router to simplify peering relationships. Which AWS service can the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway acts as a cloud router hubbing VPCs and on-premises links to simplify peering. Direct Connect (A) is a private line, Connect (C) is a contact center, and Route 53 (D) is DNS.

questions.question: A company stores a large amount of data that auditors access only twice each year. Which Amazon S3 storage class should the company use to store the data with the LOWEST cost?
questions.explanation: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is the lowest-cost class for rarely accessed data (twice yearly) that still needs millisecond retrieval. Outposts (A) runs storage on premises, Standard (C) charges full price, and Intelligent-Tiering (D) adds monitoring fees better suited to changing patterns.

questions.question: Which action should a company take to improve security in its AWS account?
options: Require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for privileged users.
Create an access key for the AWS account root user.
Create an access key for each privileged user.
questions.explanation: AWS best practice requires MFA on privileged and root users to block credential-only compromise. The root user cannot be removed (B), and creating root or standing access keys (C, D) increases risk rather than reducing it.

questions.question: Which of the following are ways to improve security on AWS? (Choose two.)
options: Granting the broadest permissions to all IAM roles
Running application code with AWS Cloud
Enabling multi-factor authentication (MFA) with Amazon Cognito
Using AWS Trusted Advisor security checks
questions.explanation: MFA through Cognito (D) hardens sign-in and Trusted Advisor security checks (E) surface misconfigurations. Artifact (A) hosts compliance reports, broad permissions (B) violate least privilege, and running code in the cloud (C) is not itself a security control.

questions.question: Which AWS service can a company use to manage encryption keys in the cloud?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules for creating and managing encryption keys. License Manager (A) tracks licenses, ACM (B) provisions TLS certificates, and Directory Service (D) hosts directories.

questions.question: A company wants to store its files in the AWS Cloud. Users need to be able to download these files directly using a public URL. Which AWS service or feature will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 serves files directly over HTTPS public URLs with versioning and lifecycle support. Redshift (A) warehouses data, EBS (B) attaches to instances, and EFS (C) mounts to instances over NFS.

questions.question: A company is using AWS for all its IT infrastructure. The company's developers are allowed to deploy applications on their own. The developers want to deploy their applications without having to provision the infrastructure themselves. Which AWS service should the developers use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk deploys developer code while provisioning and managing the underlying infrastructure automatically. CloudFormation (A) still requires writing templates, CodeBuild (B) compiles code, and CodeDeploy (D) deploys to existing infrastructure.

questions.question: A company wants to gain insights from its data and build interactive data visualization dashboards. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon QuickSight builds interactive BI dashboards with ML-powered insights. SageMaker (A) trains models, Rekognition (B) analyzes images, and Kinesis (D) streams data.

questions.question: A cloud engineer wants to store data in Amazon S3. The engineer will access some of the data yearly and some of the data daily. Which S3 storage class will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)
questions.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent, infrequent, and archive tiers as daily versus yearly access patterns change, minimizing cost. Standard (A) overpays for yearly data, Deep Archive (B) cannot serve daily reads quickly, and One Zone-IA (C) risks single-AZ durability.

questions.question: Which of the following are economic benefits of using the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: AWS Enterprise Support at no additional cost
questions.explanation: Consumption-based pay-as-you-go pricing (A) and AWS economies of scale (C) are core cloud economic benefits. Perpetual licenses (B) and bring-your-own hardware (E) are on-premises models, and Enterprise Support (D) is a paid plan.

questions.question: A user is moving a workload from a local data center to an architecture that is distributed between the local data center and the AWS Cloud. Which type of migration is this?
questions.explanation: Splitting a workload between the local data center and AWS is an on-premises-to-hybrid migration. Cloud native (A, B, D) describes fully cloud-built architectures rather than the split state.

questions.question: A company needs to store infrequently used data for data archives and long-term backups. Which AWS service or storage class will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is the low-cost archival class for infrequently accessed backups with minutes-to-hours retrieval. FSx for Lustre (A) is HPC scratch storage, EBS (B) attaches to instances, and EFS (C) is shared file storage at higher cost.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides users with AWS issued reports, certifications, accreditations, and third-party attestations?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact provides on-demand AWS-issued reports, certifications, and third-party attestations. Trusted Advisor (B) checks best practices, Health Dashboard (C) tracks service events, and Config (D) records configuration.

questions.question: A company needs to create and publish interactive business intelligence dashboards. The dashboards require insights that are powered by machine learning. Which AWS service or tool will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon QuickSight publishes interactive dashboards with ML insights such as anomaly detection and natural-language queries. Glue Studio (A) builds ETL jobs, Redshift (C) warehouses data, and Athena (D) queries S3 with SQL.

questions.question: A company wants to use AWS. The company has stringent requirements about low-latency access to on-premises systems and data residency. Which AWS service should the company use to design a solution that meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Outposts places AWS racks on premises for low-latency access with data residency control. Wavelength (A) embeds compute in telecom networks, Transit Gateway (B) routes networks, and Ground Station (C) communicates with satellites.

questions.question: A company runs an on-premises contact center for customers. The company needs to migrate to a cloud-based solution that can deliver artificial intelligence features to improve user experience. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On)
questions.explanation: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact-center service with built-in AI features such as Contact Lens analytics and Lex chatbots. Wavelength (A) is edge compute, Identity Center (B) manages SSO, and Direct Connect (C) links networks.

questions.question: A company needs the ability to acquire resources when the resources are needed. The company also needs the ability to release the resources when the resources are no longer needed. Which AWS concept represents the company's goals?
questions.explanation: Elasticity is acquiring capacity when needed and releasing it when not, scaling with demand automatically. Scalability (A) handles growth, sustainability (B) minimizes environmental impact, and operational excellence (D) runs workloads well.

questions.question: A company wants to use Amazon EC2 instances for a stable production workload that will run for 1 year. Which instance purchasing option meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: A steady 1-year production workload earns the biggest safe discount from a 1-year Reserved Instance. Dedicated Hosts (A) add physical isolation cost, On-Demand (C) has no discount, and Spot (D) risks interruption.

questions.question: A company wants to log in securely to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. How can the company accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation: AWS documentation prescribes SSH key pairs for secure Linux EC2 login instead of passwords. A VPN (B) links networks, end-to-end encryption (C) is generic, and Route 53 (D) resolves DNS.

questions.question: A company wants to use a serverless compute service for an application. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda runs code serverlessly with no servers to manage. CloudFormation (B) provisions infrastructure, Beanstalk (C) manages servers behind apps, and load balancing (D) distributes traffic.

questions.question: A company wants a solution that will automatically adjust the number of Amazon EC2 instances that are being used based on the current load. Which AWS offering will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: EC2 Auto Scaling groups add or remove instances automatically based on load policies. Dedicated Hosts (A) reserve hardware, placement groups (B) control AZ placement, and Reserved Instances (D) are pricing.

questions.question: A company is building AWS architecture to deliver real-time data feeds from an on-premises data center into an application that runs on AWS. The company needs a consistent network connection with minimal latency. What should the company use to connect the application and the data center to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Direct Connect provides a private dedicated link with consistent minimal latency for real-time feeds. Public internet (B) varies, VPN (C) traverses the internet, and Connect (D) is a contact center.

questions.question: A company plans to migrate its custom marketing application and order-processing application to AWS. The company needs to deploy the applications on different types of instances with various configurations of CPU, memory, storage, and networking capacity. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 offers diverse instance types with configurable CPU, memory, storage, and networking for varied applications. Lambda (A) runs functions, Cognito (B) authenticates users, and Athena (C) queries S3.

questions.question: A company wants to monitor and block malicious HTTP and HTTPS requests that its Amazon CloudFront distributions receive. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF attaches to CloudFront to inspect and block malicious HTTP/HTTPS requests. GuardDuty (A) detects threats, Inspector (B) scans vulnerabilities, and Detective (C) investigates findings.

questions.question: Which AWS services can host PostgreSQL databases? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL runs managed on Aurora PostgreSQL (B) and self-managed on EC2 (C). S3 (A) stores objects, OpenSearch (D) searches text, and EFS (E) serves files.

questions.question: Which AWS service can generate information that can be used by external auditors?
questions.explanation: AWS Config records resource configuration history used as evidence by external auditors. Cognito (A) authenticates users, FSx (B) serves files, and Inspector (D) scans vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature requires an internet service provider (ISP) and a colocation facility to be implemented?
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect requires cross-connects provisioned through an ISP at a Direct Connect colocation facility. VPN (A) traverses the internet, Connect (B) is a contact center, and an internet gateway (D) is a VPC component.

questions.question: A company wants its Amazon EC2 instances to operate in a highly available environment, even if there is a natural disaster in a particular geographic area. Which solution achieves this goal?
options: Use EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions.
Use EC2 instances in multiple edge locations.
Use EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone but in different AWS Regions.
Use Amazon CloudFront with the EC2 instances configured as the source.
questions.explanation: Spreading EC2 across multiple Regions survives a regional natural disaster, since Regions are geographically independent. Edge locations (B) cache content, an AZ cannot span Regions (C), and CloudFront (D) caches but does not relocate compute.

questions.question: Which AWS service allows for file sharing between multiple Amazon EC2 instances?
questions.explanation: Amazon EFS is a shared NFS file system mountable by many EC2 instances concurrently. Direct Connect (A) links networks, Snowball Edge (B) transfers data offline, and Backup (C) centralizes backups.

questions.question: A company needs to manage multiple logins across AWS accounts within the same organization in AWS Organizations. Which AWS service should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: IAM Identity Center provides SSO across all accounts in an Organization from one portal. VPC (A) networks resources, GuardDuty (B) detects threats, and Cognito (C) authenticates application end users rather than workforce logins.

questions.question: A company uses Amazon WorkSpaces. Which task is the responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Set up multi-factor authentication (MFA) for each WorkSpaces user account.
Ensure the environmental safety and security of the AWS infrastructure that hosts WorkSpaces.
Provide security for WorkSpaces user accounts through AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).
Configure AWS CloudTrail to log API calls and user activity.
questions.explanation: For the managed WorkSpaces service, AWS secures the underlying facilities, power, and hardware. Customer duties include user MFA (A), IAM user security (C), and enabling CloudTrail logging (D).

questions.question: A company is migrating its public website to AWS. The company wants to host the domain name for the website on AWS. Which AWS service should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 is the DNS service for registering and hosting domain names. Lambda (A) runs code, CloudFront (B) delivers content, and Direct Connect (C) links networks.

questions.question: A company uses a third-party identity provider (IdP). The company wants to provide its employees with access to AWS accounts and services without requiring another set of login credentials. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: IAM Identity Center federates third-party IdPs via SAML so employees use existing credentials across AWS accounts. Directory Service (A) hosts directories, Cognito (B) serves app end users, and RAM (C) shares resources.

questions.question: Which combination of AWS services can be used to move a commercial relational database to an Amazon-managed open-source database? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: AWS DMS replicates the data into the open-source engine and the Schema Conversion Tool converts commercial schemas and procedures. SDKs (B) build applications, Systems Manager (D) manages operations, and EMR (E) processes big data.

questions.question: Which AWS service gives users on-demand, self-service access to AWS compliance control reports?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact provides self-service compliance control reports on demand. Config (A) records configuration, GuardDuty (B) detects threats, and Trusted Advisor (C) checks best practices.

questions.question: A company runs a legacy workload in an on-premises data center. The company wants to migrate the workload to AWS. The company does not want to make any changes to the workload. Which migration strategy should the company use?
questions.explanation: Rehost (lift and shift) moves workloads unchanged onto AWS infrastructure. Repurchase (A) swaps products, replatform (B) makes small optimizations, and refactor (C) re-architects applications.

questions.question: A company is planning to migrate applications to the AWS Cloud. During a system audit, the company finds that its content management system (CMS) application is incompatible with cloud environments. Which migration strategies will help the company to migrate the CMS application with the LEAST effort? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: For an incompatible CMS, Retire (A) decommissions unused parts with zero migration effort and Repurchase (C) replaces it with a SaaS product instead of porting code. Rehost (B) and replatform (D) still require running the incompatible app, and refactor (E) rewrites it at maximum effort.

questions.question: Which option is AWS responsible for under the AWS shared responsibility model?
questions.explanation: Hardware and infrastructure, including facilities, power, and physical hosts, are entirely AWS's responsibility. Network and firewall configuration (A), client-side encryption (B), and user permissions (C) are customer duties.

questions.question: A company wants to run a graph query that provides credit card users’ names, addresses, and transactions. The company wants the graph to show if the names, addresses, and transactions indicates possible fraud. Which AWS database service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Neptune is the managed graph database for relationship queries such as fraud rings across names, addresses, and transactions. DocumentDB (A) stores documents, Timestream (B) stores time series, and DynamoDB (C) is key-value.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides machine learning capability to detect and analyze content in images and videos?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition applies ML to detect objects, faces, text, and unsafe content in images and videos. Connect (A) is a contact center, Lightsail (B) bundles VPS instances, and Personalize (C) builds recommendations.

questions.question: A company wants its AWS usage to be more sustainable. The company wants to track, measure, review, and forecast polluting emissions that result from its AWS applications. Which AWS service or tool can the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: The customer carbon footprint tool tracks, measures, and forecasts emissions from AWS usage for sustainability reporting. Health Dashboard (A) tracks service events, Support Center (C) handles cases, and QuickSight (D) dashboards BI data.

questions.question: Which AWS service gives users the ability to deploy highly repeatable infrastructure configurations?
questions.explanation: CloudFormation templates deploy identical infrastructure repeatedly as versioned stacks. CodeDeploy (B) deploys apps, CodeBuild (C) compiles code, and Systems Manager (D) manages operations.

questions.question: A company needs to provide customer service by using voice calls and web chat features. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Connect provides cloud voice and web-chat contact centers. Aurora (A) is a database, WorkSpaces (C) delivers desktops, and Organizations (D) manages accounts.

questions.question: Which AWS service is designed to help users handle large amounts of data in a data warehouse environment?
questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift is the managed petabyte-scale data warehouse for large analytical datasets. RDS (A) and Aurora (D) are transactional databases, and DynamoDB (B) is NoSQL.

questions.question: A company is building a web application using AWS. Which AWS service will help prevent network layer DDoS attacks against the web application?
questions.explanation: AWS Shield (Standard and Advanced) protects against network and transport layer DDoS attacks. WAF (A) filters application-layer requests, Firewall Manager (B) centrally manages WAF rules, and GuardDuty (C) detects threats.

questions.question: Which of the following are advantages of moving to the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: Users can implement all AWS services in seconds.
AWS assumes all responsibility for the security of infrastructure and applications.
Users experience increased speed and agility.
Users benefit from massive economies of scale.
Users can move hardware from their data center to the AWS Cloud.
questions.explanation: Cloud advantages include increased speed and agility (C) and massive economies of scale (D). No service deploys in seconds universally (A), security remains shared (B), and hardware cannot move into AWS data centers (E).

questions.question: Which AWS compute service gives users the ability to securely and reliably run containers at scale?
questions.explanation: Amazon ECS securely runs containers at scale with IAM task roles, networking, and orchestration. Aurora (B) is a database, Athena (C) queries S3, and Polly (D) converts text to speech.

questions.question: Which AWS tool or feature acts as a VPC firewall at the subnet level?
questions.explanation: Network ACLs act as stateless firewalls at the subnet level. Security groups (A) filter at the instance level, Traffic Mirroring (C) copies packets for inspection, and internet gateways (D) route to the internet.

questions.question: A company runs an application on AWS that performs batch jobs. The application is fault-tolerant and can handle interruptions. The company wants to optimize the cost to run the application. Which AWS offering will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: EC2 Spot Instances use spare capacity at up to 90% off, ideal for fault-tolerant interruptible batch jobs. Macie (A) finds PII, Neptune (B) is a graph database, and On-Demand (D) costs more without interruption risk.

questions.question: Which AWS service can be used to send alerts when a specific Amazon CloudWatch alarm is invoked?
questions.explanation: CloudWatch alarms publish to SNS topics, which fan out notifications via email, SMS, and Lambda. CloudTrail (A) audits APIs, SQS (C) queues messages without push notification, and EventBridge (D) routes events rather than serving as the alarm's notification channel.

questions.question: A cloud practitioner wants to use a highly available and scalable DNS service for its AWS workload. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 is the highly available, scalable DNS service with global anycast routing. Lightsail (B) bundles VPS instances, Amplify Hosting (C) hosts web apps, and S3 (D) stores objects.

questions.question: According to the AWS shared responsibility model, which task is the customer's responsibility?
options: Maintaining the infrastructure needed to run AWS Lambda
Updating the operating system of Amazon DynamoDB instances
Updating the guest operating system on Amazon EC2 instances
questions.explanation: Customers patch guest operating systems on EC2 instances they control. Lambda infrastructure (A), DynamoDB OS updates (B), and S3 infrastructure (C) are all AWS-managed.

questions.question: A company is learning about its responsibilities that are related to the management of Amazon EC2 instances. Which tasks for EC2 instances are the company’s responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model? (Choose two.)
options: Install and patch the machine hypervisor.
Encrypt data at rest on associated storage.
Install the physical hardware and cabling.
Provide physical security for the EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: On EC2, customers patch the guest OS (B) and encrypt data at rest on EBS volumes (C). The hypervisor (A), hardware (D), and physical security (E) are AWS duties.

questions.question: A company runs MySQL database workloads on self-managed servers in an on-premises data center. The company wants to migrate the database workloads to an AWS managed service. Which migration strategy should the company use?
questions.explanation: Moving MySQL to RDS or Aurora with minor changes is replatforming (lift and reshape). Rehost (A) moves unchanged servers, repurchase (B) swaps products, and refactor (C) re-architects code.

questions.question: A company is planning to migrate a monolithic application to AWS. The company wants to modernize the application by splitting it into microservices. The company will deploy the microservices on AWS. Which migration strategy should the company use?
questions.explanation: Splitting a monolith into microservices is refactoring or re-architecting. Rehost (A) lifts unchanged, repurchase (B) swaps products, and replatform (C) makes only small platform changes.

questions.question: A company wants to implement detailed tracking of its cloud costs by department and project. Which AWS feature or service should the company use?
questions.explanation: Cost allocation tags label resources by department and project so bills and Cost Explorer break down spend accordingly. Consolidated billing (A) combines accounts, Marketplace (C) sells software, and Budgets (D) alerts on thresholds.

questions.question: A user wants to invoke an AWS Lambda function when an Amazon EC2 instance enters the “stopping” state. Which AWS service is appropriate for this use case?
questions.explanation: Amazon EventBridge receives EC2 state-change events (such as stopping) and triggers Lambda targets via rules. Config (B) audits configuration, SNS (C) sends notifications, and CloudFormation (D) provisions infrastructure.

questions.question: A company has a MariaDB database on premises. The company wants to move the data to the AWS Cloud. Which AWS service will host this database with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS supports MariaDB as a managed engine with automated patching, backups, and failover for least overhead. Neptune (B) is a graph database, S3 (C) stores objects, and DynamoDB (D) is NoSQL requiring a rewrite.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature supports governance, compliance, and risk auditing of AWS accounts?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail logs API activity across accounts, providing the audit trail needed for governance, compliance, and risk auditing. MFA (A) hardens sign-in, Lambda (B) runs code, and SNS (C) sends notifications.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud design principle is a company using when the company implements AWS CloudTrail?
questions.explanation: Enabling CloudTrail activates traceability by recording every API action for auditing and forensics. Serverless architectures (B), operations as code (C), and global deployment (D) are separate design principles.

questions.question: A company needs a threat detection service that will continuously monitor its AWS accounts, workloads, and Amazon S3 buckets for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior. Which AWS service meets these requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC flow, and DNS logs plus S3 protection for malicious activity. Shield (A) mitigates DDoS, Firewall Manager (B) manages WAF rules, and Inspector (C) scans vulnerabilities.

questions.question: A company is planning to migrate to the AWS Cloud. The company is conducting organizational transformation and wants to become more responsive to customer inquiries and feedback. Which task should the company perform to meet these requirements, according to the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)?
options: Realign teams to focus on products and value streams.
Create new value propositions with new products and services.
Use a new data and analytics platform to create actionable insights.
questions.explanation: The CAF people perspective realigns teams around products and value streams to improve customer responsiveness. New value propositions (B) are business perspective, analytics platforms (C) are platform, and migration (D) is delivery execution.

questions.question: A company wants to rightsize its Amazon EC2 instances. Which configuration change will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Add EC2 instances in another Availability Zone.
Change the size and type of the EC2 instances based on utilization.
Convert the payment method from On-Demand to Savings Plans.
Reprovision the EC2 instances with a larger instance type.
questions.explanation: Rightsizing means changing instance size and type to match utilization, directly aligning capacity with need. Adding AZ instances (A) increases cost, Savings Plans (C) discount pricing without resizing, and upsizing (D) may worsen over-provisioning.

questions.question: Which AWS service supports user sign-up functionality and authentication to mobile and web applications?
questions.explanation: Amazon Cognito user pools provide sign-up, sign-in, and federation for mobile and web apps. Config (B) audits resources, GuardDuty (C) detects threats, and Systems Manager (D) manages operations.

questions.question: Which benefit of the AWS Cloud helps companies achieve lower usage costs because of the aggregate usage of all AWS users?
options: Ability to go global in minutes
questions.explanation: Economies of scale spread AWS infrastructure costs across all users, lowering everyone's unit price. Capacity guessing (A), global reach (B), and agility (D) are separate benefits.

questions.question: Which task is the responsibility of the customer, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Patch the Amazon DynamoDB operating system.
Secure Amazon CloudFront edge locations by allowing physical access according to the principle of least privilege.
Protect the hardware that runs AWS services.
Use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) according to the principle of least privilege.
questions.explanation: Customers must apply IAM least privilege to their own users and roles. DynamoDB patching (A), edge-location physical access (B), and hardware protection (C) are all AWS duties.

questions.question: A company wants to manage its cloud resources by using infrastructure as code (IaC) templates. The company needs to meet compliance requirements. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Service Catalog publishes compliant IaC product portfolios so teams provision only approved templates. Artifact (A) hosts compliance reports, Resource Explorer (B) searches resources, and License Manager (C) tracks licenses.

questions.question: A systems administrator wants to monitor the CPU utilization of a company's Amazon EC2 instances. Which AWS service can provide this information?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch collects EC2 CPU utilization metrics with alarms and dashboards. Config (A) audits configuration, Trusted Advisor (B) checks best practices, and CloudTrail (C) audits API calls.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate all of its on-premises infrastructure to the AWS Cloud. Before migration, the company wants estimate of costs for running its as-is infrastructure. Which AWS service or principle should the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: The AWS Pricing Calculator estimates as-is on-premises costs modeled on AWS before migration. The Well-Architected Framework (B) guides design, shared responsibility (C) splits security duties, and the CAF (D) guides adoption.

questions.question: An independent software vendor wants to deliver and share its custom Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to prospective customers. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS Marketplace lets vendors publish and share custom AMIs with customers for purchase or subscription. Data Exchange (B) licenses datasets, EC2 (C) runs instances, and Organizations (D) manages accounts.

questions.question: Which component must be attached to a VPC to enable inbound internet access?
questions.explanation: An internet gateway attached to the VPC routes inbound traffic from the internet to public subnets. A NAT gateway (A) allows outbound-only access, VPC endpoints (B) reach AWS services privately, and VPN (C) links on-premises.

questions.question: Which AWS service supports a company's ability to treat infrastructure as code?
questions.explanation: CloudFormation defines infrastructure as versioned JSON or YAML templates. CodeDeploy (A) deploys apps, Beanstalk (B) manages app platforms, and API Gateway (C) exposes APIs.

questions.question: A company is building an application that will receive millions of database queries each second. The company needs the data store for the application to scale to meet these needs. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB scales to millions of requests per second with single-digit millisecond latency. Cloud9 (B) is an IDE, ElastiCache Memcached (C) caches rather than persisting primary data, and Neptune (D) serves graph queries.

questions.question: An AWS user wants to proactively detect when an instance or account might be compromised or if there are threats from attacks. Which AWS service should the user choose?
questions.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty uses ML on CloudTrail, flow, and DNS logs to detect compromised instances, accounts, and attack threats. WAF (B) filters web requests, Shield (C) mitigates DDoS, and Inspector (D) scans vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Which AWS Support plan provides the full set of AWS Trusted Advisor checks at the LOWEST cost?
questions.explanation: Business Support is the cheapest plan unlocking all Trusted Advisor checks; Developer and Basic expose only a core subset. Enterprise plans (C, D) add TAMs at higher cost.

questions.question: A company's application is running on Amazon EC2 instances. The company is planning a partial migration to a serverless architecture in the next year and wants to pay for resources up front. Which AWS purchasing option will optimize the company's costs?
questions.explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply hourly-commitment discounts across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda, suiting a shift toward serverless with upfront payment. Convertible RIs (A) and EC2 Instance plans (C) cover EC2 only, and Spot (B) cannot be prepaid.

questions.question: A retail company is building a new mobile app. The company is evaluating whether to build the app at an on-premises data center or in the AWS Cloud. Which of the following are benefits of building this app in the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
options: A large, upfront capital expense and low variable expenses
Increased speed for trying out new projects
Complete control over the physical security of the infrastructure
Flexibility to scale up in minutes as the application becomes popular
Ability to pick the specific data centers that will host the application servers
questions.explanation: Cloud benefits include experimenting faster without procurement (B) and scaling up in minutes with demand (D). Large upfront capex (A) is the on-premises model, physical control (C) stays with AWS, and customers choose Regions, not specific data centers (E).

questions.question: A company must archive its documents by using a write-once, read-many (WORM) model to meet legal and compliance obligations. Which feature of Amazon S3 can the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: S3 Glacier Vault Lock enforces WORM immutability with compliance policies that cannot be altered once locked. Versioning (A) keeps copies but allows deletion, bucket policies (B) control access, and MFA delete (D) only adds an MFA prompt for deletions.

questions.question: A company has batch workloads that need to run for short periods of time on Amazon EC2. The workloads can handle interruptions and can start again from where they ended. What is the MOST cost-effective EC2 instance purchasing option to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances supply spare capacity at up to 90% off for short interruptible batch runs that can resume. Reserved (A) needs steady commitment, Dedicated (C) isolates hardware at a premium, and On-Demand (D) costs more.

questions.question: A company needs to deploy a PostgreSQL database into Amazon RDS. The database must be highly available and fault tolerant. Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?
options: Amazon RDS with a single Availability Zone
Amazon RDS with multiple Availability Zones
questions.explanation: RDS Multi-AZ deploys a synchronous standby in another AZ for automatic failover of PostgreSQL. Single-AZ (A) has no standby, snapshots (B) are point-in-time backups, and DMS (D) migrates databases.

questions.question: What is the MOST secure way to store passwords on AWS?
options: Store passwords in an Amazon S3 bucket.
Store passwords as AWS CloudFormation parameters.
Store passwords in AWS Storage Gateway.
Store passwords in AWS Secrets Manager.
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager encrypts passwords at rest, rotates them, and retrieves them programmatically. S3 (A), CloudFormation parameters (B), and Storage Gateway (C) are not credential stores with rotation.

questions.question: Which statements accurately describe the relationships among components of AWS global infrastructure? (Choose two.)
options: There are more AWS Regions than Availability Zones.
There are more edge locations than AWS Regions.
An edge location is an Availability Zone.
There are more AWS Regions than edge locations.
There are more Availability Zones than AWS Regions.
questions.explanation: AWS runs hundreds of edge locations but only dozens of Regions (B), and each Region contains multiple AZs so AZs outnumber Regions (E). Regions do not outnumber AZs (A), edges are not AZs (C), and Regions do not outnumber edges (D).

questions.question: Which AWS service provides DNS resolution?
questions.explanation: Amazon Route 53 is the DNS service for domain registration, routing, and health checks. CloudFront (A) delivers content, VPC (B) networks resources, and Direct Connect (C) links on-premises.

questions.question: A company needs to host an application in a specific geographic area to comply with regulations. Which feature of the AWS global infrastructure will help the company meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: A global footprint of Regions lets companies place workloads in specific geographies for data-residency compliance. Scalability (A), availability (C), and performance (D) describe capacity and reliability rather than location choice.

questions.question: An ecommerce company plans to move its data center workload to the AWS Cloud to support highly dynamic usage patterns. Which benefits make the AWS Cloud cost-effective for the migration of this type of workload? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Dynamic workloads benefit from elasticity that scales with demand (C) and pay-as-you-go pricing with no idle capacity cost (D). Reliability (A), security (B), and high availability (E) are architectural qualities rather than cost mechanisms.

questions.question: When designing AWS workloads to be operational even when there are component failures, what is an AWS best practice?
options: Place the main component on the us-east-1 Region.
Design for automatic failover to healthy resources.
Design workloads to fit on a single Amazon EC2 instance.
questions.explanation: Best practice designs automatic failover with health checks so traffic shifts to healthy resources on component failure. Quarterly tests (A) are too infrequent alone, single-Region concentration (B) adds risk, and single-instance design (D) creates a single point of failure.

questions.question: Which of the following can the AWS Pricing Calculator do?
options: Provide in-depth information about AWS pricing strategies.
Provide users with access to their monthly bills.
questions.explanation: The Pricing Calculator projects future monthly costs for planned architectures. Historical costs (B) live in Cost Explorer and CUR, pricing strategy depth (C) is documentation, and monthly bills (D) are in the Billing Console.

questions.question: Which AWS solution gives companies the ability to use protocols such as NFS to store and retrieve objects in Amazon S3?
questions.explanation: Storage Gateway file gateway presents S3 buckets as NFS or SMB shares for storing and retrieving objects. FSx for Lustre (A) serves HPC scratch storage, volume gateway (B) presents iSCSI block volumes, and EFS (D) is NFS-only without S3 backing.

questions.question: A user has been granted permission to change their own IAM user password. Which AWS services can the user use to change the password? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Users with iam:ChangePassword can change passwords via the AWS CLI (A) and the Management Console (C). KMS (B) manages keys, RAM (D) shares resources, and Secrets Manager (E) stores secrets rather than IAM passwords.

questions.question: Which task is the customer's responsibility, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
options: Patch a guest operating system that is deployed on an Amazon EC2 instance.
Control physical access to an AWS data center.
Control access to AWS underlying hardware.
Patch a host operating system that is deployed on Amazon S3.
questions.explanation: Customers patch guest operating systems on EC2 instances they manage. Data-center access (B), hardware access (C), and host OS patching for managed services like S3 (D) are AWS duties.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature provides a firewall at the subnet level within a VPC?
questions.explanation: Network ACLs are stateless firewalls at the subnet level within a VPC. Security groups (A) filter at the instance level, elastic network interfaces (C) attach networking to instances, and WAF (D) filters web requests.

questions.question: A company wants to use automated video analysis to identify employees that are accessing its offices. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition performs automated video and image analysis including face detection and comparison for identifying people. Polly (B) synthesizes speech, Cognito (C) authenticates users, and Lambda (D) runs code.

questions.question: A company needs to host a web server on Amazon EC2 instances for at least 1 year. The web server cannot tolerate interruption. Which EC2 instance purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: A non-interruptible 1-year server earns the best pricing from a Partial Upfront Reserved Instance with steady-state discount. On-Demand (A) has no discount, Spot (C) can be interrupted, and No Upfront (D) discounts less than partial prepayment.

questions.question: Which guidelines are best practices for using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)? (Choose two.)
options: Use inline policies instead of customer managed policies.
Grant maximum privileges to IAM users.
Use groups to assign permissions to IAM users.
questions.explanation: IAM best practices create individual users per person (B) and assign permissions through groups (E). Sharing keys (A), inline policies over managed ones (C), and maximum privileges (D) are all anti-patterns.

questions.question: Which advantage of cloud computing allows users to scale resources up and down based on the amount of load that an application supports?
options: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
questions.explanation: Stopping capacity guessing means scaling resources up and down with application load. Global reach (A), economies of scale (C), and fixed-to-variable expense (D) are separate benefits.

questions.question: A company is requesting Payment Card Industry (PCI) reports that validate the operating effectiveness of AWS security controls. How should the company obtain these reports?
options: Download reports from AWS Security Hub.
Contact an AWS technical account manager (TAM).
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact hosts on-demand PCI and other compliance reports validating AWS control effectiveness. Support (A) and TAMs (D) do not distribute reports, and Security Hub (C) aggregates findings.

questions.question: An ecommerce company wants to distribute traffic between the Amazon EC2 instances that host its website. Which AWS service or resource will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: An Application Load Balancer distributes HTTP traffic across EC2 targets. WAF (B) filters requests, CloudHSM (C) manages keys, and Direct Connect (D) links networks.

questions.question: Which AWS services or features form the AWS Cloud global infrastructure? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Availability Zones (A) and AWS Regions (C) are the building blocks of global infrastructure. ElastiCache (B), S3 (D), and VPC (E) are services that run inside that infrastructure rather than defining it.

questions.question: According to the AWS shared responsibility model, which of the following are AWS responsibilities? (Choose two.)
options: Network infrastructure and virtualization of infrastructure
questions.explanation: AWS owns the network and virtualization layers (A) plus physical hardware security (D). Application data (B), guest operating systems (C), and credentials and policies (E) are customer duties.

questions.question: A company uses Amazon Aurora as its database service. The company wants to encrypt its databases and database backups. Which party manages the encryption of the database clusters and database snapshots, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?
questions.explanation: Encrypting Aurora clusters and snapshots (enabling encryption, managing keys) is the customer's decision and duty; AWS then executes the encryption mechanics on that configuration. Marketplace and third-party partners (C, D) are uninvolved, and AWS alone (A) does not choose encryption for customer data.

questions.question: A company is hosting a web application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to implement custom conditions to filter and control inbound web traffic. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF filters inbound web traffic with custom rules for SQL injection, XSS, and geo-blocking on ALB, CloudFront, and API Gateway. GuardDuty (A) detects threats, Macie (C) finds PII, and Shield (D) mitigates DDoS.

questions.question: A company wants to maintain bandwidth throughput and provide a more consistent network experience than public internet-based connections. Which AWS service should the company choose?
questions.explanation: Direct Connect provides dedicated bandwidth with consistent throughput versus the public internet. VPN (A) traverses the internet, Connect (C) is a contact center, and CloudFront (D) caches content.

questions.question: A company has temporary workload that is also variable. The company needs to use Amazon EC2 instances for the workload. The EC2 instances need to handle short bursts of work that cannot stop before finishing. Which purchase option will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Temporary variable bursts that must finish without interruption fit On-Demand Instances with per-second billing and no commitment. Spot (A) can be interrupted, while Savings Plans (C) and Reserved Instances (D) need steady commitments.

questions.question: A company's employees are working from home. The company wants its employees to use their personal devices to connect to a managed workstation in the AWS Cloud. Which AWS service should the company use to provide the remote environment?
questions.explanation: Amazon WorkSpaces delivers managed virtual desktops accessible from personal devices. Cloud9 (B) is a browser IDE, Outposts (C) extends AWS on premises, and Lightsail (D) bundles VPS servers.

questions.question: A company needs to use SQL syntax to perform a direct query of objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. Which AWS service can the company use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena runs ANSI SQL directly against S3 objects serverlessly. Glue (A) prepares ETL data, Lambda (C) runs code, and Kinesis (D) streams data.

questions.question: A company uses Amazon RDS for a product database. The company wants to ensure the database is highly available. Which feature of Amazon RDS will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: RDS Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby in another AZ for automatic failover. Read replicas (A) scale reads asynchronously, blue/green (B) stages upgrades, and Reserved Instances (D) are pricing.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides serverless compute for use with containers?
questions.explanation: AWS Fargate runs containers serverlessly on ECS or EKS with no servers to manage. SQS (A) queues messages, Beanstalk (B) manages app platforms on servers, and SageMaker (D) trains ML models.

questions.question: A company is using multiple AWS accounts for different business teams. The finance team wants to receive one bill for all of the company's accounts. Which AWS service or tool should the finance team use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations with consolidated billing rolls all member-account charges into one payer-account bill. Trusted Advisor (B) checks best practices, Cost Explorer (C) visualizes spend, and Budgets (D) alerts on thresholds.

questions.question: A company needs a firewall that will control network connections to and from a single Amazon EC2 instance. This firewall will not control network connections to and from other instances that are in the same subnet. Which AWS service or feature can the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Security groups are stateful firewalls attached to a single instance without affecting others in the subnet. NACLs (A) filter whole subnets, WAF (B) filters web requests, and route tables (C) direct traffic.

questions.question: A company is planning to use the Amazon EC2 instances as web servers. Customers from around the world will use the web servers. Most customers will use the web servers only during certain hours of the day. How should the company deploy the EC2 instances to achieve the LOWEST operational cost?
questions.explanation: An Auto Scaling group adds instances for peak hours and removes them when idle, minimizing cost for time-varying global traffic. Multiple AZs alone (A) keep capacity always on, placement groups (C) optimize placement, and private subnets (D) control routing.

questions.question: Which benefit is always free of charge with AWS, regardless of a user’s AWS Support plan?
questions.explanation: Community support through AWS Developer Forums (now re:Post) is free for everyone regardless of support plan. Developer Support (A), programmatic case management (C), and TAMs (D) require paid plans.

questions.question: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances to run its application. The application needs to be available and running continuously for three or more years. What type of EC2 instance should the company purchase for a discount on the EC2 pricing?
questions.explanation: A continuous 3-plus-year workload earns the deepest discount from multi-year Reserved Instances. Spot (B) can be interrupted, On-Demand (C) has no discount, and EC2 Fleet (D) only launches capacity mixes.

questions.question: A company needs to perform an audit of recent AWS account activity. The audit will investigate who initiated an event and what actions were performed. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail records who initiated each API event and what actions ran, the audit trail for account activity. Config (A) tracks configuration history, Rekognition (B) analyzes images, and SNS (D) sends notifications.

questions.question: Which design principles are included in the reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
options: Grant everyone access to increase AWS service quotas.
Design applications to run in a single Availability Zone.
Plan to increase AWS service quotas first in a secondary AWS Region.
questions.explanation: Reliability principles include automatically recovering from failure (A) and stopping capacity guessing with elastic scaling (C). Open access (B) and single-AZ design (D) are anti-patterns, and quota planning (E) is operational rather than a reliability design principle.

questions.question: Which recommendation can AWS Cost Explorer provide to help reduce cost?
options: Change the programming language for an application.
questions.explanation: Cost Explorer analyzes usage and recommends terminating idle or underused instances to cut spend. It does not dictate database engines (A), programming languages (B), or operating systems (C).

questions.question: A company wants to deploy an application in multiple Availability Zones in a single AWS Region. Which benefit will this deployment provide to the company?
options: Improved connection performance for global customers
Resilient architecture and a highly available solution
Ability to shut down an Availability Zone during periods of low demand
questions.explanation: Deploying across multiple AZs isolates failures to one zone, giving resilience and high availability within the Region. Global performance (A) needs more Regions or CloudFront, storage costs (C) are unchanged, and AZs cannot be shut down on demand (D).

questions.question: Which AWS service can companies use to subscribe to RSS feeds for updates about all AWS service issues?
questions.explanation: The AWS Health Dashboard (Service Health view) publishes RSS feeds for service issues and events. SNS (A) sends custom notifications, Config (C) audits configuration, and CodeCommit (D) hosts Git repositories.

questions.question: Which Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances term commitment will give users the MOST cost savings?
questions.explanation: Reserved Instance discounts grow with term length, so a 3-year commitment (the longest offered) saves most. One year (A) discounts less, and 2-year (B) and 5-year (D) terms are not offered for Reserved Instances.

questions.question: A company is running big data analytics and massive parallel computations on its AWS test and development servers. The company can tolerate occasional downtime. What is the MOST cost-effective Amazon EC2 purchasing option for the company to use?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances offer the deepest discount for test and dev analytics that tolerate downtime and interruption. On-Demand (A) costs more, Reserved (C) needs steady commitment, and Savings Plans (D) need hourly commitments.

questions.question: A company runs Amazon EC2 instances in a research lab. The instances run for 3 hours each week and cannot be interrupted. What is the MOST cost-effective instance purchasing option to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: Three non-interruptible hours weekly fit On-Demand pay-per-use with no commitment waste. Savings Plans and Reserved Instances (A, C) need steady hourly use, and Spot (D) can be interrupted.

questions.question: A new AWS user needs to interact with AWS Support by using API calls. Which AWS Support plan will meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: Business Support is the cheapest plan with full Support API access for programmatic case management. Basic (A) has no Support API, Developer (B) offers limited business-hours access, and Enterprise (D) costs far more.

questions.question: A company migrated to the AWS Cloud. Now the company pays for services on an as-needed basis. Which advantage of cloud computing is the company benefiting from?
options: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
questions.explanation: Paying as-needed trades fixed capex for variable expense. Stopping data-center spend (A) is related but the as-needed phrasing defines variable expense, while speed (B) and global reach (C) are separate benefits.

questions.question: A company will run a predictable compute workload on Amazon EC2 instances for the next 3 years. The workload is critical for the company. The company wants to optimize costs to run the workload. Which solution will meet these requirements?
questions.explanation: A critical predictable 3-year workload fits Savings Plans with a 3-year hourly commitment and flexibility across instance families. Spot (A) risks interruption, Dedicated Hosts (B) add isolation cost, and On-Demand (D) has no discount.

questions.question: A company wants to estimate the cost for its AWS architecture solution before migration. Which AWS service or feature will meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: The Pricing Calculator models pre-migration architecture costs. Detective (A) investigates security, Budgets (B) alerts on spend, and Resource Explorer (C) searches resources.

questions.question: A company wants to centrally manage its employee's access to multiple AWS accounts. Which AWS service or feature should the company use to meet this requirement?
options: AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer
